summary: Comprehensive web survey + deep-read + cross-analysis of ISM-related methylation tools/papers vs our ISM method (chunked waves to avoid rate-limit)
logs: Phase 1: 10 tool categories, waves of 4 (rate-limit safe)
Phase 2: deep-read 8 critical tools, waves of 4

survey.category: External tool deep-survey: ONT modkit (modified-base toolkit) — #1 comparison target for ISM (InterSubMod)

tools.name: modkit (overall)
tools.type: ONT long-read modified-base CLI toolkit (Rust)
tools.method_core: Converts modBAM (MM/ML tags from ONT basecallers) to bedMethyl pileup via best-practice probability thresholding, plus manipulation/QC/stats subcommands. NOT a clustering/structure engine — a per-position aggregation + Bayesian-comparison toolkit.
tools.granularity: Primarily POSITION-level (pileup aggregates per genomic position); two subcommands are read-level (entropy, pileup-hemi).
tools.purpose: Standard ONT epigenetics workflow: modBAM -> bedmethyl -> DMR / entropy / QC. The de-facto ONT reference toolkit.
tools.input: modBAM with MM/ML tags + reference FASTA; downstream stats consume bgzip+tabix bedMethyl.
tools.statistics: Bayesian conjugate-prior likelihood ratio (DMR), MAP-based effect-size p-value, Cohen's h, 2-state HMM segmentation, Shannon methylation entropy.
tools.haplotype_aware: PARTIAL / upstream-only. pileup --phased reads HP tag -> hp1.bedmethyl / hp2.bedmethyl / combined.bedmethyl. NO --haplotype flag inside dmr/entropy; haplotype analysis = feed pre-partitioned hp1/hp2 bedMethyl as the two 'samples' to dmr pair. Haplotype is a data partition, never an internal model term.
tools.cancer_somatic: Germline-agnostic; used in cancer/aging epigenetics but NO somatic-vs-normal or tumor-normal-paired model, NO CN/ploidy/LOH coupling, NO somatic-controlled (HP1 vs HP1-1) axis.
tools.vs_ism: modkit aggregates calls PER POSITION then compares groups; ISM keeps read x CpG matrix and measures BETWEEN-MOLECULE structure (read-read distance + clustering + PERMANOVA). modkit asks 'is mean methylation different between two groups/haplotypes here'; ISM asks 'are reads structurally organized into subclonal/haplotype groups'. modkit lacks normal-anchored cis-test, LOH/CN coupling, read-clustering.
tools.key_claims: VERSION v0.6.3 (latest, GitHub README ~May 2026). Supports 5mC/5hmC/6mA/4mC. ONT long-read specific.
tools.citation: https://nanoporetech.github.io/modkit/ ; https://github.com/nanoporetech/modkit

tools.name: modkit pileup
tools.type: Position-level aggregation
tools.method_core: Aggregates per-read MM/ML calls to per-position counts (Nmod, Ncanonical, Nother, Nfiltered) after a pass-probability threshold (auto percentile or explicit). Produces bedMethyl.
tools.granularity: Position-level (collapses reads).
tools.purpose: Core modBAM -> bedMethyl conversion; foundation for dmr.
tools.input: modBAM + ref FASTA.
tools.statistics: Counts + percent-modified per position; threshold via sample-probs percentile (default ~10th).
tools.haplotype_aware: YES via --phased: partitions output by HP tag into hp1/hp2/combined. The ONLY place HP is consumed.
tools.cancer_somatic: Group-agnostic aggregation.
tools.vs_ism: ISM also reads MM/ML but BINARIZES (>0.8 meth / <0.2 unmeth) and keeps the full read x CpG matrix instead of collapsing to per-position counts — preserving molecule-level co-occurrence that pileup discards.
tools.key_claims: --phased emits hp1.bedmethyl/hp2.bedmethyl/combined.bedmethyl.
tools.citation: https://github.com/nanoporetech/modkit

tools.name: modkit pileup-hemi
tools.type: Read-level (single-molecule, double-stranded) hemimethylation
tools.method_core: At palindromic motifs (default CpG, --cpg = --motif CG 0) counts double-stranded methylation patterns on the SAME molecule: requires both + and - strand calls above pass threshold (duplex). Reports 4 patterns m,m / m,- / -,m / -,-.
tools.granularity: Read-level / single-molecule (both strands of one molecule), then aggregated per position.
tools.purpose: Detect hemimethylation (one strand methylated, complementary strand not) at CpG.
tools.input: Duplex modBAM + ref; --max-depth default 8000.
tools.statistics: Pattern-specific counts (Npattern, Ncanonical, Nother_pattern...) in ~18-col bedMethyl.
tools.haplotype_aware: No HP interaction documented.
tools.cancer_somatic: Germline-agnostic; requires duplex reads.
tools.vs_ism: Both molecule-level, but pileup-hemi measures strand-pair asymmetry (top vs bottom of ONE CpG); ISM measures read-to-read organization ACROSS many CpGs (subclonal/haplotype structure). Orthogonal axes.
tools.key_claims: Requires duplex/both-strand calls; ~18-col output.
tools.citation: https://nanoporetech.github.io/modkit/intro_pileup_hemi.html

tools.name: modkit dmr (pair / multi)
tools.type: Differential methylation scoring (Bayesian likelihood ratio)
tools.method_core: BAYESIAN conjugate-prior LIKELIHOOD RATIO on per-position counts (NOT a frequentist Fisher/chi-square LRT). Binary: X|p~Bin(n,p), p~Beta(a,b); multi-state (h/m/C): X|pi~Mult(n,pi), pi~Dir(alpha); Jeffreys prior. score = log[ l_a(Xa)*l_b(Xb) / l_{a+b}(X_{a+b}) ] of log marginal likelihoods (higher=more differential). Single-site adds MAP-based effect-size p-value: posterior Beta(a0+Nmod, b0+Ncan) per condition; p_MAP=f(0)/f(d), d=phat1-phat2, f=PDF of Z=X-Y (difference of two Betas). Region mode reports Cohen's h (avoids coverage-driven significance). Optional 2-state HMM ('Same'/'Different') segments DMRs: emission p_Same=e^-score, p_Diff=1-p_Same; distance-decaying transitions (default d=0.9, p=0.1, decay_distance=500bp) so nearby modified bases share state.
tools.granularity: POSITION-level (single-site, no --regions) OR REGION-level (--regions). NEVER read-level.
tools.vs_ism: CRITICAL DIFF. (1) dmr compares per-position COUNT proportions between two pre-defined groups via Bayesian LR + MAP effect-size; ISM Delta-beta does paired per-CpG MEAN difference + Wilcoxon signed-rank + Cohen d, AND tests STRUCTURE (PERMANOVA on read-read distance) which dmr cannot. (2) Haplotype: dmr NOT internally haplotype-aware (no --haplotype flag); HP DMRs need pileup --phased first then hp1 vs hp2 as two samples (treats haplotype as two static samples, loses molecule linkage). ISM HP-axis is somatic-controlled (HP1 vs HP1-1) with normal-anchored cis-test (d_somatic/d_cis/d_drift) holding CN/ploidy constant — modkit has no equivalent. (3) No LOH/CN coupling, no tumor-normal residualization, no read-clustering/subclone calling.
tools.haplotype_aware: NO internal --haplotype flag (verified across intro_dmr, advanced_usage, GitHub book src). Haplotype DMR = upstream pileup --phased -> hp1/hp2 bedMethyl -> dmr pair -a hp1 -b hp2. Haplotype = data partition, not a model term.
tools.cancer_somatic: Compares any two/multi bedMethyl groups (samples, replicates, haplotypes, tumor vs normal) but NO built-in somatic model, NO germline-het null, NO normal-baseline residual. Tumor-normal must be supplied manually as the two samples.
tools.statistics: Bayesian marginal-likelihood ratio score; MAP-based p-value (single-site); Cohen's h + 95% CI (region); 2-state HMM segmentation. dmr pair = 2 samples (single-site OR region); dmr multi = all-pairwise across >2 samples, REGIONS ONLY.
tools.purpose: Find differentially methylated CpGs/regions between two or more bedMethyl groups (incl. haplotype-partitioned).
tools.input: bgzip+tabix bedMethyl from pileup; --regions BED optional; --ref; --base C.
tools.key_claims: 5mC/5hmC/6mA/4mC supported. pair=single-site(LR+MAP) or region; multi=region-only all-pairwise. HMM defaults d=0.9 p=0.1 decay=500bp.
tools.citation: https://nanoporetech.github.io/modkit/dmr_scoring_details.html ; https://nanoporetech.github.io/modkit/intro_dmr.html

tools.name: modkit entropy
tools.type: Read-level methylation entropy (Shannon)
tools.method_core: YES — modkit HAS a methylation-entropy module. Shannon entropy of epiallele patterns across reads in a window: ME = -(1/N) sum_i Pr(n_i) log2 Pr(n_i), sum over distinct methylation patterns n_i on reads spanning the window, Pr(n_i)=empirical pattern frequency. Reads co-occurrence on INDIVIDUAL reads (input is modBAM, NOT pileup). Prefix-trie enumerates patterns; filtered/low-confidence positions become wildcards getting fractional counts. --num-positions default 4 (modified positions per pattern); --window-size = max bp span.
tools.granularity: Read-level co-occurrence (epialleles on single molecules), aggregated into genomic windows then optionally summarized over regions.
tools.purpose: Quantify epiallele randomness/information content; correlates with regulation, aging, CANCER.
tools.input: modBAM + ref; sliding windows or --regions.
tools.statistics: Shannon entropy (bits). Window output=bedGraph (chrom,start,end,entropy,num_reads); region output=mean/median/min/max entropy + read/window counts. NME/MSE normalized variants NOT documented on entropy page (UNVERIFIED whether normalized form emitted).
tools.haplotype_aware: No haplotype option documented for entropy.
tools.cancer_somatic: Group-agnostic; entropy noted to correlate with cancer but no somatic vs germline model.
tools.vs_ism: OVERLAP but ISM broader. modkit entropy = pattern-frequency Shannon entropy on n-position windows ('disorder'). ISM ALSO computes NME + epipolymorphism on 4-CpG windows ('disorder' family) but only as CONTRAST against its primary 'structure' engine (read-read distance + clustering + PERMANOVA), which modkit entropy lacks. modkit measures randomness; ISM core measures organized between-molecule structure. ISM num-CpG window ~ modkit --num-positions=4.
tools.key_claims: Read-level, modBAM input, default 4 positions/pattern, prefix-trie, wildcard fractional counts for filtered calls.
tools.citation: https://nanoporetech.github.io/modkit/intro_entropy.html

tools.name: modkit sample-probs
tools.type: QC / probability distribution estimation
tools.method_core: Samples modification-probability values from a modBAM, computes empirical percentiles/quantiles (default percentiles 10,50,90) + optional histogram. Used to choose the pileup pass threshold.
tools.granularity: Per-call probability distribution (no genomic structure).
tools.purpose: Pick filtering thresholds; QC ML-probability calibration.
tools.input: modBAM.
tools.statistics: Empirical percentiles/quantiles; histogram.
tools.haplotype_aware: No.
tools.cancer_somatic: Agnostic.
tools.vs_ism: ISM uses fixed binarization cutoffs (>0.8/<0.2) rather than sample-derived percentiles; conceptually the threshold-calibration step, no direct analog.
tools.key_claims: Default percentiles 10,50,90; --hist optional.
tools.citation: https://nanoporetech.github.io/modkit/advanced_usage.html

tools.name: modkit adjust-mods
tools.type: modBAM transformation
tools.method_core: Edits MM/ML tags: --ignore <code> removes a mod; --convert <from> <to> remaps codes (summing probabilities); --motif/--cpg keeps only motif-context calls; --filter-probs drops lowest-confidence calls.
tools.granularity: Per-call tag editing.
tools.purpose: Pre-process modBAM (e.g. collapse 5hmC into 5mC, restrict to CpG).
tools.input: modBAM -> modBAM.
tools.statistics: None (deterministic transform).
tools.haplotype_aware: No.
tools.cancer_somatic: Agnostic.
tools.vs_ism: ISM reads raw MM/ML directly (keeps 5mC AND 5hmC separately); no equivalent rewrite. ISM's known 5mC+5hmC collapse artifact maps to this subcommand's --convert behavior.
tools.key_claims: --convert sums probabilities of the two codes.
tools.citation: https://nanoporetech.github.io/modkit/advanced_usage.html

tools.name: modkit repair
tools.type: modBAM tag transfer
tools.method_core: Transfers MM/ML tags from a donor modBAM to an acceptor modBAM by matching reads on sequence identity (both sorted by name; donor must be superset; ambiguous matches rejected+logged). For when re-alignment/trimming stripped mod tags.
tools.granularity: Per-read tag projection.
tools.purpose: Recover mod calls onto a re-processed (re-aligned/clipped) BAM.
tools.input: donor modBAM + acceptor BAM -> output modBAM.
tools.statistics: None.
tools.haplotype_aware: No.
tools.cancer_somatic: Agnostic.
tools.vs_ism: No analog; pure data-plumbing utility.
tools.key_claims: Sequence-identity read matching; rejects ambiguous.
tools.citation: https://nanoporetech.github.io/modkit/advanced_usage.html

tools.name: modkit validate
tools.type: Accuracy benchmarking against ground truth
tools.method_core: Compares modBAM predictions to a ground-truth BED (known modified/canonical sites), applies a filter threshold (default filter-quantile 0.1 or explicit --filter-threshold), reports detection accuracy. -c/--canonical-base for canonical-only truth; --edge-filter excludes read ends.
tools.granularity: Per-call classification vs truth.
tools.purpose: QC basecaller mod-calling accuracy on controls.
tools.input: paired (modBAM, truth BED), repeatable.
tools.statistics: Accuracy / confusion metrics at chosen probability threshold.
tools.haplotype_aware: No.
tools.cancer_somatic: Agnostic (control samples).
tools.vs_ism: ISM has no basecaller-validation step; trusts MM/ML. Different scope.
tools.key_claims: Default filter-quantile 0.1.
tools.citation: https://nanoporetech.github.io/modkit/advanced_usage.html

tools.name: modkit motif (bed / search / refine)
tools.type: Motif analysis (Bayesian motif model)
tools.method_core: motif bed = list all genomic locations of a sequence motif. motif search = scan bedMethyl+ref for modification-ENRICHED sequence contexts via a Bayesian motif model with --low-thresh (0.2) / --high-thresh (0.6) and --context-size (12,12 default). motif refine = optimize/trim motif definitions by enrichment.
tools.granularity: Sequence-context (k-mer) level, aggregated over genome.
tools.purpose: De novo discovery of methylated sequence motifs (esp. bacterial 6mA/4mC; less central to human CpG cancer work).
tools.input: bedMethyl + ref FASTA.
tools.statistics: Bayesian enrichment scoring of contexts vs thresholds.
tools.haplotype_aware: No.
tools.cancer_somatic: Agnostic; oriented to motif/microbial methylation.
tools.vs_ism: No analog; ISM does not do sequence-motif discovery. Out of scope for somatic-CpG comparison.
tools.key_claims: low-thresh 0.2 / high-thresh 0.6 / context 12,12 defaults.
tools.citation: https://nanoporetech.github.io/modkit/advanced_usage.html

survey.notes:
VERSION: modkit v0.6.3 (latest, GitHub README ~May 2026) — VERIFIED.

=== ANSWERS TO THE THREE CRITICAL QUESTIONS ===

(1) HOW DOES modkit dmr DETECT DIFFERENTIAL METHYLATION? — VERIFIED from dmr_scoring_details.html. BAYESIAN conjugate-prior LIKELIHOOD RATIO on per-position counts, NOT a frequentist Fisher/G-test/chi-square LRT. Binary: X|p~Bin(n,p), p~Beta; multi-state (h/m/C): Mult/Dirichlet; Jeffreys prior. score = log[ l_a(Xa)*l_b(Xb) / l_{a+b}(X_{a+b}) ] of log marginal likelihoods. Single-site additionally gives a MAP-based EFFECT-SIZE p-value: posterior Beta(a0+Nmod, b0+Ncan) per condition; p_MAP=f(0)/f(d), d=phat1-phat2, f=PDF of Z=X-Y (difference of two Betas). Region mode reports Cohen's h (+95% CI) to avoid coverage-driven significance. Optional 2-state HMM ('Same'/'Different') segments DMRs with distance-decaying transitions (default d=0.9, p=0.1, decay_distance=500bp; emission p_Same=e^-score). The user's hypothesis 'likelihood-ratio on per-position counts' is CORRECT in spirit, with the nuance it is a BAYESIAN marginal-likelihood ratio + a separate MAP effect-size p-value, not a classical chi-square LRT.

(2) IS dmr HAPLOTYPE-AWARE (--haplotype / partition by HP)? — VERIFIED: NO internal --haplotype flag in modkit dmr (confirmed across intro_dmr.html, advanced_usage.html, and the GitHub book master source). Haplotype DMRs are produced by running `modkit pileup --phased` FIRST (the ONLY place the HP tag is read — splits output into hp1.bedmethyl / hp2.bedmethyl / combined.bedmethyl), THEN feeding hp1 vs hp2 as the two 'samples' to `modkit dmr pair -a hp1 -b hp2`. Haplotype is an UPSTREAM DATA PARTITION, never a model term. Key differentiator vs ISM, whose HP-axis is somatic-controlled (HP1 vs HP1-1) with a normal-anchored cis-test holding CN/ploidy/alignment constant — modkit has no somatic/cis machinery.

(3) DOES IT HAVE A METHYLATION-ENTROPY MODULE? — VERIFIED YES: `modkit entropy`. Read-level Shannon entropy of epiallele patterns: ME = -(1/N) sum Pr(n_i) log2 Pr(n_i) over distinct patterns on reads in a window; input is modBAM (not pileup); --num-positions default 4, --window-size = max bp span; prefix-trie pattern enumeration; filtered calls -> wildcard fractional counts. Outputs window bedGraph + optional region summary. NME/MSE normalized variants NOT documented on the entropy page — UNVERIFIED whether a normalized form is emitted.

=== DOMAIN FRAMING (per task rules) ===
modkit is LONG-READ ONT specific (MM/ML tags from ONT basecallers), supports 5mC/5hmC/6mA/4mC. GERMLINE-AGNOSTIC / general-purpose: no somatic-vs-normal model, no tumor-normal-paired residualization, no germline-het null, no LOH/CN coupling, no read-clustering/subclone calling. POSITION-level for flagship dmr; only entropy and pileup-hemi are read-level.

=== modkit vs ISM — ONE-LINE CONTRAST ===
modkit collapses reads to per-position counts then runs Bayesian group comparison (dmr) or per-window pattern entropy (entropy) — a 'disorder + mean-difference' toolkit. ISM keeps the read x CpG matrix and measures BETWEEN-MOLECULE STRUCTURE (read-read distance -> hierarchical clustering -> PERMANOVA pseudo-F) = 'structure not disorder', PLUS a somatic-controlled HP-axis + normal-anchored cis-test coupling ASM to LOH/CN. Overlap is only in the 'disorder family': modkit entropy ~ ISM's NME/epipolymorphism contrast metrics (both ~4-position windows). modkit dmr's per-CpG comparison overlaps ISM's Delta-beta (Wilcoxon) but ISM adds Fisher+BH-FDR and, crucially, the structural PERMANOVA engine and somatic/cis design modkit lacks. Paper positioning: modkit = strongest baseline for 'mean methylation difference between haplotypes/samples' and 'epiallele entropy', but provides NO read-clustering structure test, NO somatic-controlled HP1-vs-HP1-1 axis, and NO LOH/CN-coupled cis-test — exactly ISM's differentiated contribution.

=== PRIMARY SOURCES (all WebFetched & verified) ===
- GitHub README (v0.6.3, subcommand list, --phased): https://github.com/nanoporetech/modkit
- DMR model/stats (Bayesian LR, MAP p, HMM, Cohen's h): https://nanoporetech.github.io/modkit/dmr_scoring_details.html
- DMR intro (pair/multi, single-site vs region, haplotype-partitioned workflow): https://nanoporetech.github.io/modkit/intro_dmr.html + book master src
- Entropy (ME formula, num-positions=4, read-level): https://nanoporetech.github.io/modkit/intro_entropy.html
- pileup-hemi (duplex hemimethylation, 4 patterns, read-level): https://nanoporetech.github.io/modkit/intro_pileup_hemi.html
- advanced_usage (sample-probs, adjust-mods, repair, validate, motif help): https://nanoporetech.github.io/modkit/advanced_usage.html

UNVERIFIED: (a) whether modkit entropy emits a NORMALIZED entropy (NME) or methylation-specific entropy (MSE) variant — not stated on the fetched entropy page. (b) Exact dmr multi statistical method string / --method default — advanced_usage summary partial. (c) Peer-reviewed modkit journal DOI/PMID not separately confirmed in this pass (a preprint/Bioinformatics publication is referenced via nanoporetech.com resource page but not fetched) — citations point to official docs/GitHub, not a journal DOI.

survey.category: Long-read modBAM methylation extraction / DMR / visualization toolkits (non-modkit) — surveyed for ONT cancer-somatic context, compared against ISM (InterSubMod)

tools.name: modbam2bed
tools.type: Extraction / aggregation tool (modBAM -> bedMethyl). Site-level. NOT DMR, NOT visualization, NOT read-level.
tools.method_core: htslib pileup API over MM/ML tags. Per-strand base-count matrix; each base classed canonical / modified / filtered(ambiguous) / no-call. Modification frequency = modified / (canonical + modified); low-confidence calls below the probability threshold are dropped (filtered) but substitutions+deletions count toward coverage. No model, no statistical test — pure deterministic counting.
tools.purpose: Summarise one or more modBAMs into a single bedMethyl file of per-CpG-site modification percentages for downstream tools.
tools.granularity: Site/region-level aggregate ONLY (per reference position across reads). Does NOT emit per-read methylation; no single-molecule output.
tools.haplotype_aware: YES, by pre-filtering (one hap per run, not one-pass split). Flags: --haplotype=VAL (process reads of one HP value); generic --tag_name=TN / --tag_value=VAL to filter by any tag (e.g. HP). Reads must be pre-phased (HP added upstream by whatshap/longphase).
tools.input: Aligned modBAM with Mm/Ml (or MM/ML) tags + reference FASTA used for alignment. ONT (Guppy/Dorado) or any GA4GH-compliant modBAM.
tools.statistics: None inferential. Deterministic count-based methylation %. -f/--threshold default 0.66 (below = filtered/ambiguous); older -a canon_threshold / -b mod_threshold deprecated for unified --threshold. -m/--mod_base selects 5mC/5hmC/6mA; -e/--extended adds count columns (canonical, modified, filtered, no-call, alt-mod).
tools.vs_ism: Complementary, not competing. modbam2bed = the EXTRACTION/AGGREGATION primitive that ISM's MethylationMatrix replaces at READ level. modbam2bed collapses reads to a per-site % (loses between-molecule structure); ISM keeps the full read x CpG matrix + read-to-READ distance + PERMANOVA. No clustering, no distance metric, no haplotype STRUCTURE test, no normal-baseline residual, no Delta-beta. Its HP handling is one-hap-at-a-time filtering vs ISM's somatic-controlled HP-axis (HP1 vs HP1-1) paired by CpG. Use only to produce a baseline aggregate %; cannot detect the structure-not-disorder signal ISM targets.
tools.cancer_somatic: Tool-agnostic, long-read ONT-oriented. No germline/cancer-specific logic. Repo is unsupported (ONT directs to support@nanoporetech.com).
tools.key_claims: Verified: bedMethyl aggregation, htslib pileup, --haplotype + --tag_name/--tag_value filtering, --threshold default 0.66, -m/-e flags, site-level only.
tools.citation: GitHub epi2me-labs/modbam2bed README (raw master). No peer-reviewed paper; ONT EPI2ME-Labs tool.

tools.name: modbamtools
tools.type: Read-level visualization + lightweight per-region stats + read clustering. NOT a DMR engine.
tools.method_core: Parses MM/ML (pysam/htslib) into per-read modification state. Subcommands: plot (single-read base-modification browser-style figures), calcMeth (per-region aggregate methylation %), cluster (groups reads by modification state).
tools.purpose: Manipulate and produce publication-ready interactive single-molecule modification visualizations + simple region stats + read clustering for heterogeneity/long-range profiling.
tools.granularity: Read-level for plot and cluster (single-molecule); region-level aggregate for calcMeth.
tools.haplotype_aware: YES via --hap (separate reads by HP tag). plot supports --hap + --strands; calcMeth --hap emits per-haplotype stats (9 cols = 3/hap vs 3). cluster: NO --hap documented.
tools.input: modBAM with MM/ML tags; optional GTF/BED/BigWig/Bedgraph tracks for plot; BED region file for calcMeth/cluster.
tools.statistics: cluster = HDBSCAN (hierarchical density-based spatial clustering; scikit-learn-contrib/hdbscan) on reads 'based on modification state' -> outputs n_clusters + n_reads passing QC appended to BED. (UNVERIFIED: docs do NOT state the feature matrix is read x CpG nor the distance metric.) calcMeth = average percent modification + std + coverage over reads spanning >=80% of region (default), >=5 mod calls. NO p-value / DMR test.
tools.vs_ism: Closest conceptual neighbour to ISM's clustering core but weaker for ISM's question. modbamtools cluster = HDBSCAN returning a cluster COUNT; ISM = explicit read-to-read DISTANCE matrix (NHD/L1/Bernoulli/Pearson/Jaccard, min 5 common CpG) -> UPGMA/Ward -> silhouette k=2..10 -> PERMANOVA (pseudo-F, 999 perms) + dispersion test that statistically asks whether HP/somatic groups are STRUCTURALLY separated. No PERMANOVA, no separation significance, no Cramer-V gate, no NormalBaseline residual / cis-test, no Delta-beta Wilcoxon. Right tool to VISUALIZE ISM reads + a quick cluster count; cannot adjudicate structure-vs-disorder or somatic-vs-drift.
tools.cancer_somatic: Long-read, technology-agnostic (ONT + PacBio modBAM). Heterogeneity framing generic, not cancer-somatic specific; no tumor-normal model.
tools.key_claims: Verified: HDBSCAN for cluster (tutorial); calcMeth 80%/5-call defaults + avg%/std/cov; --hap for plot & calcMeth; plot = single-read. UNVERIFIED: exact cluster feature matrix/distance; journal status (remains bioRxiv preprint).
tools.citation: Razaghi R, Hook PW, Ou S, Schatz MC, Hansen KD, Jain M, Timp W. Modbamtools. bioRxiv 2022.07.07.499188 (2022). DOI 10.1101/2022.07.07.499188. PREPRINT (not journal-published per search).

tools.name: methylartist
tools.type: Visualization suite (read-level + aggregate); produces DSS-ready input but delegates DMR. NOT a native statistics engine.
tools.method_core: Python suite consuming modBAM MM/ML or tabular per-read calls (megalodon/nanopolish/guppy: read name, base position, mod probability). Locus plots (single aligned reads), segment-based + composite repeat-element aggregate plots, plus bedMethyl and DSS-input files.
tools.purpose: Process, visualize and analyse nanopore-derived modified-base calls across all detectable types (5mCpG, 5hmC, 6mA), incl. non-CpG motifs for chromatin footprinting.
tools.granularity: Both: read-level single-molecule locus plots AND aggregate (segment/composite) plots.
tools.haplotype_aware: YES. Locus plots separate methylation by phase if BAMs are first phased (PS + HP tags via WhatsHap or other). Splitting is by pre-added HP/PS tags.
tools.input: modBAM with SAM-spec base-mod tags; OR tabular per-read calls from megalodon/nanopolish/guppy/custom.
tools.statistics: NO native DMR test. Emits files 'suitable for input to DSS' (Park & Wu) for differential methylation; statistics delegated to DSS externally. Visualization-primary.
tools.vs_ism: Pure visualization overlap; near-zero analytic overlap. Best off-the-shelf way to render ISM's per-region read x CpG data as a phased single-molecule locus plot (which ISM itself does not do). NO distance matrix, NO PERMANOVA, NO clustering with significance, NO somatic/normal-baseline residual; only differential capability = export to DSS (smoothing + Wald-test DMR, germline-style, site/region group comparison). Cannot test haplotype-linked between-molecule STRUCTURE. Use downstream of ISM for figures only.
tools.cancer_somatic: Long-read nanopore-specific. No cancer/germline restriction in method; tested partly on MCF-7 (breast cancer cell line) but framed as generally applicable. No tumor-normal somatic model.
tools.key_claims: Verified from peer-reviewed paper: visualization-primary, DSS delegation, HP/PS phase splitting via WhatsHap, read+aggregate, nanopore.
tools.citation: Cheetham SW, Kindlova M, Ewing AD. Methylartist: tools for visualizing modified bases from nanopore sequence data. Bioinformatics 2022;38(11):3109-3112. DOI 10.1093/bioinformatics/btac292. PMID 35482479.

tools.name: NanoMethViz
tools.type: R/Bioconductor visualization package; format converter + plots. Explicitly visualization-only, delegates DMR.
tools.method_core: Converts caller output (nanopolish, f5c, megalodon) into a compact intermediate (sample, 1-based chrom position, methylation log-likelihood-ratio, read name; bgzip+tabix). Produces spaghetti (per-read) plots with smoothed methylation probability + aggregate feature-level plots with binned means.
tools.purpose: Visualize long-read methylation and bridge callers to the Bioconductor DMR ecosystem (GenomicRanges-compatible).
tools.granularity: Both: read-level spaghetti plots AND aggregate/feature-level smoothed/binned plots.
tools.haplotype_aware: PARTIAL / UNVERIFIED as native. Paper demonstrates haplotyped data (maternal vs paternal X via WhatsHap) and renders haplotype-separated results, but does NOT explicitly confirm NanoMethViz itself performs the split vs consuming pre-phased input. Treat as: compatible with pre-phased data; native HP-split UNVERIFIED.
tools.input: Tabular caller output (nanopolish/f5c/megalodon); modBAM support exists in later versions but the paper emphasizes tabular log-lik-ratio inputs.
tools.statistics: NONE native. 'Not a complete pipeline; modular component.' Delegates DMR to bsseq, DSS and edgeR (DSS = beta-binomial smoothing + Wald test; edgeR = NB GLM; paper does not detail). Plots let you eyeball externally-called DM regions.
tools.vs_ism: Visualization-and-handoff overlap only. R-side counterpart to methylartist: good for spaghetti/aggregate figures and piping to bsseq/DSS/edgeR (site/region group-level DMR, count-based NB/beta-binomial, germline-oriented). NO read-to-read distance, NO PERMANOVA structure test, NO somatic normal-baseline residual or copy-partition. Overlaps ISM only on 'render the reads' + 'aggregate %'; the structure-not-disorder + somatic-cis machinery of ISM has no analogue.
tools.cancer_somatic: Long-read nanopore-specific. Demonstrated on germline (mouse placental imprinting); NO cancer/somatic example or tumor-normal model. Downstream DSS/edgeR = general group comparison.
tools.key_claims: Verified from peer-reviewed paper: visualization-only, modular, converts nanopolish/f5c/megalodon, delegates to bsseq/DSS/edgeR, spaghetti+aggregate, germline imprinting demo. UNVERIFIED: native haplotype splitting; PMID not surfaced in fetch.
tools.citation: Su S, Gouil Q, Blewitt ME, Cook D, Hickey PF, Ritchie ME. NanoMethViz: An R/Bioconductor package for visualizing long-read methylation data. PLOS Comput Biol 2021;17(11):e1009524. DOI 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009524 (PMC8568149).

tools.name: pb-CpG-tools (aligned_bam_to_cpg_scores)
tools.type: Extraction / per-site scoring tool. Site-level. NOT DMR, NOT visualization, NOT read-level.
tools.method_core: Reads C+m (5mC) from MM/ML tags of aligned HiFi BAM/CRAM. Two pileup modes: 'model' (default/recommended) uses distributions of modification scores + a built-in ML model to compute per-CpG-site modification probability; 'count' classifies a base as modified if mod-prob > 0.5 and reports site methylation = fraction modified, plus base counts + average scores.
tools.purpose: Summarise CpG/5mC methylation per site from PacBio HiFi reads into bed + bigwig tracks (whole-read-set and per-haplotype).
tools.granularity: Site-level (per CpG). No per-read output.
tools.haplotype_aware: YES, automatic split. When HP tags present (default tag HP, configurable via --hap-tag), outputs separate [prefix].hap1.* and [prefix].hap2.* bed.gz + bigwig alongside combined. Reads must be phased upstream.
tools.input: Aligned HiFi BAM/CRAM with MM/ML C+m tags (other mod keys e.g. A+a ignored). Mapped with pbmm2 or minimap2 -Y.
tools.statistics: 'model' mode = built-in ML model over score distributions giving per-site probability (architecture/training NOT documented = internals UNVERIFIED). 'count' mode = deterministic 0.5-threshold proportion. Outputs per-site % + coverage + estimated mod/unmod counts. NO differential test, NO DMR.
tools.vs_ism: Cross-PLATFORM (PacBio HiFi, NOT ONT) and 5mC-ONLY -> only weakly comparable to ISM. An extraction/scoring analogue of modbam2bed for PacBio: site-level % + automatic hap1/hap2 tracks. NO 5hmC (ISM uses 5mC AND 5hmC), no read-level matrix, no distance/PERMANOVA/clustering, no somatic normal-baseline. For ISM's ONT cancer-somatic context, mainly a reference for how PacBio's stack natively splits haplotypes (cleaner hap1/hap2 emission than modbam2bed), not a usable engine on ONT data.
tools.cancer_somatic: PacBio HiFi platform (NOT ONT). 5mC only. Tool-agnostic to germline/cancer; no tumor-normal somatic logic.
tools.key_claims: Verified from README: model vs count mode, 0.5 threshold in count mode, HP auto-split hap1/hap2 bed+bigwig, --hap-tag, C+m only, PacBio HiFi, site-level, no DMR. UNVERIFIED: model architecture/training internals.
tools.citation: GitHub PacificBiosciences/pb-CpG-tools README (main). No standalone peer-reviewed paper for the tool itself.

tools.name: ONT EPI2ME wf-human-variation (methylation module = modkit)
tools.type: Nextflow workflow wrapper; methylation step is modkit (extraction -> bedMethyl, optional haplotype split, optional DMR via modkit dmr). NOT a novel method — orchestrates modkit.
tools.method_core: Workflow calls modkit for modified-base aggregation. Default: modkit pileup --cpg --combine-strands (strand-collapsed CpG bedMethyl). --force_strand reverts to per-strand. --phased partitions phased reads into hp1.bedmethyl / hp2.bedmethyl / combined.bedmethyl (= modkit --partition-tag HP). DMR is a separate downstream step: modkit dmr pair on bgzip+tabix bedMethyl.
tools.purpose: End-to-end human variant workflow (Clair3 SNV + Sniffles2 SV + Straglr STR + whatshap/longphase phasing + modkit methylation); methylation arm produces (optionally haplotype-resolved) bedMethyl and supports DMR scoring.
tools.granularity: Site/region-level aggregate bedMethyl. modkit dmr discards within-region ordering (each potentially-methylated base modeled from one distribution) -> region-level, NOT read-level.
tools.haplotype_aware: YES. --phased -> hp1/hp2/combined bedMethyl (modkit --partition-tag HP under the hood; reads phased by whatshap/longphase within workflow). modkit supports multiple --partition-tag combos (e.g. RG x HP).
tools.input: modBAM (Dorado MM/ML) + reference. Recommended >=30x coverage (20x absolute minimum).
tools.statistics: modkit dmr pair: log MARGINAL LIKELIHOOD RATIO comparing two conditions modeled separately vs jointly = log(L_a * L_b / L_{a+b}); conjugate priors with Jeffrey's prior — Beta-Binomial (binary meth/unmod) or Dirichlet-Multinomial (multi-state e.g. 5hmC/5mC/C). Region score has NO direct p-value; a separate MAP-based p-value (Bernoulli posterior, effect-size) exists ONLY for single-site analysis (omit --regions). pileup % is deterministic count-based.
tools.vs_ism: The production reference pipeline ISM sits beside; contrast is sharpest here. wf-human-variation/modkit = extraction + haplotype-split bedMethyl + region DMR via a Dirichlet-Multinomial/Beta-Binomial marginal-likelihood-ratio that EXPLICITLY DISCARDS within-region read ordering — i.e. aggregate per-site frequency differences (a 'disorder/frequency' family), the opposite of ISM CORE 1-3 which preserve read identity + test BETWEEN-molecule STRUCTURE (read-to-read distance + PERMANOVA). modkit dmr pair = tumor-vs-normal at SITE/REGION level (closest to ISM CORE 4 Fisher/Delta-beta contrast, but aggregate + ordering-blind) with no read-level subclonal clustering, no silhouette k, no dispersion test, no NormalBaseline cis-test, no copy-partition of d_HP. modkit --partition-tag HP gives hap1/hap2 frequencies; ISM HP-axis (HP1 vs HP1-1) is somatic-controlled, paired by CpG, Wilcoxon signed-rank. Bottom line: modkit/wf-human-variation = standard aggregate + region-DMR engine; ISM adds the read-level structure + somatic-cis layer modkit deliberately omits.
tools.cancer_somatic: Long-read ONT (Dorado). Human germline-oriented workflow; modkit dmr pair is framed for tumor-vs-normal but uses a general two-condition likelihood ratio, NOT a somatic-specific/normal-baseline-residual model, and no within-tumor subclonal read clustering.
tools.key_claims: Verified: --cpg --combine-strands default, --force_strand, --phased hp1/hp2/combined, modkit --partition-tag HP, modkit dmr pair log-marginal-likelihood-ratio with Jeffrey's prior Beta-Binomial/Dirichlet-Multinomial, region score no direct p-value, MAP p-value single-site only, region-level discards ordering, >=20x/30x coverage.
tools.citation: EPI2ME wf-human-variation docs (epi2me.nanoporetech.com); modkit DMR scoring docs (nanoporetech.github.io/modkit/dmr_scoring_details.html); modkit pileup --partition-tag (gensoft.pasteur.fr/docs/modkit intro_bedmethyl). No single peer-reviewed paper; ONT software.

survey.notes:
METHODOLOGY: WebSearch -> WebFetch on primary sources only (GitHub READMEs, official docs sites, peer-reviewed papers, bioRxiv). Every algorithm/statistic was confirmed from a fetched primary source; URLs/DOIs/PMIDs attached per tool.

ROLE TAXONOMY (extraction / DMR / visualization axis), all long-read unless noted:
- EXTRACTION/AGGREGATION (modBAM -> per-site bedMethyl, NO inferential stats): modbam2bed (ONT), pb-CpG-tools (PacBio HiFi, 5mC only). modkit (engine inside wf-human-variation) is fundamentally this plus an optional region-DMR.
- VISUALIZATION-PRIMARY (delegate DMR): methylartist (Python -> DSS), NanoMethViz (R/Bioc -> bsseq/DSS/edgeR), modbamtools plot (interactive HTML single-read).
- DMR / STATISTICAL TEST natively: among this set ONLY modkit dmr (via wf-human-variation) — log marginal likelihood ratio, Beta-Binomial/Dirichlet-Multinomial + Jeffrey's prior, region-level, ordering discarded, no direct p-value (MAP p-value single-site only). methylartist/NanoMethViz do NOT test; hand off to DSS/edgeR. modbamtools 'cluster' = HDBSCAN read grouping (cluster count, no significance) — heterogeneity, not DMR.

HAPLOTYPE-SPLIT (all require pre-phased reads via whatshap/longphase; HP/PS tags):
- Native auto hap1/hap2 emission: pb-CpG-tools (HP, --hap-tag), wf-human-variation/modkit (--phased -> hp1/hp2/combined; or --partition-tag HP).
- Per-haplotype via flag: modbamtools (--hap for plot & calcMeth; cluster has NO --hap), modbam2bed (--haplotype=VAL or --tag_name/--tag_value, one hap per run).
- Compatible-with-phased plotting: methylartist (phase-separated locus plots), NanoMethViz (demonstrated, NATIVE splitting UNVERIFIED).

PLATFORM/DOMAIN CAVEATS for ISM's ONT cancer-somatic context:
- pb-CpG-tools = PacBio HiFi, 5mC-ONLY -> NOT directly usable on ONT 5mC+5hmC data; include only as cross-platform reference for clean native hap split.
- methylartist (MCF-7) and modbamtools touch cancer cell lines but have NO tumor-normal somatic model. NanoMethViz demo = germline imprinting. wf-human-variation/modkit dmr framed for tumor-vs-normal but uses a generic two-condition likelihood ratio, not a somatic/normal-baseline-residual model, no within-tumor subclonal read clustering.

ISM DIFFERENTIATION (what NONE of these six do): read-to-READ distance matrix (NHD/L1/Bernoulli/Pearson/Jaccard, min 5 common CpG) + hierarchical clustering with silhouette k-selection + PERMANOVA (pseudo-F, 999 perms) + dispersion test = the structure-not-disorder between-molecule engine; PLUS NormalBaseline residual + normal-anchored cis-test (d_somatic/d_cis/d_drift holding CN/ploidy/alignment constant) + copy-partition of d_HP. The six cover ISM's EXTRACTION layer (modbam2bed/pb-CpG-tools), VISUALIZATION layer (methylartist/NanoMethViz/modbamtools plot), and per-site frequency/Delta-beta CONTRAST layer (modkit dmr ~ ISM CORE 4 Fisher/Delta-beta, but aggregate + ordering-blind). The read-level structure (CORE 1-3) and somatic-cis (CORE 6) layers have NO analogue in any of the six.

UNVERIFIED / CAVEATS explicitly flagged: (a) modbamtools 'cluster' exact feature matrix (read x CpG?) + distance metric — docs do not state; (b) modbamtools remains a bioRxiv preprint (DOI 10.1101/2022.07.07.499188), not journal-published per search; (c) NanoMethViz native (vs pre-phased) haplotype splitting unconfirmed by paper, PMID not surfaced; (d) pb-CpG-tools 'model' mode ML architecture/training data undocumented. biorxiv modbamtools v1 page returned HTTP 403; details taken from official docs site + HPC mirror + Semantic Scholar metadata instead. ISM build-derived facts were treated as given context, not independently re-verified here.

survey.category: long-read READ-LEVEL methylation clustering & disorder tools (vs ISM)
survey.notes: All three verified from primary full-text sources (PMC / Oxford Academic / PLOS). KEY FINDINGS FOR ISM POSITIONING: (1) NONE of the three builds a read-to-read pairwise DISTANCE MATRIX with hierarchical clustering + PERMANOVA the way ISM does — cvlr is the only clustering tool and it is MODEL-BASED (EM mixture, no distance matrix); pycoMeth and Metheor do no read clustering at all. (2) NONE does normal-anchored somatic cis-test / NormalBaseline residual / LOH-CN coupling — ISM's CORE 6 + copy-partition decomposition is unique among these. (3) Metheor is the closest on the "disorder" family (ME entropy, PM epipolymorphism, LPMD within-read discordance) which overlaps ISM CORE 4, BUT Metheor is BISULFITE SHORT-READ only and does NO between-molecule structure test — confirming ISM's "structure not disorder" engine (PERMANOVA on the distance matrix) has no equivalent here. (4) cvlr's EM mixture finds subpopulations of molecules (read-level cluster assignment) which is the conceptual cousin of ISM's silhouette-selected subclonal read groups, but cvlr uses posterior membership (no distance metric, no UPGMA/Ward, no PERMANOVA significance). (5) HAPLOTYPE: pycoMeth is the only genuinely haplotype-aware one (MetH5 read-groups from WhatsHap haplotagging, consensus segmentation per read-group); cvlr is explicitly phasing-FREE (validates against HP post-hoc via Fisher); Metheor only has MHL (methylation haplotype load = consecutive-CpG conservation, not phasing). CONTEXT GAP: all three are germline/cell-line — pycoMeth=GIAB trio (germline), cvlr=NA12878 imprinting (germline), Metheor=CCLE cancer cell lines but bisulfite & no somatic tumor-normal design. ISM's tumor-normal-paired somatic ONT (5mC AND 5hmC) niche is unoccupied by all three. UNVERIFIED: the standalone GitHub repo github.com/EmanueleRaineri/cvlr now returns HTTP 404 (repo moved/renamed since 2023 publication; author's methyl_diff repo is live) — cite the DOI as the authoritative source. pycoMeth official docs site (pmbio.github.io/pycoMeth) returned 403/limited but the Genome Biology PMC full text was fully readable.

tools.name: pycoMeth (Meth_Seg + Meth_Comp + Comp_Report)
tools.type: long-read ONT (Nanopore), germline; region-level differential methylation + haplotype-aware consensus segmentation; downstream of Nanopolish/MetH5
tools.method_core: Meth_Seg = Bayesian changepoint / methylome segmentation modeled as an HMM solved by Baum-Welch (EM) with forward-backward posteriors; emission models methylation-call uncertainty via Nanopolish LLRs (sigmoid->prob); parameterizes methylation rate mu(s,g) per segment s x read-group g to produce ONE consensus segmentation across multiple read-groups. Meth_Comp = per-interval differential methylation across samples/read-groups with three test modes.
tools.granularity: Region/interval-level OUTPUT (DMRs/DMIs as BED/TSV). Read-level info is used INTERNALLY (per-read LLRs feed segmentation + binarized beta per read) but NOT emitted per-read. No read clustering, no read-to-read distance matrix.
tools.vs_ism: Closest on HAPLOTYPE-AWARENESS (genuine: MetH5 read-groups = WhatsHap haplotags -> consensus segmentation treats each haplotype as a read-group). BUT: pycoMeth does NOT build a read-to-read distance matrix and does NOT cluster reads (ISM CORE 1-3 absent). Its DM test is rank/contingency per-interval (vs ISM PERMANOVA structural test on a distance matrix). No somatic/normal-anchored cis-test (ISM CORE 6 absent). Germline GIAB trio context, not cancer somatic. Output is region-level DMR, whereas ISM is read-level structure + per-CpG contrast. Overlaps ISM only at the 'compare HP groups per region' layer, via different statistics.
tools.haplotype_aware: YES - explicit. Haplotype assignment per read stored as MetH5 read-groups (from WhatsHap haplotagging of input BAM); segmentation produces consensus across read-groups incl. haplotypes.
tools.cancer_somatic: Germline. Benchmarked on Genome-in-a-Bottle father-mother-son trio. No tumor-normal somatic design; no LOH/CN coupling.
tools.statistics: Meth_Comp three modes: (a) llr_diff = ranked test on mean per-read LLR differences; (b) bs_diff = two-sided Mann-Whitney-U (2 samples) / Kruskal-Wallis (n>2) on binarized methylation rates; (c) count_dependency = Fisher exact (2 samples) / chi-square (>2). Multiple testing = Benjamini-Hochberg FDR, optional Independent Hypothesis Weighting (IHW) weighting by scaled SD of methylation rates. LLR binarization threshold default |LLR|>=2.0.
tools.input: Nanopolish methylation call LLRs ingested into MetH5 (read-level reference-anchored HDF5 store); haplotagged BAM read-groups via WhatsHap.
tools.purpose: Multi-sample / multi-read-group consensus methylome segmentation + differential methylation interval testing for ONT data.
tools.key_claims: Novel MetH5 rapid read-level storage; haplotype-aware multi-sample consensus segmentation; interval-level DM testing with BH/IHW correction. Region-level deliverable.
tools.citation: Snajder R, et al. pycoMeth: a toolbox for differential methylation testing from Nanopore methylation calls. Genome Biology 2023;24:83. DOI 10.1186/s13059-023-02917-w. PMC10120131.

tools.name: cvlr (cluster variant long reads)
tools.type: long-read ONT (Nanopore), germline; read-level model-based clustering to find heterogeneously methylated regions / subpopulations of molecules
tools.method_core: Model-based clustering: fits a MIXTURE OF MULTIVARIATE BERNOULLI distributions over reads via an Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithm that tolerates incomplete (missing) CpG observations. Input is a binary read x position matrix X (Xij in {0 unmeth, 1 meth, -1 unknown}); user sets k (e.g. k=2). EM yields posterior cluster-membership probabilities per read. Cluster methylation covariance computed as sum_l pi_l{Sigma_l + mu_l mu_l^T} - E[x]E[x]^T with Sigma_l = diag(mu_l(1-mu_l)).
tools.granularity: Dual: READ-LEVEL cluster assignment (posterior membership per read) + REGION-LEVEL scan (5 kb windows, e.g. chr15) flagging heterogeneity. Operates per genomic window.
tools.vs_ism: The ONLY one of the three that does per-READ clustering into subpopulations -> conceptual cousin of ISM CORE 2 (subclonal read groups). BUT cvlr is MODEL-BASED (EM Bernoulli mixture, posterior membership) and explicitly does NOT compute a read-to-read pairwise distance matrix -> fundamentally different mechanism from ISM CORE 1 (NHD/L1/Bernoulli/Jaccard distance) + CORE 3 (UPGMA/Ward hierarchical + silhouette + PERMANOVA significance). cvlr's significance = empirical null (1000 random cluster assignments) + Fisher test for HP enrichment, vs ISM's pseudo-F PERMANOVA (999 perms) + dispersion test on the distance matrix. cvlr is phasing-FREE; ISM consumes HP tags. cvlr is germline imprinting (NA12878); no somatic, no normal-anchored cis-test, no LOH/CN coupling. cvlr handles 5mC CpG only; ISM uses 5mC AND 5hmC.
tools.haplotype_aware: NO (by design). Clustering does NOT use phase/HP and explicitly 'does not rely on a previous phasing step.' Haplotype used only POST-HOC for validation (WhatsHap haplotag + Fisher exact for cluster-vs-HP enrichment).
tools.cancer_somatic: Germline. Demonstrated on NA12878 lymphoblastoid line, known imprinted genes (GNAS, H19, SNRPN, PEG10, MEG3, IGF2, PLAGL1) on chr15. Detects allele-specific methylation + cell-subpopulation heterogeneity; no tumor-normal somatic design.
tools.statistics: EM for Bernoulli mixture (posterior responsibilities). Heterogeneity statistic = median absolute methylation difference between clusters across positions; threshold at 95th percentile (~0.53 for chr15 scan). Significance via empirical null of 1000 random cluster assignments; Fisher's exact test for haplotype enrichment of clusters.
tools.input: ONT BAM with per-read CpG methylation calls (via cvlr-meth-of-bam) or Nanopolish output -> binary read x CpG matrix with missing entries allowed.
tools.purpose: Find genomic windows where reads split into methylation-defined subpopulations (imprinting / ASM / cell-subpopulation heterogeneity) directly from long reads without prior phasing.
tools.key_claims: Exploits long-read co-methylation; phasing-free EM mixture; recovers known imprinted loci; chr15 genome-window scan for heterogeneous methylation. Read-level molecule subpopulations.
tools.citation: Raineri E, Alberola i Pla M, Dabad M, Heath S. cvlr: finding heterogeneously methylated genomic regions using ONT reads. Bioinformatics Advances 2023;3(1):vbac101. DOI 10.1093/bioadv/vbac101. PMC9887406.

tools.name: Metheor
tools.type: SHORT-READ bisulfite (Bismark alignments), cancer cell lines; within-read CpG-CpG methylation heterogeneity/disorder measures (one-sweep, no clustering)
tools.method_core: Single-pass ('one-sweep') read-centric scan over Bismark-tagged bisulfite alignments computing intra-molecule (within-read) co-methylation disorder. Implemented in Rust. Computes a family of heterogeneity scores; NO model fitting, NO clustering, NO distance matrix. LPMD (novel) = proportion of reads showing DIFFERENT methylation states for a pair of CpGs placed at a FIXED genomic distance apart (scanned over distances ~2-16 bp), normalizing PDR's read-length bias by binning on inter-CpG distance.
tools.granularity: Multi-level OUTPUT: CpG-wise (PDR, MHL, FDRP, qFDRP), CpG-quartet/window-wise (PM/epipolymorphism, ME entropy), genome-wide averages, and region-level (CpG islands/promoters/gene bodies). All derived from WITHIN-READ CpG co-occurrence; never between-read clustering.
tools.vs_ism: Overlaps ISM CORE 4 'disorder family' (ME = normalized methylation entropy ~ ISM NME; PM = epipolymorphism over a 4-CpG window = ISM 4-CpG epipolymorphism; LPMD/PDR = within-read discordance). BUT Metheor is BISULFITE SHORT-READ (not ONT long-read, no 5hmC, no MM/ML tags) and crucially does the DISORDER axis ONLY -> it has NO between-molecule STRUCTURE test: no read-to-read distance matrix, no clustering, no PERMANOVA. This is the cleanest external confirmation that ISM's 'structure not disorder' engine (distance matrix + hierarchical clustering + PERMANOVA pseudo-F) is distinct. Metheor is not haplotype-phasing aware (MHL is consecutive-CpG conservation, not HP). No somatic tumor-normal cis-test, no LOH/CN coupling, no delta-beta-by-haplotype.
tools.haplotype_aware: NO genuine phasing. Only MHL (Methylation Haplotype Load) measures conserved consecutive-CpG methylated stretches within a read = co-methylation block load, not haplotype/HP-tag phasing.
tools.cancer_somatic: Cancer-oriented application (928 CCLE cancer cell lines; links methylation homogeneity to stemness/metastatic potential/Wnt) BUT short-read bisulfite, cell-line, no tumor-normal-paired somatic-variant design.
tools.statistics: Descriptive heterogeneity metrics (no inferential test in core): PDR (proportion discordant reads), ME (Shannon methylation entropy over CpG window), PM/epipolymorphism, FDRP, qFDRP (quantitative fraction discordant read pairs), MHL (methylation haplotype load), LPMD (local pairwise methylation discordance at fixed CpG distance). Validated as numerically identical to reference implementations.
tools.input: Bisulfite read alignment BAM with Bismark XM methylation-call strings (NOT nanopore MM/ML).
tools.purpose: Ultrafast genome-wide computation of DNA-methylation intramolecular heterogeneity/disorder metrics for downstream epigenomic analysis.
tools.key_claims: Up to 300x faster execution and 60x lower memory than prior R/Perl/Python tools (methclone, WSHPackage) with identical results; single-thread beat 32-thread WSHPackage 13.7-175.8x on PDR/FDRP/qFDRP. Novel LPMD distance-aware discordance.
tools.citation: Lee D, et al. Metheor: Ultrafast DNA methylation heterogeneity calculation from bisulfite read alignments. PLOS Computational Biology 2023;19(3):e1010946. DOI 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1010946. PMC10062925. Code github.com/dohlee/metheor (GPL-3.0).

survey.category: long-read phasing and allele-specific-methylation (ASM) tools — comparison vs ISM (InterSubMod)

tools.name: MethPhaser
tools.type: long-read (ONT R9/R10), 5mC CpG via Remora/Dorado; standalone Python tool
tools.purpose: EXTEND SNV-based haplotype phase blocks across stretches of homozygosity (no het SNVs) using haplotype-specific methylation — i.e. methylation is USED TO PHASE, not the readout.
tools.method_core: SNV-FIRST then methylation extension. Input = pre-phased SNVs (WhatsHap) + BAM with MM/ML tags. Between two adjacent SNV phase blocks separated by a homozygous gap, it tests whether the two alleles' base-modification probabilities differ, then assigns/votes reads from the gap to a block by which haplotype methylation pattern they match. Iterative block-to-block linkage.
tools.statistics: Wilcoxon rank-sum test on per-allele base-modification probabilities (haplotype-specific methylation if p<0.05). Read assignment via VOTING (not a probabilistic model): default min coverage per haplotype = 3, min votes = 3.
tools.granularity: read-level assignment operating within SNV-defined phase-block context; output is extended/linked phase blocks (haplotype-level product).
tools.haplotype_aware: yes — its entire purpose is haplotype phasing; methylation is the linkage signal, not the output.
tools.cancer_somatic: GERMLINE / diploid genomes (HG002 cell lines). Authors explicitly state somatic/cancer heterogeneous signals are FUTURE work, not implemented.
tools.input: pre-phased SNV VCF (WhatsHap) + BAM with 5mC MM/ML tags (ONT). Output: re-phased/linked blocks.
tools.key_claims: N50 increased 78–151% (~1.6–2.5x) on HG002 R9/R10; phasing accuracy 83.4–98.7%; minimal added error (~0.0012% switch error increase). VERIFIED from PMC11193733 methods.
tools.vs_ism: OPPOSITE direction of use. MethPhaser CONSUMES methylation to build phase; ISM CONSUMES haplotype (HP tags from LOH-constrained phasing) to MEASURE somatic ASM structure. MethPhaser stat = Wilcoxon on per-allele mod-probability (2-sample location test, germline diploid); ISM = read-to-read DISTANCE matrix + PERMANOVA (pseudo-F, 999 perm) testing structural separation of read groups + per-CpG Δβ Wilcoxon signed-rank (CpG-paired) + NormalBaseline cis-test. MethPhaser is region-gap read-voting; ISM is between-molecule clustering/dispersion. MethPhaser has NO normal-anchored somatic control, NO LOH/CN coupling, NO 5hmC (5mC only). ISM is the somatic-cancer mirror image: phasing is the INPUT not the goal.
tools.citation: Fu Y, Aganezov S, Mahmoud M, Beaulaurier J, Juul S, Treangen TJ, Sedlazeck FJ. MethPhaser: methylation-based long-read haplotype phasing of human genomes. Nat Commun 2024;15:5328. DOI 10.1038/s41467-024-49588-0. PMID 38909018. PMC11193733.

tools.name: NanoMethPhase
tools.type: long-read (ONT) only; Python tool + companion SNVoter NN. 5mC only (Nanopolish-based).
tools.purpose: PHASE 5mC reads to the two germline haplotypes and detect allele-specific methylation / differentially methylated regions between haplotypes — the canonical 'phase-first, then ASM' tool.
tools.method_core: PHASE-FIRST then ASM. Phased SNVs + per-read CpG methylation calls are used to assign reads to diploid haplotypes ('phase reads along their CpG methylation to diploid haplotypes'); then differential methylation between the two haplotype read sets is called. SNVoter optionally upgrades low-coverage SNV calls before phasing.
tools.statistics: DMR/differential-methylation-analysis via the DSS R/Bioconductor package (Dispersion Shrinkage for Sequencing; beta-binomial / Wald with area statistic across CpGs in a region) — NOT a simple Fisher/threshold. SNVoter = fully-connected ANN (4 hidden layers, ReLU) classifying true vs false SNV from base quality + 5-mer mutation frequencies.
tools.granularity: region-level (DMR) is the primary ASM output; reads are first haplotagged (read-level intermediate) then aggregated into haplotype-level methylation tracks/DMRs.
tools.haplotype_aware: yes — diploid germline haplotypes (HP1/HP2); designed around het SNVs.
tools.cancer_somatic: GERMLINE / imprinting (parent-of-origin, ICRs) is the design target. Paper NOTES LOH-cancer is a possible application ('can also be leveraged to investigate cancers presenting loss of heterozygosity') but provides NO somatic algorithm or normal control — it is an aspirational sentence, not a method.
tools.input: phased het SNV VCF + ONT BAM with 5mC; ~10x coverage sufficient (vs ~250x/strand for array/short-read). Output: per-haplotype methylation + DMRs.
tools.key_claims: Megabase-scale phasing at ~10x; DSS-based DMR. VERIFIED from PMC7898412 methods. (LOH-cancer = mentioned only, UNVERIFIED as an implemented capability.)
tools.vs_ism: Closest archetype to the GERMLINE counterpart of ISM, but three core divergences: (1) Germline imprinting, het-SNV-anchored — ISM is somatic cancer, LOH-constrained (often NO het SNVs, so HP tags come from copy/somatic phasing not germline het). (2) DSS beta-binomial DMR region statistic vs ISM PERMANOVA-on-distance-matrix (structure) + per-CpG Δβ Wilcoxon-signed-rank (CpG-paired magnitude) + Cramér-V Cochran gate. (3) NO normal-anchored cis-test — NanoMethPhase cannot separate true cis-driven somatic ASM from baseline allelic methylation drift; ISM's NormalBaseline residual + d_somatic/d_cis/d_drift decomposition exists precisely to remove the confound NanoMethPhase ignores. Also 5mC-only vs ISM 5mC+5hmC.
tools.citation: Akbari V, Garant J-M, O'Neill K, Pandoh P, Moore R, Marra MA, Hirst M, Jones SJM. Megabase-scale methylation phasing using nanopore long reads and NanoMethPhase. Genome Biol 2021;22:68. DOI 10.1186/s13059-021-02283-5. PMID 33618748. PMC7898412.

tools.name: NANOME
tools.type: long-read (ONT R9.4.1/R10.4) only; Nextflow pipeline (cloud/container).
tools.purpose: Consensus single-molecule 5mC calling (combine 3 callers) PLUS a haplotype-aware allele-specific-methylation module bolted on via variant-calling + phasing.
tools.method_core: Two parts. (a) CONSENSUS CALLER: XGBoost meta-model over Megalodon + Nanopolish + DeepSignal per-CpG predictions + 17-nt sequence feature, inverse-class-frequency weighting toward discordant/non-singleton hard regions. (b) HAPLOTYPE-AWARE ASM: PHASE-FIRST — Clair3 variant calling + long-read phasing, then allele-specific methylation in imprinting controls (incl. previously unresolved regions).
tools.statistics: Consensus model: XGBoost (lr=0.1, n_estimators=60, max_depth=9, subsample=0.8; F1=0.926). ASM/DMR: methylKit Chi-squared test, q<0.05, 1000bp sliding window/step. Phasing validated against NanoMethPhase + trio (36.6 vs 36.3 abs methylation diff).
tools.granularity: all three: single-molecule/read-level (F1), site-level (MSE), and haplotype-level (phased CpG diffs).
tools.haplotype_aware: yes — Clair3 + phasing; explicitly markets 'haplotype-aware allele-specific consensus DNAme'. Germline het-SNV anchored.
tools.cancer_somatic: GERMLINE imprinting controls (NA12878/NA19240/NA24385 B-lymphocyte lines). NOT cancer/somatic; no LOH handling described.
tools.input: FAST5/POD5 ONT signal (needs raw signal for the 3 callers), hg38 or T2T-CHM13. Output: consensus per-CpG + per-haplotype methylation.
tools.key_claims: Consensus +11% site-level precision (MSE), +2.4% read-level F1 vs best single tool on NA12878; ~200k more CpGs covered than any single tool. VERIFIED from PMC12236756. 2025 bioRxiv preprint (not yet peer-reviewed journal).
tools.vs_ism: Different layer. NANOME's novelty is the CONSENSUS CALLER (caller-ensembling at signal level — orthogonal to ISM, which consumes already-called MM/ML probabilities from the BAM, no re-calling). Its ASM module is again phase-first germline imprinting with methylKit Chi-square sliding-window DMR — a per-window association test, NOT the read-to-read distance/PERMANOVA structure engine of ISM, and NO somatic normal-anchored cis decomposition, NO LOH/CN coupling. Needs raw FAST5/POD5 (heavy); ISM works from MM/ML-tagged BAM only. Preprint, single germline cell line for ASM.
tools.citation: Liu Y, Taha HB, Zhang Q, Pan Z, Chatzipantsiou C, Wade E, Slocum T, Karuturi L, Zhao Y, Karmakar S, Li S. NANOME: A Nextflow pipeline for haplotype-aware allele-specific consensus DNA methylation detection by nanopore long-read sequencing. bioRxiv 2025.06.29.662079 (posted 2025-07-04). PMC12236756.

tools.name: HapBridge
tools.type: long-read (ONT R9/R10 + PacBio HiFi); methylation-guided phasing add-on. 2025 preprint.
tools.purpose: Improve EXISTING SNV-based phasing: correct switch errors and bridge adjacent phased blocks using haplotype-specific methylation — same family as MethPhaser (methylation USED TO PHASE), positioned as its successor.
tools.method_core: PHASE-FIRST then methylation refinement, two modules. (1) switch-error-correction: identifies haplotype-specific methylation (HSM) sites and uses their INTER-SITE CONSISTENCY to localize and flip switch errors. (2) block-bridging: iteratively infers haplotype tags for unphased reads from HSM sites, then uses those newly-tagged reads to discover MORE HSM sites (EM-like bootstrap). Requires no extra sequencing.
tools.statistics: Mechanism = haplotype-specific-methylation-site detection + inter-site consistency scoring + iterative inference (per abstract). EXACT statistical test (e.g. whether HSM detection uses a t-test / Fisher / beta-binomial / consistency-threshold) NOT confirmed — methods PDF/full-text returned HTTP 403, could not fetch. UNVERIFIED at the test level.
tools.granularity: site-level (HSM sites) + read-level (unphased read tagging) → haplotype-level (corrected/bridged blocks).
tools.haplotype_aware: yes — phasing is the goal; methylation is linkage signal.
tools.cancer_somatic: GERMLINE diploid (HG002-type cell lines, R9/R10/HiFi). No somatic/LOH-specific method described in available abstract.
tools.input: pre-phased SNVs + BAM with methylation; ONT R9/R10 + PacBio HiFi. Output: switch-corrected, bridged phase blocks.
tools.key_claims: vs MethPhaser: switch errors reduced 3.07–18.72%; N50 improved 5.84–68.61%; higher accuracy/contiguity. VERIFIED from abstract/search; numbers from primary preprint listing. Full methods UNVERIFIED (403).
tools.vs_ism: Same axis as MethPhaser — a phasing IMPROVER that EATS methylation, the inverse of ISM (which eats phasing to MEASURE somatic methylation structure). Differs from MethPhaser by adding switch-error correction + iterative HSM bootstrap and PacBio HiFi support, but still germline, het-SNV-rooted, no normal-anchored somatic cis-test, no LOH-as-feature, no PERMANOVA/distance-matrix structure test. Relevant to ISM only as a potential UPSTREAM phaser (better HP tags) — never as an ASM-measurement competitor.
tools.citation: Chen H, Nie F, Luo F, Wang J. HapBridge: A Methylation-Guided Approach for Correcting Switch Errors and Bridging Phased Blocks in Long-Read Phasing. bioRxiv 2025.11.07.687303 (posted Nov 2025).

tools.name: longphase modcall (+ co-phasing)
tools.type: long-read (ONT + PacBio HiFi/CCS); C/C++ tool (Lin & Huang). modcall subcommand of LongPhase.
tools.purpose: modcall = detect allele-specific (haplotype-differential) 5mC modification sites and emit them as a VCF; the phase command then CO-PHASES SNP+INDEL+5mC jointly, so methylation both contributes to and is phased by the haplotype assignment.
tools.method_core: modcall scans MM/ML-tagged BAM, binarizes per-position modification, and emits sites where the two allele groups differ in methylation into modcall.vcf. Phasing: `phase --mod-file modcall.vcf` jointly phases SNP+INDEL+modification (graph/weighted-edge phasing, same engine that co-phases SNP+SV). v2.0 adds ModCall x SNP-modification co-phasing.
tools.statistics: THRESHOLD-based, not a hypothesis test: modThreshold=0.8 (call modified if ML>0.8), unModThreshold=0.2 (unmod if <0.2), heterRatio=0.7 (keep sites where mod/unmod ratio looks allelic), noiseRatio=0.2 (drop ambiguous). Phasing = max-weight haplotype assignment over variant+mod edges (no p-value).
tools.granularity: site-level modification calls (modcall.vcf) consumed by haplotype-level phasing; produces phased SNP+mod VCFs.
tools.haplotype_aware: yes — co-phases modifications with SNPs/indels/SVs into haplotype blocks.
tools.cancer_somatic: GERMLINE-oriented (ultra-fast whole-genome diploid phasing; benchmarked on standard cell-line genomes). Not a somatic/LOH ASM tool; no normal control.
tools.input: BAM with MM/ML tags (ONT or PacBio) + SNP VCF. Output: modcall.vcf + phased SNP/mod VCFs. Original 2022 paper = SNP+SV phasing; methylation co-phasing is a later v2.0 extension.
tools.key_claims: Core 2022: co-phasing SNP+SV N50≈25Mbp, 10x faster than WhatsHap/HapCUT2/Margin (VERIFIED, Bioinformatics 2022, btac058). Methylation co-phasing v2.0: ModCall-only SNP-methylation N50≈5.17Mb vs ~3.10Mb SNP-only (from project release notes, peer-review status of this specific number UNVERIFIED).
tools.vs_ism: Notable: longphase modcall's binarization thresholds (mod>0.8, unmod<0.2) are IDENTICAL to ISM's MethylationMatrix binarization (>0.8 meth / <0.2 unmeth) — same upstream convention. But modcall is a phasing-engine site-caller using fixed ratio thresholds and graph max-weight assignment; it has NO statistical structure test, NO read-to-read distance matrix, NO PERMANOVA, NO normal-baseline somatic cis-test, NO LOH/CN coupling. modcall ASKS 'do alleles differ enough to phase?'; ISM ASKS 'are somatic read groups structurally organized, and is the ASM cis-driven after holding CN/normal constant?'. longphase is the canonical UPSTREAM phaser ISM-style pipelines build on (provides HP tags); not an ASM-measurement competitor.
tools.citation: Lin J-H, Chen L-C, Yu S-C, Huang Y-T. LongPhase: an ultra-fast chromosome-scale phasing algorithm for small and large variants. Bioinformatics 2022;38(7):1816-1822. DOI 10.1093/bioinformatics/btac058. (modcall/methylation co-phasing = later v2.0; GitHub twolinin/longphase.)

survey.notes:
SCOPE/TASK TYPE: this is a literature-survey (D-handoff-flavored reference table), all claims sourced from primary docs; marked verified=false where I could not fetch the methods-level text.

KEY CROSS-CUTTING FINDING (the framing that matters for the InterSubMod/G6 paper):
All five tools sit on the OPPOSITE side of the methylation<->haplotype relationship from ISM, EXCEPT they split into two sub-families:
  - FAMILY 1 'methylation -> phasing' (USE methylation to build/extend/correct haplotypes): MethPhaser, HapBridge, longphase modcall-cophasing. For them methylation is the INPUT signal; the deliverable is a better phase block. Stats are Wilcoxon (MethPhaser), inter-site consistency/iterative (HapBridge), fixed ratio thresholds + graph max-weight (longphase).
  - FAMILY 2 'phasing -> ASM readout' (phase FIRST by germline het SNV, then report per-haplotype methylation / DMR): NanoMethPhase (DSS beta-binomial DMR), NANOME (methylKit Chi-square sliding window + XGBoost consensus caller). This family is the closest archetype to ISM's *output*, but is GERMLINE-IMPRINTING in design.

ISM's distinct niche (none of the five occupy it):
  1. SOMATIC CANCER, LOH-CONSTRAINED — haplotypes often come from copy/somatic phasing where germline het SNVs are absent (the exact regime every one of these 5 germline tools is weakest/undefined in). NanoMethPhase only *mentions* LOH-cancer in one sentence (UNVERIFIED as implemented); none others touch it.
  2. STRUCTURE-NOT-DISORDER ENGINE — read-to-read DISTANCE matrix (NHD/L1/Bernoulli/Pearson/Jaccard) + hierarchical clustering + PERMANOVA pseudo-F (999 perm) + dispersion test. NO surveyed tool builds a between-molecule distance matrix or runs PERMANOVA; they all do per-site/per-region association or location tests.
  3. NORMAL-ANCHORED CIS-TEST — NormalBaseline residual + d_somatic/d_cis/d_drift + copy-partition (d_copy + d_within + drift). This is ISM's confound-control answer to exactly the baseline-allelic-methylation confound that Family 2 (DSS/Chi-square DMR) cannot separate. No surveyed tool has a normal-anchored somatic control.
  4. 5mC AND 5hmC (from MM/ML); MethPhaser/NanoMethPhase/longphase are effectively 5mC-only.
  5. EXPLICIT NEGATIVE FRAMING — ISM concludes methylation is NOT a usable TP/FP somatic-variant filter and positions LOH-constrained phasing as the live positive; none of the surveyed tools test methylation as a variant-quality filter (different question entirely).

CONVERGENCE worth citing in the paper: longphase modcall binarization thresholds (mod>0.8 / unmod<0.2) are IDENTICAL to ISM's MethylationMatrix binarization — shared upstream convention, supports that ISM's calling layer is community-standard while its analysis layer (distance/PERMANOVA/cis) is the novel part.

PIPELINE RELATIONSHIP not rivalry: longphase (and potentially MethPhaser/HapBridge) are legitimate UPSTREAM phasers that could supply ISM's HP tags. They are not ASM-measurement competitors.

VERIFICATION STATUS: MethPhaser, NanoMethPhase, NANOME, longphase — methods verified from PMC/journal primary text (PMC11193733, PMC7898412, PMC12236756, Bioinformatics btac058 / longphase GitHub). HapBridge — abstract + headline numbers verified from bioRxiv listing, but full methods/exact statistical test could NOT be fetched (HTTP 403 on full-text PDF and v1 page); its statistic is marked UNVERIFIED. longphase methylation-co-phasing N50≈5.17Mb number is from release notes (UNVERIFIED peer-review status); the 2022 SNP+SV N50≈25Mbp/10x-speed claims are journal-verified.

CAVEAT: NANOME and HapBridge are 2025 preprints (not peer-reviewed). MethPhaser N50 was reported by the Nat Commun paper as 78-151% increase (~1.6-2.5x) — both phrasings appear; I report both.

survey.category: Short-read (2nd-gen WGBS/RRBS) and array general DMR/DMC callers — surveyed as the comparison baseline against ISM (ONT long-read cancer somatic, read-level haplotype-aware). KEY CONTRAST: every tool below operates on COLLAPSED per-CpG count summaries (methylated/unmethylated read counts per cytosine per sample) and tests BETWEEN-GROUP MEAN methylation differences (group = condition/case-control, defined a priori). NONE is read-level (no read x CpG matrix), NONE is haplotype-aware (no within-sample HP1-vs-HP1-1 axis), NONE models between-molecule subclonal STRUCTURE via a read-to-read distance matrix + PERMANOVA. All are designed for germline/population EWAS-style group comparison; cancer use is as a downstream cohort application, not a tumor-internal somatic/allelic engine. Spatial CpG correlation is handled by SMOOTHING (DSS, BSmooth, DMRcate, dmrseq), SEGMENTATION (metilene), or P-VALUE AUTOCORRELATION COMBINATION (comb-p) — i.e. on the 1D genomic-coordinate axis, never on the molecule axis that ISM's distance matrix uses.

tools.name: DSS (Dispersion Shrinkage for Sequencing)
tools.type: short-read WGBS/RRBS; general/germline (group case-control); region+single-CpG; NOT long-read, NOT cancer-specific, NOT haplotype-aware
tools.method_core: Beta-binomial model of methylated read counts per CpG. Two-paper lineage: (1) original DSS — arcsine/Wald with a moving-average SMOOTHING step (default 500 bp window) to estimate mean methylation, then empirical-Bayes (log-normal prior) dispersion SHRINKAGE borrowing info from neighboring CpGs as pseudo-replicates, then a Wald test per CpG modified for the smoothing; (2) Park & Wu 2016 generalization — beta-binomial REGRESSION with an 'arcsine' link function for general experimental design (covariates, multi-factor). DML (single-CpG) called by Wald p-value; DMR called by callDMR aggregating adjacent significant DML under p-value threshold + min-length/min-CpG criteria.
tools.granularity: DML = single CpG; DMR = aggregated multi-CpG region (callDMR). Both levels native.
tools.statistics: Beta-binomial; empirical Bayes dispersion shrinkage (log-normal prior); Wald test; arcsine-link beta-binomial GLM (Park&Wu). Spatial CpG correlation handled by 500bp moving-average SMOOTHING of mean methylation + neighbor-borrowing for dispersion. Works WITHOUT replicates (smoothing supplies pseudo-replicates).
tools.haplotype_aware: No — tests between-GROUP mean (condition contrast). No within-sample haplotype axis, no read-to-read structure.
tools.cancer_somatic: General-purpose; no somatic/tumor-normal or LOH/CN coupling. Cancer use only as a cohort group comparison.
tools.input: Per-CpG methylated/total read counts per sample (collapsed pileup), e.g. from Bismark. No reads, no MM/ML, no 5hmC distinction.
tools.vs_ism: DSS aggregates reads into per-CpG counts and tests GROUP MEAN difference (Wald on beta-binomial); ISM keeps the read x CpG matrix and tests whether read GROUPS are STRUCTURALLY separated (read-to-read distance + PERMANOVA pseudo-F). DSS's smoothing handles 1D genomic spatial correlation; ISM's distance matrix handles between-MOLECULE organization. DSS Wald-DML is the closest analogue to ISM's CORE-4 per-CpG Fisher+BH 'disorder' family, but DSS has no haplotype/somatic-residual (no NormalBaseline) and no subclonal clustering. ISM's Delta-beta (paired Wilcoxon signed-rank per CpG) parallels DSS DML logic but on HP1-vs-HP1-1 (somatic-controlled) rather than case-vs-control groups.
tools.key_claims: Empirical-Bayes dispersion shrinkage enables DMR detection WITHOUT replicates (PMC4666378). Park&Wu arcsine beta-binomial GLM extends to general design.
tools.purpose: Detect DML/DMR between predefined sample groups in BS-seq.
tools.citation: Feng, Conneely, Wu 2014 Nucleic Acids Res, PMID 26184873 / DOI 10.1093/nar/gkv715 (DML+smoothing+EB shrinkage+Wald); Wu et al 2015 (no-replicate DMR) PMC4666378; Park & Wu 2016 Bioinformatics 32(10):1446-53, PMID 26819470 / DOI 10.1093/bioinformatics/btw026 (arcsine beta-binomial GLM, general design)

tools.name: methylKit
tools.type: short-read WGBS/RRBS (+ array-compatible counts); general/germline; per-base or tiled-region; NOT long-read, NOT haplotype-aware
tools.method_core: calculateDiffMeth: if multiple samples/group -> logistic regression of (methylated C, unmethylated C) on group, tested by Chi-square (default) or F-test; if one sample/group -> Fisher's exact test (fast.fisher or midPval). Optional overdispersion correction overdispersion='MN' (McCullagh & Nelder 1989 scaling) or experimental 'shrinkMN'. Logistic regression allows sample-specific covariates / confounder adjustment. Region analysis via fixed tiling windows (tileMethylCounts) or predefined regions, not de-novo segmentation.
tools.granularity: Per-CpG (per-base) primary; tiled fixed-window regions optional. No de-novo boundary detection.
tools.statistics: Logistic regression (Chisq/F) or Fisher's exact; overdispersion='none'(default)/'MN'/'shrinkMN'; p-value adjust default SLIM (also BH/qvalue/bonferroni). Does NOT model adjacent-CpG spatial correlation in its core test (each CpG/tile tested independently).
tools.haplotype_aware: No — group (treatment vs control) contrast only.
tools.cancer_somatic: General; covariate adjustment supports EWAS but no somatic/allelic or tumor-normal residual model.
tools.input: Per-CpG methylated/unmethylated counts per sample (CpG report). No read-level matrix, no MM/ML, no 5hmC vs 5mC separation in the test.
tools.vs_ism: methylKit's logistic regression is a per-site GROUP-mean test with explicit independence across CpGs (it openly does NOT model spatial correlation) — the opposite of ISM, which is built ON the between-read distance matrix. methylKit covariate adjustment is the analogue of ISM's NormalBaseline residual conceptually, but operates between groups not within-sample haplotypes. Fisher's exact single-pair mode mirrors ISM CORE-4 per-CpG Fisher, but ISM uses it as a 'disorder' contrast alongside the PERMANOVA 'structure' engine, whereas methylKit Fisher IS the whole test.
tools.key_claims: Logistic regression advantage = covariate/confounder adjustment vs Fisher (paper + docs). SLIM is default q-value method.
tools.purpose: Genome-wide differential methylation between groups; widely used general toolkit.
tools.citation: Akalin et al 2012 Genome Biology 13:R87, PMID 23034086 / DOI 10.1186/gb-2012-13-10-r87; calculateDiffMeth docs rdrr.io/bioc/methylKit

tools.name: metilene
tools.type: short-read WGBS/RRBS / any methylation-level input; general/germline; de-novo DMR + DMC; NOT long-read, NOT haplotype-aware
tools.method_core: Fast circular binary segmentation (CBS) on the MEAN methylation DIFFERENCE signal between two groups to define candidate DMR boundaries de novo; after filter steps (min CpG count, min length) each candidate is tested by a two-dimensional Kolmogorov-Smirnov test (2D-KS); output also reports an independent Mann-Whitney U test p-value. Handles multiple groups and works without replicates; can estimate missing data.
tools.granularity: DMR (de-novo segmented region) primary; also reports DMC (single CpG). Region boundaries discovered by segmentation, not fixed windows.
tools.statistics: Circular binary segmentation (signal = group mean-difference) + 2D Kolmogorov-Smirnov test (adjusted + unadjusted p) + independent Mann-Whitney U. Spatial CpG correlation handled IMPLICITLY by the segmentation grouping (no explicit kernel/GLS). No replicates required.
tools.haplotype_aware: No — two-group (or multi-group) contrast on collapsed levels.
tools.cancer_somatic: General; no somatic/allelic model. Often applied to tumor cohorts but treats them as a group.
tools.input: Tab matrix of per-CpG absolute methylation levels + coordinates per sample. No reads/MM/ML.
tools.vs_ism: metilene's CBS segments along the GENOMIC axis using the between-group mean-difference; ISM's hierarchical clustering segments along the MOLECULE axis using read-to-read distance — orthogonal segmentation targets. metilene 2D-KS tests distributional difference between two GROUPS' per-CpG levels; ISM PERMANOVA tests structural separation of read GROUPS within one sample's distance matrix. Neither KS nor MWU is haplotype/somatic-aware. metilene is the cleanest 'region-level, no-replicate, group-difference' counterpart to highlight ISM's read-level/haplotype novelty.
tools.key_claims: CBS + 2D-KS gives DMRs 'in minutes', sensitive at low coverage, reliable without replicates (abstract).
tools.purpose: Fast de-novo DMR calling for large multi-group methylation experiments.
tools.citation: Juhling et al 2016 Genome Research 26(2):256-262, PMID 26631489 / DOI 10.1101/gr.196394.115

tools.name: bsseq / BSmooth
tools.type: short-read WGBS (low-coverage friendly); general/germline; region (DMR); NOT long-read, NOT haplotype-aware
tools.method_core: BSmooth: local-likelihood SMOOTHING of methylation levels via locfit (bandwidth = max of genomic distance h and a width containing ns methylation loci), giving reliable semi-local estimates from low coverage. Then a signal-to-noise t-statistic = difference of smoothed group means / estimated SD; SDs are themselves smoothed (running mean width k) and thresholded (qSd quantile floor). DMRs = runs of CpGs exceeding a t-stat cutoff. Requires biological replicates to estimate biological variation.
tools.granularity: Region (DMR = contiguous CpG runs over t-stat threshold). Smoothing is semi-local per-CpG but inference is region-oriented.
tools.statistics: Local-likelihood (locfit) smoothing; signal-to-noise t-statistic with smoothed + thresholded SD. Spatial CpG correlation handled directly by SMOOTHING. Needs >=2 replicates per group (BSmooth.tstat errors on single replicate).
tools.haplotype_aware: No — between-group t-statistic.
tools.cancer_somatic: General; no somatic-residual / allelic model.
tools.input: Per-CpG methylated/total counts per sample. No reads/MM/ML.
tools.vs_ism: BSmooth smooths along genomic coordinate to denoise low-coverage GROUP means then takes a t-stat — a 'mean-difference + smoothing' philosophy. ISM does NOT smooth; it preserves per-read binarized states (>0.8 / <0.2) and measures between-molecule distance.
