BSmooth t-stat is group-level; ISM Delta-beta uses a paired Wilcoxon signed-rank per CpG within haplotype pairs. BSmooth's smoothing = 1D spatial-correlation handling; ISM's distance matrix = molecular-correlation handling. Good contrast for 'smoothing-based region caller' vs ISM's 'structure engine'.
tools.key_claims: Smoothing yields reliable estimates from low-coverage WGBS; signal-to-noise t-stat localizes DMRs (Hansen 2012).
tools.purpose: WGBS read-to-DMR pipeline robust to low/variable coverage.
tools.citation: Hansen, Langmead, Irizarry 2012 Genome Biology 13:R83, PMID 23034175 / DOI 10.1186/gb-2012-13-10-r83

tools.name: dmrseq
tools.type: short-read WGBS/RRBS; general/germline; region-level inference with genome-wide-comparable statistic; NOT long-read, NOT haplotype-aware
tools.method_core: Two-stage: (1) candidate DMR detection by segmenting genome into CpG groups with consistent differential-methylation evidence; (2) region statistic from a generalized least squares (GLS) regression with a NESTED AUTOREGRESSIVE (AR-type) correlated error structure on transformed (arcsine) methylation proportions — simultaneously accounting for inter-individual (biological-replicate) variability AND spatial correlation among neighboring loci. Region significance via PERMUTATION using a pooled null distribution (from as few as 2 replicates); FDR by Benjamini-Hochberg q-values.
tools.granularity: Region (collection of neighboring CpGs); the statistic is explicitly designed to be COMPARABLE across regions genome-wide.
tools.statistics: GLS with nested AR(1) correlated errors on arcsine-transformed proportions; region PERMUTATION test (pooled null); BH FDR. Spatial CpG correlation modeled EXPLICITLY inside the GLS error structure (not just smoothing). Requires >=2 samples/condition.
tools.haplotype_aware: No — condition/covariate effect, between groups.
tools.cancer_somatic: General; rigorous FDR for EWAS-style designs; no somatic/allelic engine.
tools.input: Per-CpG methylated/total counts per sample (BSseq object). No reads/MM/ML.
tools.vs_ism: dmrseq is the most statistically rigorous short-read analogue and shares ISM's PERMUTATION-test philosophy — but the permutation is over SAMPLE LABELS to get a region p-value, whereas ISM's PERMANOVA permutes read-group labels within ONE sample's distance matrix (999 perms, pseudo-F). dmrseq's AR(1)-in-GLS models spatial correlation on the genomic axis; ISM models molecular correlation on the read axis. dmrseq needs >=2 biological replicates; ISM works on a single sample's read population (no cross-sample replication needed for the structure test). dmrseq = best 'rigorous region FDR' baseline to position ISM as 'rigorous read-level STRUCTURE' rather than region mean-difference.
tools.key_claims: GLS+AR error gives genome-comparable region statistic; permutation pooled null controls FDR accurately from >=2 replicates (Korthauer 2018 Biostatistics).
tools.purpose: Accurate region-level differential methylation with calibrated FDR.
tools.citation: Korthauer, Chakraborty, Benjamini, Irizarry 2018 Biostatistics 19(3):367-383, PMID 29481604 / DOI 10.1093/biostatistics/kxy007; GitHub kdkorthauer/dmrseq

tools.name: DMRcate
tools.type: array (Illumina 450K/EPIC) primary, also WGBS; general/germline; region; NOT long-read, NOT haplotype-aware
tools.method_core: Takes per-CpG/probe differential-methylation statistics from limma's moderated t (uses the SQUARED moderated t, t^2, as an unsigned per-site metric -> agnostic to DM direction). Applies a GAUSSIAN KERNEL to smooth t^2 within a window; kernel scale sigma = lambda/C (default lambda=1000bp, optimal sigma~500bp at C=2). Corrects for irregular/reduced-representation CpG spacing using coordinate-only constants (S_K, S_KK) to derive the expected smoothed value. DMR significance: smoothed statistic modeled via Satterthwaite approximation as scaled chi-squared, p-value vs null, then BH correction. DMRs = contiguous regions of significant smoothed signal.
tools.granularity: Region (DMR); input statistic is per-probe/CpG from limma.
tools.statistics: limma moderated-t (empirical Bayes) -> Gaussian-kernel smoothing of t^2 -> Satterthwaite scaled chi-square p-value -> BH FDR. Spatial CpG correlation handled by Gaussian KERNEL with explicit irregular-spacing correction. Replicates handled by limma design.
tools.haplotype_aware: No — limma group/coefficient contrast.
tools.cancer_somatic: General EWAS/array tool; cancer cohorts are a common application but no somatic/allelic model. Array-first (450K/EPIC).
tools.input: Beta/M-values per probe per sample (array) or per-CpG (WGBS). No reads/MM/ML; arrays cannot distinguish 5mC vs 5hmC (ISM does).
tools.vs_ism: DMRcate smooths the per-probe limma t^2 with a Gaussian kernel along genomic coordinate to merge correlated array probes into DMRs — it is array-native and unsigned. ISM operates on ONT long reads with raw 5mC AND 5hmC probabilities (arrays can't separate hydroxymethylation; DMRcate can't either), keeps per-read resolution, and tests molecular structure rather than smoothing probe statistics. DMRcate's irregular-spacing correction parallels ISM's min-common-CpG=5 coverage gate in spirit (both handle uneven CpG density) but on opposite axes (probe spacing vs read overlap). DMRcate = canonical ARRAY baseline to show ISM's long-read / read-level / 5hmC advantages.
tools.key_claims: Kernel smoothing of limma t^2 with spacing correction gives unbiased de-novo DMRs on irregular arrays; significance via scaled chi-square vs null (Peters 2015).
tools.purpose: De-novo DMR calling on Illumina arrays (and WGBS) from limma statistics.
tools.citation: Peters et al 2015 Epigenetics & Chromatin 8:6, PMID 25972926 / DOI 10.1186/1756-8935-8-6

tools.name: comb-p
tools.type: input-agnostic p-value combiner (any spatially-ordered p-values: BS-seq, arrays, ChIP/tiling); general; region; NOT a primary methylation model, NOT long-read, NOT haplotype-aware
tools.method_core: Operates on a BED of (possibly irregularly spaced) per-site p-values produced by ANY upstream test. Pipeline: (1) compute spatial AUTOCORRELATION of p-values across lags; (2) Stouffer-Liptak-Kechris (SLK) sliding-window combination — converts neighboring p-values to z-scores, sums/scales them WEIGHTED by the observed autocorrelation at each lag (a dependence correction for correlated tests); (3) BH FDR adjustment; (4) find enriched regions and apply 1-step Sidak correction for region multiple-testing (based on number of possible regions of that size given total coverage).
tools.granularity: Region (enriched runs of low combined p-values). Site-level p-values are external inputs, not computed by comb-p.
tools.statistics: Stouffer-Liptak (z-sum) with Kechris autocorrelation weighting; BH FDR; Sidak region correction. Spatial CpG correlation handled DIRECTLY via empirical autocorrelation weighting of adjacent p-values — its defining feature.
tools.haplotype_aware: No — agnostic to biology; just combines correlated p-values along coordinates.
tools.cancer_somatic: General; no biological model at all.
tools.input: BED of per-site p-values (from DSS/methylKit/limma/etc.) + coordinates. No reads/counts/MM/ML.
tools.vs_ism: comb-p is purely a SPATIAL-CORRELATION p-value aggregator on the genomic axis — it is the most explicit 'handle spatial CpG correlation' tool but does NOT generate methylation statistics itself and never sees reads. ISM generates its own structure statistic (PERMANOVA pseudo-F) from a read-to-read distance matrix and handles molecular correlation, not p-value autocorrelation. comb-p could in principle post-process ISM's CORE-4 per-CpG Fisher/BH p-values into regions, but adds nothing to ISM's haplotype/somatic structure engine. Useful to cite as 'the spatial-autocorrelation correction step' that ISM's distance+PERMANOVA design makes unnecessary at read level.
tools.key_claims: Autocorrelation-weighted Stouffer-Liptak + Sidak correctly combines/corrects spatially correlated p-values into regions (Pedersen 2012).
tools.purpose: Combine, FDR-adjust and region-ize spatially correlated p-values from any source.
tools.citation: Pedersen et al 2012 Bioinformatics 28(22):2986-2988, PMID 22954632 / DOI 10.1093/bioinformatics/bts545

tools.name: MOABS
tools.type: short-read WGBS/RRBS; general/germline; single-CpG (DMC) + post-hoc HMM DMR; NOT long-read, NOT haplotype-aware
tools.method_core: Beta-binomial HIERARCHICAL model: methylated reads ~ Binomial given methylation ratio p; p ~ Beta capturing sampling + biological variation. Empirical-Bayes prior estimated genome-wide (exploits bimodal methylation distribution: most CpGs ~0 or ~1). Outputs CDIF (Credible methylation DIFference) = distance from 0 to the nearer bound of the 95% credible interval of the between-sample difference — a single metric uniting biological magnitude + statistical significance, adjusting nominal difference by depth and reproducibility. No smoothing (preserves single-CpG resolution); DMCs clustered into DMRs post-hoc via a Hidden Markov Model.
tools.granularity: Single CpG (DMC) primary; DMR by post-hoc HMM clustering of DMCs.
tools.statistics: Beta-binomial hierarchical + empirical-Bayes genome-wide prior; CDIF = 95% credible-interval-based effect (not a p-value). Spatial CpG correlation NOT modeled in the per-CpG test; structure imposed AFTER via HMM. Works with or without replicates.
tools.haplotype_aware: No — between-sample/between-group difference.
tools.cancer_somatic: General; no somatic-residual / tumor-normal / allelic model.
tools.input: Per-CpG methylated/total counts per sample. No reads/MM/ML.
tools.vs_ism: MOABS shares ISM's EFFECT-SIZE-over-p-value instinct: CDIF (credible-interval lower bound) is conceptually similar to ISM reporting Delta-beta + Cohen d + CI ribbon rather than bare p-values. Both also use a genome/normal-wide prior/baseline (MOABS empirical-Bayes prior vs ISM NormalBaseline residual) — but MOABS's prior is for shrinkage of per-CpG ratios across the genome, while ISM's normal baseline subtracts per-CpG normal mean to isolate PURELY SOMATIC haplotype ASM. MOABS post-hoc HMM gives genomic-axis structure; ISM gives molecular-axis structure (clustering reads, not CpGs). MOABS = best 'credible-difference / effect-size-first' baseline to anchor ISM's Delta-beta + Cohen-d reporting.
tools.key_claims: CDIF combines biological + statistical significance and controls depth-driven false positives; detects single-CpG DM in small regulatory regions at 4-10x where region-averaging misses (Sun 2014).
tools.purpose: Single-CpG-resolution differential methylation with a unified credible-difference metric.
tools.citation: Sun et al 2014 Genome Biology 15:R38, PMID 24565500 / DOI 10.1186/gb-2014-15-2-r38

tools.name: RnBeads (RnBeads 2.0)
tools.type: array (Infinium 27k/450k/EPIC) + WGBS/RRBS/MeDIP/MRE-seq; general/germline (multi-platform suite); site + region; NOT long-read, NOT haplotype-aware, NOT cancer-specific
tools.method_core: Comprehensive analysis suite, not a single test. Site-level differential methylation: hierarchical linear models from limma fitted by EMPIRICAL BAYES on M-values (logit-transformed betas). Combined ranking of each site by THREE criteria — (a) absolute mean methylation difference, (b) quotient/relative ratio of means, (c) limma p-value (whether values come from distinct distributions) — combined rank = MAXIMUM (worst) of the three individual ranks. Region level: combines uncorrected per-CpG p-values within predefined regions via an EXTENSION of Fisher's method (Fisher's combined probability).
tools.granularity: Site (per-CpG/probe) + region (predefined annotation: promoters, genes, CpG islands, tiling). Uses predefined regions, not de-novo segmentation.
tools.statistics: limma hierarchical linear model + empirical Bayes (M-values); max-of-3-ranks combined ranking; region p = Fisher's-method combination of site p-values. Spatial CpG correlation handled at region level only by Fisher combination of within-region p-values (no kernel/GLS). Multi-group / paired / adjustment supported via limma design.
tools.haplotype_aware: No — sample-group contrast.
tools.cancer_somatic: Explicitly general-purpose (stem cells, EWAS, biomarker discovery incl. cancer cohorts) — NOT cancer/somatic-specific; no allelic/tumor-normal model.
tools.input: Beta/M-values (arrays) or per-CpG counts (seq) per sample. No reads/MM/ML; arrays cannot separate 5hmC.
tools.vs_ism: RnBeads is a multi-platform PIPELINE whose differential engine is limma (same family as DMRcate's input) with a max-rank fusion of effect-size + ratio + p-value — a rank-combination philosophy unlike any single ISM statistic. Its region step (Fisher combination of within-region p-values) parallels comb-p/ISM CORE-4 per-CpG Fisher+BH conceptually but with no autocorrelation weighting. RnBeads never touches reads, haplotypes, 5hmC, or molecular structure; it is the broad 'EWAS suite' baseline showing the ecosystem ISM departs from (read-level ONT cancer somatic + haplotype structure vs collapsed-count group EWAS). RnBeads max-of-3-ranks is a useful reference for ISM's multi-criterion reporting (effect + significance) but ISM adds the structural PERMANOVA axis none of these have.
tools.key_claims: limma empirical-Bayes site test + max-of-3-criteria combined rank + Fisher's-method region combination across Infinium and BS-seq platforms (Assenov 2014; Muller 2019 RnBeads 2.0).
tools.purpose: End-to-end multi-platform DNA-methylation analysis incl. differential methylation at site and region level.
tools.citation: Assenov et al 2014 Nature Methods 11(11):1138-1140, PMID 25262207 / DOI 10.1038/nmeth.3115; Muller et al 2019 (RnBeads 2.0) Genome Biology 20:55, DOI 10.1186/s13059-019-1664-9

survey.notes:
VERIFICATION STATUS: All 10 tools verified from primary sources (peer-reviewed paper + official Bioconductor/GitHub docs). Every DOI/PMID below was confirmed against PMC/PubMed/publisher pages, NOT recalled from memory.

PER-TOOL PRIMARY-SOURCE CONFIRMATION:
- DSS: PMC4666378 (no-replicate DMR) + PMID 26184873/DOI 10.1093/nar/gkv715 (DML smoothing+EB+Wald) + PMID 26819470/DOI 10.1093/bioinformatics/btw026 (Park&Wu arcsine beta-binomial GLM) — note DSS is TWO papers; the 'Wald' the user named is the original Feng/Wu DML, the 'general design' is Park&Wu. CONFIRMED arcsine link, 500bp smoothing window, EB dispersion shrinkage with neighbor pseudo-replicates.
- methylKit: PMID 23034086/DOI 10.1186/gb-2012-13-10-r87 + calculateDiffMeth rdrr docs. CONFIRMED logistic-regression-vs-Fisher selection, overdispersion='MN' (McCullagh&Nelder 1989), test=Chisq/F/fast.fisher/midPval, adjust default SLIM. CONFIRMED docs state it does NOT model adjacent-CpG correlation.
- metilene: PMID 26631489/DOI 10.1101/gr.196394.115 (Genome Research 2016). CBS + 2D-KS + MWU + de-novo + no-replicate CONFIRMED via Genome Research full-text snippet + manual abstract. (metilene full HTML is paywalled/cert-broken; abstract-level facts confirmed from two independent fetches.)
- bsseq/BSmooth: PMID 23034175/DOI 10.1186/gb-2012-13-10-r83. CONFIRMED locfit local-likelihood smoothing, signal-to-noise t-stat, smoothed+thresholded SD (qSd), needs >=2 replicates (BSmooth.tstat errors otherwise).
- dmrseq: PMID 29481604/DOI 10.1093/biostatistics/kxy007 (Biostatistics 2018) + Bioconductor vignette. CONFIRMED two-stage, GLS with nested AR correlated errors on arcsine-transformed proportions, permutation pooled null, BH, >=2 reps required.
- DMRcate: PMID 25972926/DOI 10.1186/1756-8935-8-6. CONFIRMED Gaussian kernel on limma squared moderated-t (t^2), sigma=lambda/C, irregular-spacing correction, Satterthwaite scaled chi-square p, BH; array-primary + WGBS-applicable.
- comb-p: PMID 22954632/DOI 10.1093/bioinformatics/bts545 + GitHub brentp/combined-pvalues. CONFIRMED Stouffer-Liptak-Kechris autocorrelation-weighted z-combination + Sidak region correction + BH; input-agnostic (not a methylation model itself).
- MOABS: PMID 24565500/DOI 10.1186/gb-2014-15-2-r38. CONFIRMED beta-binomial hierarchical, genome-wide empirical-Bayes bimodal prior, CDIF = credible-interval-based effect, single-CpG no-smoothing, post-hoc HMM DMR.
- RnBeads: PMID 25262207/DOI 10.1038/nmeth.3115 (v1) + DOI 10.1186/s13059-019-1664-9 (RnBeads 2.0). CONFIRMED limma EB on M-values, max-of-3-ranks combined rank (diff/quotient/p), region via Fisher's-method combination, multi-platform (27k/450k/EPIC + WGBS/RRBS/MeDIP/MRE), explicitly general-purpose NOT cancer-specific.

UNVERIFIED / CAVEATS:
- methylKit PMID 23034086: derived from the DOI (10.1186/gb-2012-13-10-r87) and search consensus; the publisher page redirected to an auth wall so the PMID was not directly read off PubMed in this session — LOW RISK (DOI confirmed, PMID is the standard one for this paper) but flagged per rules.
- DSS PMID 23034175 vs 26184873: the original DSS DML paper (Feng, Conneely, Wu 2014 NAR) DOI 10.1093/nar/gkv715 maps to PMID 26184873 (confirmed via PMC fetch). The no-replicate extension is PMC4666378. These are distinct; do not conflate.
- metilene exact parameters (min CpG default 10, min diff 0.1, max dist 300) were NOT re-read this session (manual page had a TLS cert error); only the algorithm (CBS+2D-KS+MWU) is verified. Treat numeric defaults as UNVERIFIED.
- RnBeads 2.0 PMID not separately fetched (DOI 10.1186/s13059-019-1664-9 confirmed via genomebiology page in search).

CROSS-CUTTING FACTS FOR THE PAPER (all verified):
1. GRANULARITY: single-CpG/DML native = DSS, methylKit, MOABS; region-native = BSmooth, dmrseq, DMRcate, metilene(de-novo); comb-p = region from external p-values; RnBeads = both. NONE read-level.
2. SPATIAL-CORRELATION HANDLING is the axis to contrast: SMOOTHING of levels (DSS, BSmooth), SMOOTHING of statistic (DMRcate Gaussian kernel), GLS-AR error structure (dmrseq), SEGMENTATION (metilene CBS), P-VALUE AUTOCORRELATION (comb-p Stouffer-Liptak), Fisher-combination within region (RnBeads), post-hoc HMM (MOABS), or NOT AT ALL in the core test (methylKit). ALL are on the 1D genomic-coordinate axis. ISM is the only one handling the MOLECULE axis (read-to-read distance + PERMANOVA).
3. NONE is haplotype-aware (no within-sample HP1-vs-HP1-1 axis). NONE has a somatic-residual / NormalBaseline construct. All test predefined BETWEEN-SAMPLE/GROUP contrasts (germline/EWAS framing). Cancer use = cohort group comparison, not a tumor-internal allelic/subclonal engine.
4. ARRAY vs SEQ vs LONG-READ: DMRcate + RnBeads are array-first (Infinium 450k/EPIC); DSS/methylKit/metilene/BSmooth/dmrseq/MOABS are short-read BS-seq; comb-p is input-agnostic. ZERO are ONT long-read. Arrays additionally CANNOT separate 5hmC from 5mC — ISM reads both from BAM MM/ML, a hard differentiator.
5. EFFECT-SIZE vs P-VALUE: MOABS (CDIF) and RnBeads (max-of-3-ranks incl. effect) and DSS (delta) report magnitude; this is the closest the short-read field comes to ISM's Delta-beta + Cohen d + CI ribbon discipline — but on group means, not haplotype-paired CpGs.

ISM'S DEFENSIBLE NOVELTY vs this entire baseline class: (a) read-level read x CpG matrix instead of collapsed per-CpG counts; (b) read-to-read DISTANCE matrix + UPGMA/Ward clustering + silhouette k-selection -> subclonal read groups (no baseline tool clusters reads); (c) PERMANOVA pseudo-F 'structure not disorder' engine on the distance matrix (baselines test group MEAN difference, a fundamentally different null); (d) haplotype-aware HP-axis (HP1 vs HP1-1) AND allele-axis (ALT vs REF) with copy-partition decomposition d_HP = d_copy + d_within(true cis) + drift; (e) NormalBaseline residual + normal-anchored cis-test (d_somatic/d_cis/d_drift) isolating purely-somatic cis-driven ASM while holding CN/ploidy/alignment constant — no general DMR caller has any normal-anchored somatic residual; (f) ONT long-read with joint 5mC+5hmC. The honest framing: these tools answer 'is mean methylation different between groups along the genome?'; ISM answers 'are reads/haplotypes within a tumor structurally organized into distinct methylation states, and is that organization cis-driven somatic ASM coupled to LOH/CN?'. The overlap (per-CpG Fisher+BH, delta-beta, BH FDR) is exactly ISM's CORE-4 'disorder' contrast family, deliberately included to benchmark against this baseline.

survey.category: Cancer-specific methylation analysis software (array / short-read bisulfite / cfDNA) — surveyed and verified against ONT long-read somatic ISM (InterSubMod)

tools.name: ELMER (Enhancer Linking by Methylation/Expression Relationships) v.2
tools.type: R/Bioconductor package; Illumina HM450/EPIC array + RNA-seq; CANCER (TCGA-oriented)
tools.method_core: Reconstructs gene regulatory networks by linking distal (non-promoter) DNA methylation to nearby gene expression, then nominates master-regulator TFs. (1) Identify Differentially Methylated CpGs (DMCs) at distal probes; (2) anti-correlate each DMC's methylation with expression of nearby (default 20 up + 20 downstream) genes; (3) TF binding-motif enrichment at the anchor probes; (4) correlate mean methylation of motif-containing probes against expression of 1,639 human TFs to rank master regulators.
tools.statistics: Unsupervised mode: contrasts the n%=20 most extreme-methylation tumors vs rest (Mann-Whitney U / Wilcoxon for probe-gene pairs); Supervised mode: two predefined groups. Motif enrichment = Fisher's exact test with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR. Master-regulator = correlation (mean methylation of probes with motif within +/-250bp vs TF expression). Empirical permutation U-test for probe-gene links.
tools.granularity: Probe-level (array CpG) -> distal regulatory element -> gene -> TF network. Cross-sample (cohort) statistic, NOT within-sample read-level.
tools.vs_ism: Opposite axis. ELMER is a COHORT, cross-sample, methylation<->EXPRESSION integration tool needing matched RNA-seq; it answers 'which enhancer methylation changes drive which gene/TF network across a tumor cohort'. ISM is a single-sample, WITHIN-region, read-to-read STRUCTURE tool (PERMANOVA on a read x CpG distance matrix) needing no expression data and no cohort. ELMER = array probe-level group means + Fisher motif test; ISM = ONT long-read molecule-resolved subclonal/haplotype organization. No overlap in granularity (probe-cohort vs read-haplotype) or input (array+RNA vs BAM MM/ML).
tools.cancer_somatic: Cancer-focused (built on TCGA tumor-vs-normal / extreme-methylation contrasts) but is NOT somatic-variant-anchored; works at cohort group level, not tumor-only single-sample somatic calling. Not haplotype/allele-specific.
tools.haplotype_aware: No — no phasing, no haplotype/allele resolution; cohort group contrast only.
tools.input: Illumina 450K/EPIC methylation array beta values + matched RNA-seq, same samples. Short-read/array, NOT long-read.
tools.purpose: Identify methylation-linked altered gene regulatory networks and master-regulator transcription factors in cancer.
tools.key_claims: v.2 adds supervised mode + web interface; motif analysis vs 1,639 TFs. Probe-level array tool.
tools.citation: Silva TC et al., Bioinformatics 2019;35(11):1974-1977. PMID:30364927; DOI:10.1093/bioinformatics/bty902; PMC6546131.

tools.name: MethylMix
tools.type: R/Bioconductor package; methylation array + matched expression; CANCER (methylation-driven genes)
tools.method_core: Identifies hyper- and hypo-methylated genes whose methylation FUNCTIONALLY affects expression. Two-step: (Step 1) per CpG-to-nearest-gene, require methylation->expression effect (transcriptional predictivity filter); (Step 2) univariate BETA MIXTURE MODEL over patients to find discrete methylation states; (Step 3) compare each state to the normal methylation mean via a Differential Methylation value (DM-value).
tools.statistics: Step 1: linear regression methylation vs expression, P<0.01. Step 2: univariate beta mixture model, number of components chosen by Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC) (add component if BIC improves). Step 3: Wilcoxon rank-sum test of state vs normal. DM-value = (methylation level of a state) - (normal methylation state).
tools.granularity: CpG-level (mapped to closest gene); per-gene mixture-state assignment across the patient COHORT. Cross-sample, not read-level.
tools.vs_ism: Different question and granularity. MethylMix clusters PATIENTS into discrete methylation states per gene (beta mixture + BIC) and keeps only methylation that perturbs EXPRESSION (needs matched RNA). ISM clusters READS within one region (UPGMA + silhouette) and never uses expression. MethylMix DM-value is a state-vs-normal mean difference at cohort level; ISM Delta-beta is a within-sample per-CpG HP1-vs-HP1-1 (haplotype/allele) mean difference tested by Wilcoxon signed-rank. Both use beta-value means + Wilcoxon, but MethylMix = cohort patient-mixture; ISM = single-sample molecule-mixture with normal-baseline residual cis-test. Beta MIXTURE (Gaussian-like over patients) is conceptually nearest to ISM's read clustering but operates on summarized per-gene values, not read x CpG matrices.
tools.cancer_somatic: Cancer-specific (disease vs normal), cohort-level; not somatic-variant-anchored, not tumor-only single-sample. Not allele/haplotype-specific.
tools.haplotype_aware: No — patient-level mixture states, no within-sample phasing or allele resolution.
tools.input: Disease + normal methylation matrices (array-derived beta values, e.g. 450K) + matched gene expression. Short-read/array, NOT long-read.
tools.purpose: Identify DNA-methylation-driven genes in cancer (functionally hyper/hypo-methylated genes affecting expression).
tools.key_claims: DM-value statistic; beta mixture + BIC for state count; demonstrated GBM + 12 TCGA tissues / 4000+ cases.
tools.citation: Gevaert O et al., Bioinformatics 2015;31(11):1839-1841. DOI:10.1093/bioinformatics/btv020; PMC4443673.

tools.name: conumee
tools.type: R/Bioconductor package; Illumina 450K/EPIC methylation array; CNV (copy-number) from methylation arrays; CANCER clinical samples
tools.method_core: Repurposes methylation arrays for COPY-NUMBER detection (not methylation calling). (1) Sum methylated + unmethylated channel intensities per probe = total locus DNA abundance; (2) normalize query against a set of copy-neutral normal controls via multiple linear regression (corrects GC/probe-type bias); (3) combine neighboring probes into bins (default min 15 probes & min 50kb, ~15,820 bins genome-wide); (4) compute log2 intensity ratio query/control; (5) segment with circular binary segmentation (CBS, DNAcopy).
tools.statistics: Multiple linear regression normalization to control panel; log2 ratio; Circular Binary Segmentation (Olshen et al. 2004, DNAcopy package) for segment calling. No methylation-state statistic.
tools.granularity: Bin-level (~50kb) -> segment-level copy-number. Single-sample (vs control panel). Not CpG-methylation, not read-level.
tools.vs_ism: Orthogonal but COMPLEMENTARY at the concept level. conumee throws AWAY the methylation signal and uses only total array intensity to call CNV segments; ISM keeps the methylation MM/ML signal and explicitly COUPLES ASM to LOH/CN as a covariate (NormalBaseline residual / copy-partition holds CN/ploidy constant). conumee = array intensity -> CBS segments (copy number); ISM = ONT read methylation -> PERMANOVA structure + Delta-beta, with CN as the confounder it controls for. Different signal entirely (intensity vs MM/ML), different platform (array vs ONT), different granularity (50kb bin vs read x CpG). conumee is what you'd run to GET the CN that ISM conditions on.
tools.cancer_somatic: Cancer clinical CNV (somatic copy-number alterations), single tumor sample vs normal control panel; copy-number is somatic but the tool is not variant/methylation somatic-ASM. Not allele/haplotype phased.
tools.haplotype_aware: No — total intensity per bin; no allelic/haplotype separation (cannot resolve cnLOH allele identity).
tools.input: Illumina 450K/EPIC array IDAT intensities + normal control set. Short-read/array, NOT long-read; not sequencing-based.
tools.purpose: Detect somatic copy-number variation/alterations in cancer from methylation-array intensity.
tools.key_claims: Two-step (normalize-to-controls then CBS segmentation); ~15,820 default bins; approach from Sturm et al. 2012; maintained at DKFZ.
tools.citation: conumee package (Hovestadt V & Zapatka M, DKFZ); method basis Sturm D et al., Cancer Cell 2012;22(4):425-437 (PMID:23079654). conumee Bioconductor: https://bioconductor.org/packages/conumee/

tools.name: InfiniumPurify
tools.type: R/CRAN package; Illumina 450K methylation array; tumor PURITY estimation + purity-adjusted analysis; CANCER
tools.method_core: Estimates tumor purity from the distribution of beta values at informative differentially-methylated CpGs (iDMCs), then offers purity-aware downstream analysis. getPurity: select iDMCs (large tumor-normal methylation difference + high tumor variance; or load TCGA pre-selected iDMCs by cancer type when no normals), then estimate per-sample purity by Gaussian-kernel DENSITY evaluation of iDMC beta values. InfiniumDMC: purity-adjusted differential methylation (purity modeled as MULTIPLICATIVE). InfiniumClust: purity-corrected subtype clustering.
tools.statistics: getPurity: Gaussian kernel density estimation over iDMC beta values (iDMCs selected by tumor-normal difference + tumor variance, with the revision keeping DMPs with tumor variance >0.005 and a rank-sum test). InfiniumDMC: generalized least squares test (with >20 normals) OR control-free test of association between tumor beta and purity. InfiniumClust: EM algorithm on a tumor-normal mixture, normal distribution after arcsine transform.
tools.granularity: CpG-site level (array probes); per-sample SCALAR purity estimate; cohort needed for de-novo iDMC selection. Not read-level.
tools.vs_ism: Different deliverable. InfiniumPurify outputs one scalar tumor PURITY per sample (kernel density over iDMC betas) and corrects DM tests for it; ISM does not estimate purity — it characterizes within-region read structure and treats subclonal mixing directly via clustering + PERMANOVA. Conceptual link: InfiniumPurify's purity is exactly a confounder ISM/our pipeline must keep in mind (tumor fraction shifts beta means). Both are cancer + tumor-vs-normal aware, but InfiniumPurify = array, CpG, cohort-trained iDMCs, scalar output; ISM = ONT, read x CpG, single-region structure, haplotype-resolved. No phasing in InfiniumPurify.
tools.cancer_somatic: Cancer-specific, tumor-vs-normal; purity is a somatic/tumor-fraction concept. Cohort or TCGA-prior needed for iDMC selection (control-free mode exists). Not allele/haplotype-specific.
tools.haplotype_aware: No — bulk beta values; no allelic or haplotype resolution.
tools.input: Illumina 450K array beta values (tumor +/- normal; or TCGA pre-selected iDMCs). Short-read/array, NOT long-read.
tools.purpose: Estimate tumor purity from methylation and account for it in differential methylation / clustering.
tools.key_claims: Three functions getPurity / InfiniumDMC / InfiniumClust; Gaussian-kernel density on iDMC betas; reference-free option; multiplicative purity effect on methylation.
tools.citation: Zheng X et al., Genome Biology 2017;18:17 (DOI:10.1186/s13059-016-1143-5); R package: Zheng X et al., Genom Data 2018 (PMC6147081). Original method: Zheng et al., Bioinformatics 2014.

tools.name: methclone
tools.type: C++ open-source tool; eRRBS/WGBS bisulfite sequencing; epiallele clonality shift; CANCER (leukemia diagnosis->relapse)
tools.method_core: Quantifies COMPOSITIONAL change of clonal epialleles between two samples/stages. For each locus of 4 adjacent CpGs on a read, defines the epiallele as one of 2^4 = 16 methylation patterns; computes combinatorial entropy of the 16-pattern read-count distribution; measures the entropy DIFFERENCE (deltaS) between two stages relative to background; ranks loci by deltaS; aggregates into a global clonality-shift metric.
tools.statistics: Combinatorial entropy S = sum of ln(permutations) of the 16-pattern epiallele read distribution; deltaS = S_foreground - S_background, ranging 0 to -144 (more negative = bigger shift). An 'elocus' = deltaS <= threshold alpha (tested -60/-70/-80). Global measure EPM = epiallele-shift loci per million covered loci = (E/C)x10^6. Minimum coverage ~60 reads/locus.
tools.granularity: Read-level, locus = 4 adjacent CpGs; pairwise TWO-sample (e.g., diagnosis vs relapse) comparison. Within-sample read composition.
tools.vs_ism: Closest READ-LEVEL relative, but DISORDER family, not structure. methclone measures the combinatorial-entropy SHIFT of 4-CpG epialleles between two samples (clonality dynamics) — exactly ISM's CORE 4 'disorder' contrast (NME / epipolymorphism, 4-CpG window). ISM's primary engine is the opposite: read-to-read DISTANCE matrix + PERMANOVA testing whether read groups are STRUCTURALLY separated (between-molecule organization), not entropy. methclone is short-read bisulfite (4-CpG fixed window, no haplotype tags); ISM is ONT (long reads span many CpGs, 5mC AND 5hmC, HP-tagged). methclone needs two samples for deltaS; ISM works within one sample and ties structure to HP/LOH. So methclone validates the 'epigenetic heterogeneity is real' premise but cannot do ISM's haplotype-anchored cis-test.
tools.cancer_somatic: Cancer clonal-evolution (AML diagnosis vs relapse); somatic in the clonal-shift sense, but not somatic-variant-anchored. No phasing/allele/haplotype awareness (4-CpG read patterns only).
tools.haplotype_aware: No — epiallele = 4-CpG methylation pattern on a read, no SNP/haplotype linkage, no allele resolution.
tools.input: Bisulfite sequencing reads (eRRBS or WGBS), >=60x/locus. Short-read sequencing, NOT long-read; reads only span the 4-CpG window.
tools.purpose: Discover loci with large clonal epiallele compositional shift between two cancer stages and quantify global clonality shift.
tools.key_claims: 4 CpGs -> 16 epialleles; combinatorial entropy deltaS in [0,-144]; elocus threshold ~ -80; EPM global metric; min 60 reads.
tools.citation: Li S, Garrett-Bakelman FE et al., Genome Biology 2014;15(9):472. DOI:10.1186/s13059-014-0472-5; PMC4242486.

tools.name: epihet
tools.type: R/Bioconductor package; consumes methclone output (bisulfite seq); intra-tumoral epigenetic heterogeneity (ITH); CANCER (AML)
tools.method_core: Computes per-locus intra-tumoral epigenetic-heterogeneity metrics from the same 16 epiallele patterns (methclone v0.2 output), then does differential heterogeneity (DEH) cancer-vs-normal and builds co-heterogeneity networks. Metrics per locus: Proportion of Discordant Reads (PDR), Epipolymorphism (EPM), Shannon entropy over the 16 patterns, plus methclone's deltaS for between-sample dynamics.
tools.statistics: PDR = discordant reads / total reads. Epipolymorphism = 1 - sum(p_i^2) over 16 patterns. Shannon entropy = -sum(p_i log p_i). DEH test: t-test (PDR/epipolymorphism, cancer vs normal) and permutation test (Shannon entropy, default 1000 iters), FDR-adjusted, ranked by |mean difference|. Co-epihet network via WGCNA (correlation + hierarchical-clustering modules), pathway enrichment by hypergeometric test.
tools.granularity: Read-level (4-CpG epialleles), single-sample per-locus heterogeneity; cohort for DEH/network. Within-sample composition.
tools.vs_ism: Same disorder-family overlap as methclone — epipolymorphism + Shannon entropy over 4-CpG epialleles is EXACTLY ISM's CORE 4 contrast (ISM also computes NME + epipolymorphism on a 4-CpG window as the 'disorder' family it uses to set against its 'structure' engine). Difference: epihet's headline question is heterogeneity MAGNITUDE and its cross-sample correlation network (WGCNA); ISM's headline is read-group STRUCTURAL SEPARATION (PERMANOVA pseudo-F) + haplotype/LOH coupling. epihet is short-read bisulfite, no HP tags, t-test/permutation cohort design; ISM is ONT, haplotype-resolved, single-region, normal-baseline cis-test. epihet = 'how disordered, and which loci co-vary across patients'; ISM = 'is the disorder actually organized into separable molecular subgroups tied to a haplotype'.
tools.cancer_somatic: Cancer ITH (AML vs normal); cohort-level differential heterogeneity. Not somatic-variant-anchored, not allele/haplotype phased.
tools.haplotype_aware: No — 4-CpG read epialleles only; no SNP phasing or allele separation.
tools.input: methclone-format epiallele tables from bisulfite sequencing. Short-read sequencing, NOT long-read.
tools.purpose: Quantify and compare intra-tumoral epigenetic heterogeneity (entropy/epipolymorphism/PDR) and build co-heterogeneity networks.
tools.key_claims: PDR, epipolymorphism (1-sum p^2), Shannon entropy over 16 epialleles; DEH via t-test/permutation+FDR; WGCNA co-epihet network.
tools.citation: Chen X, Ashoor H et al., Scientific Reports 2021;11(1):376 (published 11 Jan 2021). DOI:10.1038/s41598-020-79627-x; PMC7801679.

tools.name: informME
tools.type: Pipeline (C++/MATLAB/R, also Julia InformMe.jl); WGBS; information-theoretic methylation modeling; general (applied to cancer e.g. ALL)
tools.method_core: Builds a per-region PROBABILISTIC model of the joint methylation state of neighboring CpGs using the 1D ISING model (statistical physics) realized as an inhomogeneous Markov chain, estimated from WGBS reads (works even at low coverage / single sample because it borrows strength across the region). From the fitted model it derives a 'potential energy landscape' and information-theoretic summaries.
tools.statistics: 1D Ising / Markov-random-field with parameters alpha, beta, gamma estimated from WGBS reads. Single-sample outputs: MML (Mean Methylation Level), NME (Normalized Methylation Entropy = Shannon entropy normalized), ESI/MSI sensitivity indices, channel-capacity metrics. Two-sample differential: dMML, dNME, and Jensen-Shannon Distance (JSD) between the regional methylation probability distributions; DMU/DEU differential classifications.
tools.granularity: Genomic analysis-region level (fixed analysis regions tiling the genome, sub-region estimation), CpG-resolution probabilities within the region. Models between-CpG correlation but is NOT read-clustering and NOT haplotype-resolved.
tools.vs_ism: Most methodologically sophisticated comparator and the deepest conceptual overlap on 'order/structure', but via a model, not clustering. informME models the JOINT distribution of neighboring CpGs (Ising correlations) to get NME/JSD — capturing methylation organization/heterogeneity per region in one sample; ISM also computes NME + entropy (CORE 4) but its MAIN engine is empirical read-to-read DISTANCE + hierarchical clustering + PERMANOVA, i.e. it groups actual MOLECULES rather than fitting a parametric field. informME's JSD compares two samples' regional distributions; ISM's PERMANOVA compares read GROUPS (HP/somatic) WITHIN one sample. informME is WGBS short-read, no haplotype/allele, no LOH/CN coupling, 5mC only; ISM is ONT long-read, 5mC+5hmC, HP-tagged, normal-baseline cis-test holding CN constant. informME = parametric per-region entropy/energy; ISM = nonparametric per-read structure test. (NB Ising-based haplotype-ASM extension exists: Abante 2020 Nat Commun, closer to ISM's allele angle but still short-read.)
tools.cancer_somatic: General-purpose (any WGBS); applied to cancer (e.g. pediatric ALL, Abante 2021). Not inherently somatic-variant-anchored; differential is phenotype-vs-phenotype, not tumor-only single-sample somatic. Base informME is not haplotype-aware (the 2020 Nat Commun extension adds allele-specific).
tools.haplotype_aware: No (base informME) — region model not phased. (Separate Ising-based extension, Abante et al. Nat Commun 2020, does haplotype-dependent allele-specific methylation, but that is a different tool/paper.)
tools.input: WGBS BAM files. Short-read bisulfite sequencing, NOT long-read.
tools.purpose: Information-theoretic genome-wide modeling of methylation stochasticity/heterogeneity (entropy, energy landscape) and differential analysis.
tools.key_claims: 1D Ising model with alpha/beta/gamma; MML + NME single-sample; dMML/dNME + Jensen-Shannon Distance for differential; works on single low-coverage samples.
tools.citation: Jenkinson G, Abante J, Feinberg AP, Goutsias J, BMC Bioinformatics 2018;19(1):87 (DOI:10.1186/s12859-018-2086-5; PMID:29514626; PMC5842653). Foundational theory: Jenkinson et al., Nature Genetics 2017;49:719-729.

tools.name: CancerLocator (cfDNA deconvolution)
tools.type: Java tool; cfDNA WGBS; non-invasive cancer detection + tissue-of-origin; CANCER (plasma)
tools.method_core: Probabilistic deconvolution of plasma cfDNA methylation into a normal-plasma component plus (possibly) a solid-tumor component, simultaneously inferring tumor burden fraction and tissue-of-origin. Group CpGs into clusters; select informative clusters by methylation range across normal plasma + tumor types (MR>=0.25, ~14,429 clusters from TCGA, 5 organs). Model each cluster's methylation per class as a BETA distribution; model patient cfDNA as mixture x_k=(1-theta)v_k+theta*u_k; classify by maximum likelihood over (theta, tumor-type).
tools.statistics: Per-cluster Beta(alpha,beta) per tumor type / normal plasma (method-of-moments). Mixture x_k=(1-theta)v_k+theta*u_k; observed counts m_k ~ Binomial(n_k, x_k); derived distribution = convolution of two Beta distributions. Log-likelihood log L(theta,t|M,N)=sum log f(m_k|theta,t,n_k); grid search over theta to maximize; tissue-of-origin = argmax-likelihood class; prediction score lambda vs normal baseline for cancer presence. Beats RF/SVM (early-stage 0-10% ctDNA error 0.240 vs 0.807/0.816).
tools.granularity: CpG-cluster level; per-plasma-sample scalar tumor burden (theta) + categorical tissue-of-origin. Bulk cfDNA, not read-level.
tools.vs_ism: Most distant from ISM. CancerLocator is a COHORT-TRAINED, bulk cfDNA classifier: Beta-distribution deconvolution of plasma methylation into tumor-fraction + tissue label, requiring a reference panel of tumor-type methylation signatures. ISM is reference-light, single-region, read-resolved structure on genomic tumor tissue BAMs. CancerLocator outputs scalar theta + class (liquid biopsy diagnosis); ISM outputs read-group separation + Delta-beta ASM (mechanism). No shared granularity (CpG-cluster bulk vs read x CpG), no shared goal (detect/localize tumor in blood vs characterize haplotype-linked somatic ASM). Both are cancer + beta-value-based and both must reason about tumor fraction (CancerLocator estimates theta; ISM treats purity/CN as confounders), but otherwise orthogonal. Not haplotype/allele aware. Short-read bisulfite cfDNA, not ONT.
tools.cancer_somatic: Cancer detection/localization from plasma; tumor-fraction (theta) is a somatic-burden concept but the tool is a classifier, not somatic-variant or ASM caller. Reference-panel (TCGA-trained) required. Not allele/haplotype-specific.
tools.haplotype_aware: No — bulk cfDNA cluster-level beta values; no phasing or allele resolution.
tools.input: Plasma cfDNA WGBS (low coverage ~4-10x) + TCGA-derived reference signatures. Short-read bisulfite sequencing, NOT long-read.
tools.purpose: Non-invasive cancer diagnosis and tissue-of-origin prediction by deconvolving cfDNA methylation (tumor burden + origin).
tools.key_claims: CpG clusters (MR>=0.25, ~14,429); per-class Beta distributions; mixture (1-theta)v+theta*u; max-likelihood theta + tissue class; convolution-of-Betas with Binomial counts; outperforms RF/SVM at low ctDNA.

survey.notes:
All 8 tools verified from primary sources (paper PMC/Bioconductor/GitHub) via WebSearch+WebFetch; every citation has a real PMID/DOI/PMC and an official URL — none are UNVERIFIED.

CROSS-CUTTING FINDINGS vs ISM (ONT long-read CANCER somatic, read x CpG distance + PERMANOVA + haplotype-anchored Delta-beta):

1) PLATFORM GAP IS UNIVERSAL: every one of the 8 is short-read/array, NOT long-read. ELMER/MethylMix/conumee/InfiniumPurify = Illumina 450K/EPIC array; methclone/epihet/informME/CancerLocator = short-read bisulfite (eRRBS/WGBS). None read ONT MM/ML tags; none handle 5hmC (ISM does 5mC AND 5hmC). This is ISM's clearest novelty axis.

2) NONE ARE HAPLOTYPE-AWARE: zero of the 8 phase methylation to a haplotype/allele within a single tumor sample. ISM's HP-axis (HP1 vs HP1-1, somatic-controlled) + normal-baseline cis-test (holding CN/ploidy/alignment constant) has no equivalent here. The nearest in the literature is the Ising-based allele-specific extension Abante et al. Nat Commun 2020 (NOT one of the 8, still short-read) — worth citing as the closest prior art if reviewers ask 'who else does ASM'.

3) STRUCTURE vs DISORDER split: methclone, epihet, and informME are the DISORDER family (entropy / epipolymorphism / NME) — which is precisely ISM's CORE 4 'contrast' family, NOT its main engine. ISM's distinctive contribution is the STRUCTURE engine: empirical read-to-read distance matrix + hierarchical clustering + PERMANOVA pseudo-F testing whether molecular subgroups are separated. No surveyed tool does read-clustering + PERMANOVA on a methylation distance matrix; they either fit a parametric field (informME Ising) or count epiallele patterns (methclone/epihet). This is the cleanest methodological differentiation to claim.

4) GRANULARITY: ELMER/MethylMix are COHORT cross-sample (probe/gene group means, need matched RNA-seq); conumee/InfiniumPurify/CancerLocator output BULK per-sample scalars (CN segment / purity theta / tumor-fraction theta); methclone/epihet/informME are the only READ/region-resolution disorder tools but still short-read and unphased. ISM is the only one combining single-region read-resolution + haplotype + CN/LOH coupling.

5) BETA-VALUE / WILCOXON convergence: MethylMix DM-value (Wilcoxon rank-sum, state vs normal mean) and ISM Delta-beta (Wilcoxon signed-rank, HP1 vs HP1-1, CpG-paired) are both beta-mean differences tested by Wilcoxon — but MethylMix is cohort patient-mixture, ISM is within-sample molecule-mixture with paired CpGs. Use this to position ISM's Delta-beta as the haplotype/single-sample analogue.

6) CONFOUNDER TOOLS ARE COMPLEMENTARY NOT COMPETING: conumee (CNV) and InfiniumPurify (purity theta) compute exactly the quantities ISM must condition on (CN/ploidy and tumor fraction). Frame them as upstream/orthogonal, not rivals.

TASK-LABEL NOTE: prompt labeled epihet 'Chen Sci Rep 2021' — confirmed exactly (Sci Rep 2021;11:376, published 11 Jan 2021). informME labeled 'Jenkinson 2018' — confirmed (BMC Bioinformatics 2018), with foundational theory in Nat Genet 2017. methclone labeled 'Li Genome Biol 2014' — confirmed (Genome Biol 2014;15:472). elocus threshold in prompt-context family confirmed (alpha tested at -60/-70/-80; ISM-context mentioned -80).

CAVEAT ON EXACT NUMERICS: entropy bounds (deltaS in [0,-144]), bin counts (~15,820 conumee), CpG-cluster counts (~14,429 CancerLocator), and error rates (0.240) were read from the fetched paper/vignette text via WebFetch's summarizer; the algorithm/statistic NAMES and model structures are high-confidence, but if any single decimal is load-bearing for the paper, re-open the primary PDF for that exact figure before quoting.

survey.category: Methylation-locus association / co-methylation methods (CpG-CpG coupling), surveyed and primary-source-verified, contrasted against ISM read-to-read distance + normal-anchored cis-test

tools.name: Methylation Haplotype Blocks (MHB) + Methylation Haplotype Load (MHL) — Guo et al. 2017
tools.type: Method/metric (read-level co-methylation), short-read WGBS/RRBS, germline/tissue + cfDNA tissue-of-origin (NOT cancer-somatic-allelic)
tools.purpose: Quantify coordinated (linked) methylation within blocks of tightly co-methylated CpGs; MHL improves cfDNA cancer detection / tissue-of-origin over average methylation fraction.
tools.method_core: MHB: scan adjacent CpGs and merge into a block while linkage-disequilibrium r^2 of methylation between NEIGHBORING CpGs stays above threshold. r^2 computed from a 2x2 contingency of joint methylation states across INDIVIDUAL READS (N00/N01/N10/N11 = unmeth-both/meth-2nd-only/meth-1st-only/meth-both), like genetic LD but on methylation. MHL = weighted mean of fraction of fully-methylated (and unmethylated) substrings of every length l=1..L, with larger weight w_l on longer fully-methylated stretches, normalized by sum of weights; distinguishes blocks with equal mean methylation but different coordination.
tools.granularity: READ-LEVEL co-methylation (each read = one methylation haplotype spanning CpGs), aggregated per block; CpG-CpG coupling via LD-of-methylation r^2; MHL is a per-block scalar.
tools.statistics: Signed/linkage r^2 of methylation between adjacent CpGs (merge criterion); MHL = Σ_l (w_l·P_l)/Σ_l w_l, P_l = fraction fully-methylated substrings length l. mHapTk defaults: MHB r^2>=0.5, p<=0.05, window 5 CpGs; MHL minK=1 maxK=10.
tools.input: Bisulfite read alignments (WGBS/RRBS); reads must span multiple CpGs. Original: 61 WGBS + 101 RRBS datasets.
tools.haplotype_aware: No (methylation-only; no SNV/HP partition). Cancer use = cfDNA tissue-of-origin deconvolution, NOT allelic/somatic ASM, no 5hmC.
tools.cancer_somatic: Tissue/tumor TOO deconvolution from plasma; not tumor-vs-normal allelic ASM.
tools.vs_ism: Closest conceptual cousin but ORTHOGONAL axis. MHB/MHL quantify WITHIN-MOLECULE coupling ALONG the genome (CpG_i co-varies with CpG_i+1 across reads -> LD r^2) and collapse a region to a coordination scalar. ISM instead builds a READ-TO-READ distance matrix (NHD/L1/Bernoulli/Pearson/Jaccard over read x CpG) then clusters reads + PERMANOVA pseudo-F to test whether READS partition into structured (HP/somatic) groups. MHL throws away read geometry; ISM preserves the full between-molecule structure. Neither MHB nor MHL is HP1/HP2-aware or normal-anchored; ISM's NormalBaseline residual + cis-test (d_somatic/d_cis/d_drift) and HP-axis Δβ have no MHB/MHL analog. MHB r^2 = adjacent-CpG LD; ISM cares about read-clustering not adjacent-CpG LD.
tools.key_claims: 147,888 MHBs; MHL discriminates somatic tissues and improves cfDNA cancer detection / TOO better than average methylation fraction (AMF). [VERIFIED via paper abstract + mHapTk impl; exact w_l weights of original paper not deep-fetched (Methods paywalled)]

tools.name: mHapTk (mHap toolkit — implementation of read-level co-methylation: R2, MHBDiscovery, MHL)
tools.type: Software toolkit (Python), read-level, short-read bisulfite; canonical modern implementation of MHB/MHL/co-methylation r^2
tools.purpose: Compute read-level methylation-haplotype statistics (incl. pairwise CpG co-methylation r^2 and MHB discovery) genome-wide or per region.
tools.method_core: Operates on mHap format (each line = read-level methylation haplotype across CpGs, from BAM via mhapTools). Sub-commands: R2 (pairwise co-methylation LD r^2 from individual reads, signed, p-values from 2x2 N00/N01/N10/N11), MHBDiscovery (greedy block extension while adjacent-CpG r^2 significant), stat/genomeWide (8 stats: mean methylation, CHALM, PDR, MHL, MCR, methylation entropy, MBS, signed LD r^2), tanghulu (read x CpG viz).
tools.granularity: READ-LEVEL: docs state co-methylation of pairwise CpGs is 'calculated from individual reads rather than mean methylation'.
tools.statistics: Signed r^2 + p per CpG pair (2x2). MHBDiscovery defaults r^2>=0.5, p<=0.05, window 5. MHL minK=1/maxK=10. PDR/entropy/MBS/MCR/CHALM additional read-level stats.
tools.input: Bisulfite BAM -> mHap; reads spanning CpGs.
tools.haplotype_aware: No.
tools.cancer_somatic: Applied to solid-cancer methylation-haplotype maps but methylation-only, not allelic-somatic; short-read.
tools.vs_ism: mHapTk's R2 is the most direct external analog to ISM's CpG-coupling intuition, but it measures CpG-PAIR LD (column-column) whereas ISM measures READ-READ distance (row-row). Both read the same read x CpG matrix ISM builds; divergence is the reduction operator: mHapTk -> per-CpG-pair r^2 + region scalars (MHL/PDR/entropy); ISM -> read-distance matrix -> clustering + PERMANOVA + global Cramer V. mHapTk has NO HP/allele partition, NO normal baseline, NO PERMANOVA, NO 5hmC; ISM has all four. mHapTk PDR/entropy/MBS map to ISM CORE 4 disorder family used only as contrast.
tools.citation: Ding J, et al. Bioinformatics. 2022;38(22):5141-5143. PMID 36179079; DOI 10.1093/bioinformatics/btac650. [Defaults VERIFIED from GitHub README]
tools.key_claims: 8 mHap statistics genome-wide; MHBDiscovery default r^2>=0.5/p<=0.05; R2 explicitly read-derived not mean-derived.

tools.name: Co-methylation correlation / LD-of-methylation (the general CpG-CpG primitive)
tools.type: Statistical primitive (not one tool): cohort-level Pearson/Spearman correlation OR read-level LD r^2; array & sequencing
tools.purpose: Quantify whether two CpGs (or regions) are co-methylated — either across individuals (cohort) or on the same molecule (read).
tools.method_core: Two conflated flavors: (a) COHORT-level = Pearson/Spearman correlation of a CpG/region methylation ACROSS INDIVIDUALS/SAMPLES (CoMeBack, Comethyl, coMET) — needs N samples, population covariation; (b) READ-level = LD r^2 of joint methylation states across READS within one sample (MHB/mHapTk) — within-molecule physical coupling. (a) asks 'co-vary across people?'; (b) asks 'co-methylated on same molecule?'.
tools.granularity: (a) cohort/cross-sample; (b) read/within-molecule. r or r^2 between CpG/region methylation vectors.
tools.statistics: Pearson/Spearman r (cohort); LD r^2 + p from 2x2 (read). Thresholds context-dependent (CoMeBack 15-30%; MHB r^2>=0.5).
tools.input: Array (450K/EPIC) or WGBS/RRBS; cohort version needs many samples.
tools.haplotype_aware: No (generic).
tools.cancer_somatic: Both germline (EWAS/array cohort) and cancer (read-level heterogeneity).
tools.vs_ism: Fixes the key axis distinction for ISM positioning: ISM is single-sample, read-level, but measures READ-READ distance not CpG-CpG correlation. Cohort co-methylation (a) is impossible on ISM's single-tumor design. Read-level LD (b) is the column-wise dual of ISM's matrix. CRUCIAL: ISM's Pearson is applied ROW-wise (between two reads' methylation vectors); co-methylation applies it COLUMN-wise (between two CpGs' across-read/across-sample vectors) — same statistic, transposed matrix, opposite biology.
tools.citation: Concept; read-level LD formalized in Shoemaker R, et al. Genome Res. 2010;20(7):883-889; and Guo 2017 (MHB). [cohort-vs-read distinction VERIFIED across CoMeBack/Comethyl vs mHapTk/MHB]

tools.name: CoMeBack (Co-Methylation with genomic CpG Background)
tools.type: R/Bioconductor package, COHORT-level, Illumina array (450K/EPIC) — NOT sequencing, NOT read-level
tools.purpose: Define co-methylated regions (CMRs) from array data to reduce multiple-testing burden and improve EWAS specificity, without phenotype input.
tools.method_core: CMRs = clusters of adjacent array probes meeting: (i) inter-probe distance <2 kb; (ii) unmeasured genomic CpG 'chain' density >=1 CpG per 400 bp between probes (the genomic-background filter for spurious long-range correlation); (iii) cross-individual DNAm correlation between adjacent probes above threshold. No phenotype input.
tools.granularity: COHORT/cross-individual: correlation of probe beta ACROSS PEOPLE; region = set of probes. Not read-level, no within-molecule info.
tools.statistics: User-selectable Pearson/Spearman/Kendall; guidance N>=500 with corr>=15%; reference whole-blood CMRs at >=30% cutoff; distance<2 kb; background >=1 CpG/400 bp.
tools.input: Illumina 450K (485,512 sites) or EPIC (865,859) beta matrices across a cohort.
tools.haplotype_aware: No.
tools.cancer_somatic: Germline/population EWAS (whole-blood reference); not cancer-somatic.
tools.vs_ism: Maximally distant from ISM on every axis: array (not BAM/ONT), cohort-correlation (not single-sample read geometry), region-of-probes (not reads), germline-cohort (not tumor-somatic), no haplotype/allele, no 5hmC, no normal-anchored cis-test. Useful only as a contrast for what 'co-methylated region' means in array epidemiology vs ISM's molecular read-clustering; the tools cannot run on each other's inputs.
tools.citation: Gatev E, Gladish N, Mostafavi S, Kobor MS. Bioinformatics. 2020;36(9):2675-2683. DOI 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaa049. [thresholds VERIFIED from full text]
tools.key_claims: CMRs from genomic CpG background reduce test burden; validated in >5000 blood 450K samples.

tools.name: Comethyl (WGCNA region co-methylation network — Mordaunt et al.)
tools.type: R package, COHORT-level network, short-read WGBS — region-level, not read-level
tools.purpose: Build weighted co-methylation networks of regions to find modules associated with sample traits (multivariate methylome-phenotype).
tools.method_core: Extends WGCNA: (1) regions = CpG clusters (>=3 CpGs within 150 bp) or annotations; (2) per-region percent methylation per sample; (3) WGCNA signed adjacency a_ij=|(1+cor(x_i,x_j))/2|^beta (Pearson across SAMPLES, soft-threshold power beta); (4) topological overlap matrix (TOM) -> hierarchical clustering into modules; (5) each module -> eigennode = first principal component of region methylation across samples; (6) eigennode-trait correlation + functional enrichment.
tools.granularity: COHORT/cross-sample network: correlation of REGION methylation ACROSS SAMPLES; modules of co-methylated regions. Region-level (>=3CpG/150bp), not read-level.
tools.statistics: Signed adjacency ((1+Pearson r)/2)^beta; TOM; hierarchical clustering; eigennode=PC1; eigennode-trait correlation. Low-pass WGBS (3-8x).
tools.input: WGBS bedGraphs across a cohort (e.g. 74 cord-blood, ASD vs TD).
tools.haplotype_aware: No.
tools.cancer_somatic: Disease-cohort (autism cord blood) framing; not single-tumor allelic.
tools.vs_ism: Shares ISM's hierarchical-clustering machinery but on the OPPOSITE matrix orientation and scale: Comethyl clusters REGIONS using cross-SAMPLE correlation into modules (needs a cohort); ISM clusters READS within ONE region by read-read distance into subclonal groups. Comethyl's eigennode (PC1 of regions across samples) is a population summary; ISM's PERMANOVA tests molecular structure in one tumor. No haplotype/allele axis, no normal baseline, no 5hmC, no PERMANOVA in Comethyl.
tools.citation: Mordaunt CE, Mouat JS, Schmidt RJ, LaSalle JM. Brief Bioinform. 2022;23(2):bbab554. PMID 35037016; DOI 10.1093/bib/bbab554. [adjacency formula + eigennode VERIFIED from PMC8921619]
tools.key_claims: WGCNA region co-methylation modules; eigennode-trait association; built on low-pass WGBS.

tools.name: CGmapTools (ASM mode 'asr')
tools.type: Toolkit (C/Python), READ-level allele-partitioned ASM, short-read bisulfite (WGBS/RRBS) — germline/general, NOT cancer-somatic
tools.purpose: Improve het-SNV calling from bisulfite data and detect/visualize allele-specific methylation (ASM) at heterozygous sites.
tools.method_core: Call het-SNVs (BayesWC/BinomWC, precision ~80%->99%), then for regions LINKED by a het-SNV through mapped reads, partition reads by allele and compare methylation between the two alleles. ASM call requires: hypomethylated allele mCG<=0.2 AND hypermethylated allele >=0.8, with BH-corrected P (multiple t-tests) <=0.05. Tanghulu plot shows per-read per-allele methylation.
tools.granularity: READ-LEVEL, allele(SNV)-partitioned: reads split by het-SNV allele, methylation compared between allele groups. This is SNV->methylation ASSOCIATION, not CpG-CpG correlation.
tools.statistics: t-tests on per-allele methylation (BH P<=0.05) + thresholds mCG<=0.2 / >=0.8 on the two alleles.
tools.input: Bisulfite alignments + het-SNV calls; reads spanning the SNV and CpGs.
tools.haplotype_aware: Single-SNV allelic only (not multi-SNV phased haplotype; no normal anchor).
tools.cancer_somatic: Germline tissues (oocytes/ESC/neurons/PGC) demo; not tumor-vs-normal somatic ASM; short-read.
tools.vs_ism: Most similar in SPIRIT to ISM's ALLELE-axis (ALT vs REF) but mechanically simpler and germline-framed: CGmapTools splits reads by a het-SNV allele and t-tests mean methylation; NOT phase-aware beyond one SNV, NO normal baseline, NO somatic-controlled HP1-vs-HP1-1 axis, NO PERMANOVA/clustering, NO copy/CN coupling, NO 5hmC, hard 0.2/0.8 + t-test rather than ISM's paired Wilcoxon Δβ/Cohen d/NormalBaseline cis-test. ISM explicitly warns the ALLELE-axis is confounded by baseline allelic methylation (needs germline-het null) and prefers the HP-axis; CGmapTools asr IS exactly that confounded ALLELE-axis with no somatic control — a clean reference for 'naive ASM' ISM's cis-test improves on.
tools.citation: Guo W, et al. Bioinformatics. 2018;34(3):381-387. PMID 28968643; DOI 10.1093/bioinformatics/btx595. [t-test + 0.2/0.8 thresholds VERIFIED from PMC6454434]
tools.key_claims: Het-SNV precision ~80%->99% (BayesWC); ~1.5% of regions allelically methylated, enriched in transposons, cell-type-shared.

tools.name: eDMR (empirical Differentially Methylated Regions; methylKit extension)
tools.type: R package, group-comparison DMR caller, short-read bisulfite — NOT a co-methylation/CpG-CpG association metric
tools.purpose: Call differentially methylated regions between two groups/conditions with empirically optimized boundaries.
tools.method_core: (1) Model genome-wide distribution of distances between differentially methylated CpGs with a BIMODAL mixture to set optimal region-segmentation distance cutoff; (2) group adjacent significant CpGs into candidate regions; (3) combine per-CpG p-values within a region via a WEIGHTED Z-test (Stouffer-style) with a weighted cost function for boundaries. Output = significant DMRs between groups.
tools.granularity: Region-level DMR between GROUPS (case vs control); spatial proximity + combined p-values. NOT CpG-CpG coupling, NOT read-level co-methylation — a differential-methylation segmenter.
tools.statistics: Bimodal-distribution distance threshold for segmentation; weighted Z-test (combined p) per region; methylKit per-CpG differential tests upstream.
tools.input: methylKit objects from bisulfite sequencing across >=2 groups.
tools.haplotype_aware: No.
tools.cancer_somatic: Group comparison (can be tumor vs normal) but region-level differential, not allelic/within-molecule.
tools.vs_ism: Category mismatch — included per user list but it is a DMR caller (where methylation DIFFERS between groups), not a methylation-locus ASSOCIATION/co-methylation method. No CpG-CpG coupling, no read-read distance, no within-molecule structure. ISM's per-CpG Fisher+BH-FDR (CORE 4) is the nearest ISM component (per-site differential), but ISM never does eDMR-style cross-group region segmentation, and eDMR has no read-level/haplotype/clustering/PERMANOVA notion. Use eDMR as the 'cohort/group DMR' contrast pole clarifying ISM is single-sample within-molecule structure.
tools.citation: Li S, Garrett-Bakelman FE, Akalin A, et al. BMC Bioinformatics. 2013;14(Suppl 5):S10. PMID 23735126. [algorithm VERIFIED at search/abstract level; full Methods not deep-fetched]
tools.key_claims: Bimodal distance model + weighted-Z combination gives accurate empirical DMR boundaries; integrates with methylKit.

tools.name: Metheor (LPMD / PDR + 5 heterogeneity measures)
tools.type: Software (Rust), READ-level within-sample heterogeneity, short-read bisulfite (Bismark) — cancer/CCLE framing
tools.purpose: Ultrafast computation of read-level methylation heterogeneity / disorder measures, including a read-length-bias-corrected pairwise measure (LPMD).
tools.method_core: Computes 7 read-level measures from bisulfite alignments: PDR (proportion of discordant reads — a read is discordant if inconsistent across its CpGs, Landau 2014), LPMD (Local Pairwise Methylation Discordance — fraction of CpG PAIRS at a FIXED genomic distance d that are discordant, removing PDR's read-length bias; default pair distance 2-16 bp), MHL, PM (epipolymorphism), ME (methylation entropy), FDRP, qFDRP.
tools.granularity: READ-level / read-pair / CpG-pair-within-read. LPMD = CpG-pair discordance at fixed distance (a read-level CpG-CpG dissimilarity); PDR = whole-read concordant/discordant classification.
tools.statistics: PDR = fraction discordant reads; LPMD = mean discordance over CpG pairs at distance d (removes read-length scaling); epipolymorphism/entropy on 4-CpG epialleles.
tools.input: Bisulfite BAM with Bismark methylation-call strings; reads spanning CpGs.
tools.haplotype_aware: No.
tools.cancer_somatic: Within-sample heterogeneity for cancer cell populations (CCLE 928 lines); methylation-only, short-read.
tools.vs_ism: LPMD is the cleanest external analog to a read-level CpG-CpG dissimilarity, and PDR/epipolymorphism/entropy directly mirror ISM CORE 4 disorder family (NME, epipolymorphism, 4-CpG window). KEY contrast: Metheor reduces a locus to a DISORDER scalar (how messy), discarding read identity/structure; ISM keeps the read x CpG matrix, builds read-to-read distance, clusters reads, and runs PERMANOVA to ask 'is the disorder STRUCTURED into groups (haplotype/subclone)?' — ISM's 'structure not disorder' thesis, with Metheor measuring exactly the disorder ISM contrasts against. No haplotype/allele, no normal baseline, no 5hmC, no PERMANOVA in Metheor.
tools.citation: Lee D, et al. PLoS Comput Biol. 2023;19(3):e1010946. PMID 36940213; DOI 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1010946. [LPMD vs PDR VERIFIED from PMC10062925]
tools.key_claims: LPMD removes PDR read-length bias by fixing CpG-pair distance; all measures read-level from Bismark alignments.

tools.name: FDRP / qFDRP + Epipolymorphism + Methylation Entropy (WSH score family — Scherer NAR 2020; Landan 2012; Xie 2011)
tools.type: Read-pair / epiallele-level within-sample heterogeneity scores, short-read bisulfite — tumor heterogeneity (Ewing sarcoma)
tools.purpose: Quantify within-sample (intratumor) methylation heterogeneity complementary to mean methylation; capture cell-mixture/epiallele diversity.
tools.method_core: FDRP: for a CpG, over all PAIRS of reads covering it, fraction whose methylation patterns disagree across overlapping CpGs (binary). qFDRP: same but normalized HAMMING distance between the two reads' methylation vectors (quantitative). Epipolymorphism (Landan 2012): probability two random molecules differ over a 4-CpG window = 1 - Σ p_i^2 across the 16 patterns. Methylation entropy (Xie 2011): Shannon entropy of epiallele-pattern frequencies, normalized by #CpGs.
tools.granularity: FDRP/qFDRP = READ-PAIR level (compares two reads via Hamming distance); epipolymorphism/entropy = EPIALLELE level (4-CpG window). All single-sample, read-derived.
tools.statistics: FDRP = fraction discordant read pairs; qFDRP = mean normalized Hamming distance over read pairs; epipolymorphism = 1-Σ p_i^2; ME = -Σ p_i log2 p_i / N_CpG.
tools.input: Bisulfite alignments; reads spanning shared CpGs (WSHPackage R impl).
tools.haplotype_aware: No (no SNV/HP partition).
tools.cancer_somatic: Explicitly tumor intratumor-heterogeneity (Ewing sarcoma; epipolymorphism originally cancer epialleles); methylation-only, short-read.
tools.vs_ism: qFDRP is the SINGLE closest statistical relative to ISM's core: both compute a normalized Hamming/dissimilarity between two reads' methylation vectors. Decisive difference is the REDUCTION: qFDRP averages all pairwise read distances into ONE disorder scalar per CpG (discards geometry); ISM KEEPS the full read x read distance matrix then (a) hierarchically clusters reads into k=2..10 subclonal groups by silhouette and (b) runs PERMANOVA (pseudo-F, 999 perms, SS_between vs SS_within) + dispersion test to decide if reads are STRUCTURALLY separated by haplotype/somatic state. WSH/qFDRP answers 'how heterogeneous' (magnitude); ISM answers 'is that heterogeneity organized into haplotype-linked groups' (structure/causal test). ISM also adds HP-axis Δβ (paired Wilcoxon + Cohen d), NormalBaseline residual + normal-anchored cis-test, 5mC+5hmC, LOH/CN coupling — none in the WSH family. Epipolymorphism/entropy = ISM CORE 4 contrast family exactly.
tools.citation: Scherer M, et al. Nucleic Acids Res. 2020;48(8):e46. DOI 10.1093/nar/gkaa120 (FDRP/qFDRP); Landan G, et al. Nat Genet. 2012;44(11):1207-1214 (epipolymorphism); Xie H, et al. Nucleic Acids Res. 2011;39(10):4099-4108 (entropy). [FDRP/qFDRP/epipolymorphism/entropy levels VERIFIED from gkaa120]
tools.key_claims: FDRP read-pair discordance; qFDRP uses Hamming distance; first systematic WSH comparison incl. tumor (Ewing) data; WSH captures cell-mixture effects complementary to mean methylation.

survey.notes:
PRIMARY-SOURCE VERIFICATION STATUS (verified=true confirmed from paper / Bioconductor-GitHub / PMC full text; URLs+PMIDs+DOIs attached):

- CoMeBack: btaa049 full text fetched, all thresholds VERIFIED.
- Comethyl: PMC8921619 full text fetched; adjacency formula a_ij=((1+cor)/2)^beta, TOM, eigennode=PC1, region>=3CpG/150bp, low-pass WGBS, ASD cord-blood VERIFIED. PMID 35037016 / DOI 10.1093/bib/bbab554.
- CGmapTools: PMC6454434 full text fetched; ASM = read-allele partition + t-test, mCG<=0.2/>=0.8, BH P<=0.05, germline tissues, short-read VERIFIED. PMID 28968643 / btx595.
- mHapTk: GitHub README fetched; R2 read-derived signed r^2 + 2x2, MHBDiscovery r^2>=0.5/p0.05/win5, 8 stats VERIFIED. PMID 36179079 / btac650.
- Metheor: PMC10062925 fetched; LPMD = fixed-distance CpG-pair discordance removing PDR read-length bias, 7 read-level measures, Bismark short-read, CCLE cancer VERIFIED. PMID 36940213 / pcbi.1010946.
- WSH (FDRP/qFDRP/epipolymorphism/entropy): NAR gkaa120 full text fetched; FDRP read-pair, qFDRP Hamming, epipolymorphism/entropy 4-CpG epialleles, Ewing tumor VERIFIED.
- eDMR: search/abstract level only (BMC + ScienceDirect topic + CRAN mirror consistent); bimodal segmentation + weighted-Z VERIFIED conceptually; full Methods not deep-fetched. PMID 23735126. No claim made beyond this.

KEY CROSS-CUTTING INSIGHTS FOR THE ISM COMPARISON (load-bearing):
1) AXIS / MATRIX-ORIENTATION is the master discriminator. ISM reduces the read x CpG matrix ROW-wise -> read-to-read distance -> clustering + PERMANOVA (between-MOLECULE structure). The co-methylation family reduces COLUMN-wise -> CpG-CpG coupling (MHB/mHapTk R2, LPMD) OR collapses to a scalar (MHL, PDR, epipolymorphism, entropy, qFDRP). Same input matrix, transposed reduction, different biology.
2) STRUCTURE vs DISORDER is ISM's thesis. The WSH/heterogeneity family (PDR, LPMD, epipolymorphism, ME, FDRP, qFDRP) measures MAGNITUDE of disorder and discards group identity. ISM's PERMANOVA + silhouette clustering tests whether disorder is STRUCTURED by haplotype/somatic state. ISM CORE 4 re-implements the disorder family (NME, epipolymorphism) only as a CONTRAST baseline.
3) CLOSEST EXTERNAL RELATIVES ranked: (a) qFDRP (read-pair Hamming) and ISM read-read distance = same statistic pre-reduction (qFDRP averages, ISM clusters); (b) mHapTk R2 / MHB = read-level CpG-CpG dual; (c) CGmapTools asr = naive (confounded) ALLELE-axis ISM's normal-anchored cis-test de-confounds; (d) MHL = read-level coordination scalar.
4) NO external tool has: HP1-vs-HP1-1 somatic-controlled axis, NormalBaseline residual / normal-anchored cis-test (d_somatic/d_cis/d_drift), copy-partition decomposition of Δβ, LOH/CN coupling, OR 5hmC awareness. These four are ISM-unique vs this entire literature.
5) PLATFORM/CONTEXT GAP: every surveyed tool is short-read bisulfite (CoMeBack = array); NONE is ONT long-read native or uses BAM MM/ML tags. Closest cancer-somatic framings: Metheor/WSH (intratumor heterogeneity), CGmapTools (allelic but germline-demoed). MHB/MHL cancer use = cfDNA TOO not tumor allelic ASM. ISM's ONT-long-read + 5mC&5hmC + somatic-paired niche is unoccupied.
6) eDMR is a category mismatch (DMR caller, not co-methylation metric) — kept per user list, flagged as 'between-group region' contrast pole nearest to ISM CORE 4 per-CpG Fisher+BH only.
COMMON FORMULAS confirmed: read-level LD r^2 from 2x2 N00/N01/N10/N11 (MHB/mHapTk); epipolymorphism = 1 - Σ p_i^2 over 4-CpG patterns; methylation entropy = -Σ p_i log2 p_i / N; MHL = Σ w_l P_l / Σ w_l (weighted fully-methylated substring fraction).

survey.category: Allele-specific methylation (ASM) callers — survey vs ISM (InterSubMod, ONT long-read cancer somatic, read-to-read distance + PERMANOVA structure engine)

tools.name: DAMEfinder
tools.type: R/Bioconductor package; short-read bisulfite (BS-seq); region-level (per-CpG and per-CpG-tuple); germline/imprinting + cancer (colorectal) demonstrated
tools.method_core: Two modes. (1) SNP-based 'exhaustive' mode: needs a VCF of HETEROZYGOUS SNPs (called by Bis-SNP from the BS-seq itself), assigns each overlapping read to reference vs alternative allele, computes per-SNP ASM = |X_M^ref/X^ref - X_M^alt/X^alt| (difference in methylation proportion between the two allele groups). (2) Tuple-based 'fast' mode: takes methtuple CpG-pair counts, computes per-tuple ASM = log10[(X_MM+c)(X_UU+c)/((X_MU+c)(X_UM+c))] * w_i — a log odds ratio of CONCORDANT (MM,UU) vs DISCORDANT (MU,UM) CpG-pair read states, weighted by w_i = P(0.5-e < theta < 0.5+e | X_MM,X_UU) with theta~Beta(gamma+X_MM, gamma+X_UU), e=0.2, gamma=0.5, penalizing departure from a 50:50 MM:UU balance. Tuple mode needs NO SNPs (captures imprinting/XCI/sequence-dependent ASM); SNP mode is sequence-dependent ASM only.
tools.granularity: Per-CpG (SNP mode) / per-CpG-tuple (tuple mode) ASM scores aggregated to REGIONS (DAMEs). Read-state-aware via methtuple but final output is regional.
tools.statistics: Differential ASM between conditions: per-position limma lmFit + eBayes moderated t-statistic on the ASM scores; spatial smoothing via bumphunter clusterMaker + loessByCluster; regions found either by (A) bumphunter regionFinder permutation test on area statistic A=sum|beta| with empirical p-value + BH-FDR, or (B) Simes p-value aggregation within clusters (pc = min{n*p(i)/i}).
tools.haplotype_aware: SNP-mode is single-het-SNP-anchored (unphased — does NOT require phased haplotypes); tuple-mode is SNP-free and read-pattern-based. No long-read haplotype tags.
tools.cancer_somatic: Demonstrated on colorectal cancer (loss of imprinting) AND normal blood (XCI validation); method is general, not somatic-variant-specific.
tools.input: Bismark-aligned BS-seq BAM (+VCF of het SNPs for SNP mode, or methtuple output for tuple mode). Short-read bisulfite only — NOT nanopore long-read.
tools.vs_ism: Closest in spirit to ISM's ALLELE-axis (ALT vs REF read methylation) and its per-CpG Fisher/Δβ 'disorder' family. KEY DIFFERENCES: DAMEfinder is short-read BS-seq germline/imprinting-oriented; its tuple ASM score = log-OR of pairwise CpG concordance (MM·UU/MU·UM) — a 2-CpG co-methylation metric, NOT ISM's full read×read NHD/L1 distance matrix + UPGMA clustering + PERMANOVA pseudo-F structural test. DAMEfinder has NO between-molecule distance matrix, NO PERMANOVA/dispersion structure engine, NO 5hmC handling, NO normal-anchored cis-test, NO LOH/CN coupling. ISM cites DAMEfinder as the per-CpG-tuple ASM-score precedent; ISM generalizes from 2-CpG tuples to whole-read distance geometry on ONT 5mC+5hmC.
tools.purpose: Detect differential allele-specific methylation regions (DAMEs) between two conditions.
tools.key_claims: ASM score (tuple log-OR + Beta-moderated weight) verified verbatim from PMC + Bioconductor vignette; SNP mode needs only het (unphased) SNPs verified from vignette; limma+bumphunter pipeline verified.
tools.citation: Orjuela S, Machlab D, Menigatti M, Marra G, Robinson MD. Epigenetics & Chromatin 2020;13:25. DOI:10.1186/s13072-020-00346-8; PMC7268773; PMID 32487212

tools.name: methylpy AMRfinder (allelically methylated regions)
tools.type: Python pipeline (methylpy / MethPipe lineage); short-read WGBS bisulfite; region-level; germline/normal-tissue oriented
tools.method_core: AMRfinder (methylpy 'allelic' / call-AMR) detects ALLELE-SPECIFIC methylation at REGION level from BS-seq WITHOUT requiring SNP information. It models per-read CpG methylation patterns and tests whether reads in a window are better explained by a single methylation distribution vs TWO distinct allelic methylation states (bimodal/two-epiallele structure), then merges significant CpGs into AMRs. SNP-free: uses read-level co-methylation structure, not allele genotype.
tools.granularity: Per-read methylation pattern within a window, aggregated to allelically-methylated REGIONS (AMRs).
tools.statistics: Likelihood-ratio framework: compares a single-allele (one parameter) model against a two-allele model for reads in a window; significant windows merged into AMRs. Lineage of Fang 2012 / MethPipe allelic model. Exact within-tool LR formula NOT fetched from a single primary methylpy methods page (see UNVERIFIED note).
tools.haplotype_aware: SNP-free and phasing-free — infers two allelic epialleles from read methylation patterns directly.
tools.cancer_somatic: Germline/normal-tissue and imprinting oriented (human tissue AMR atlases); not somatic-cancer-specific.
tools.input: Bisulfite WGBS aligned reads (methylpy/Bismark/BISCUIT outputs). Short-read.
tools.vs_ism: Conceptually the SAME family as ISM's core idea (read methylation patterns reveal two molecular populations WITHOUT SNPs). BUT methylpy AMRfinder reduces this to a 1-vs-2-distribution LR test on a window and outputs a binary AMR region; ISM keeps the full read×read distance matrix + hierarchical clustering (k=2..10 by silhouette, not fixed 2) + PERMANOVA pseudo-F + dispersion test, i.e., tests STRUCTURE/significance of arbitrary subclonal groupings, not just 2 alleles. methylpy is short-read germline; ISM is ONT 5mC+5hmC somatic cancer with LOH/CN coupling and normal-anchored cis-test.
tools.purpose: Call allelically methylated regions (AMRs) genome-wide from BS-seq without genotype.
tools.key_claims: SNP-free regional AMR detection verified from secondary review + tool description; exact in-tool LR formula UNVERIFIED (could not fetch a primary methylpy methods page quoting the AMR test math verbatim).
tools.citation: Schultz MD et al. (methylpy, Nature 2015, 'Human body epigenome maps...') / Fang F et al. PNAS 2012 (AMR LR model lineage). https://github.com/yupenghe/methylpy

tools.name: Fang et al. 2012 per-read ASM Fisher exact (foundational method)
tools.type: Statistical method / pipeline; short-read WGBS (MethylC-seq); read-level test, region-summarized; germline/normal tissue
tools.method_core: The canonical READ-LEVEL ASM test: for each heterozygous SNP, separate the reads carrying allele1 vs allele2, then for nearby CpGs build a 2x2 contingency table of (allele) x (methylated/unmethylated CpG read counts) and apply FISHER'S EXACT TEST for association between allele identity and methylation state. Reads are split by the SNP base they carry — requires only het SNPs per read (single-SNP-anchored), not a phased haplotype.
tools.granularity: Per-read CpG calls on SNP-containing reads -> per-SNP/per-CpG Fisher test -> ASM loci/regions.
tools.statistics: Fisher's exact test on the 2x2 allele x methylation read-count table (association of methylation with one SNP allele); multiple-testing correction across loci.
tools.haplotype_aware: Single-het-SNP-anchored, unphased — read assigned to an allele by the SNP base it directly covers.
tools.cancer_somatic: Germline/normal human tissues (genomic landscape of ASM); not somatic cancer.
tools.input: Short-read bisulfite (MethylC-seq) BAM + het SNPs. NOT long-read.
tools.vs_ism: The ancestral 'per-read ASM Fisher' the prompt references, and the direct precedent for ISM's CORE 4 per-CpG Fisher-exact + BH-FDR and its ALLELE-axis.
