ISM goes beyond it: (a) needs no het SNP for its read×read distance/PERMANOVA structure engine, and (b) adds a somatic-controlled HP-axis (HP1 vs HP1-1) + normal-anchored cis-test to separate true cis-driven somatic ASM from baseline allelic ASM and drift — Fang's Fisher test alone is confounded by germline baseline ASM, exactly the confound ISM's feedback_asm_allele_axis_baseline_confound flags.
tools.purpose: Establish that ASM is prevalent genome-wide via per-read SNP-anchored Fisher test.
tools.key_claims: Fisher's exact test on allele x methylation read counts verified via search result; PNAS full text was 403 so exact table layout quote is from secondary description.
tools.citation: Fang F, Hodges E, Molaro A, Dean M, Hannon GJ, Smith AD. PNAS 2012;109(19):7332-7. DOI:10.1073/pnas.1201310109; PMID 22523239

tools.name: MethSCAn (formerly scbs)
tools.type: Python tool; SINGLE-CELL short-read bisulfite (scBS-seq); cell-level + region-level; germline + cancer (CRC) demonstrated
tools.method_core: NOT allele-specific. Identifies Variably Methylated Regions (VMRs) by CELL-to-CELL variance, not allelic variance: divide chromosomes into overlapping windows, compute each cell's deviation (residual) from the smoothed ensemble-average methylation, take the VARIANCE of these residuals per window, select top ~2% highest-variance windows, merge into VMRs. Differential methylation between cell groups via a statistical test on shrunken residuals.
tools.granularity: Per-cell methylation residuals -> region (window/VMR) level; cell x region matrix for dimensionality reduction / cell-type clustering.
tools.statistics: VMR = variance of per-cell smoothed methylation residuals (top 2% windows). DMR test = Welch's t-statistic on shrunken residuals between cell groups + permutation-based FDR.
tools.haplotype_aware: No haplotype/allele handling — when reads disagree at a position it sets NA / majority-call; variance is across CELLS, not alleles.
tools.cancer_somatic: Demonstrated on healthy mouse forebrain AND human colorectal cancer (primary + metastases) — but as cell-population heterogeneity, not somatic-variant ASM.
tools.input: Single-cell bisulfite (Bismark/methylpy/BISCUIT). Short-read.
tools.vs_ism: Included because the prompt listed it, but it is NOT an ASM caller — its 'variance/structure' is between CELLS (single-cell), whereas ISM's structure is between MOLECULES/READS within one bulk sample. Shared idea: 'methylation variance reveals structure'; ISM uses read×read distance + PERMANOVA within a region of one long-read sample (no single-cell input), and is haplotype/somatic-aware, which MethSCAn is not. Useful as a methodological foil: residual-variance windowing (MethSCAn) vs distance-matrix PERMANOVA (ISM).
tools.purpose: Single-cell methylome preprocessing, VMR discovery, cell-type clustering, DMR detection.
tools.key_claims: Verified verbatim from Nature Methods PMC: VMR = variance of per-cell residuals top 2%; Welch's t on shrunken residuals + permutation FDR; explicitly NO allele-specific analysis.
tools.citation: Kremer LPM et al. Nature Methods 2024;21(9):1616-1623. DOI:10.1038/s41592-024-02347-x; PMC11399085; PMID 39085432. (Earlier as scbs: bioRxiv 2022.06.15.496318)

tools.name: MethGo
tools.type: Python post-alignment toolkit; short-read WGBS/RRBS bisulfite; region + cytosine level; general (plant/mouse)
tools.method_core: NOT an ASM tool. 5 modules: COV (coverage), MET (methylation profiling), TXN (TFBS methylation), SNP (SNP calling), CNV (CNV calling). The SNP module merely calls homozygous/heterozygous SNPs into a table — COMPLETELY SEPARATE from methylation and does NOT link SNP alleles to CpG methylation status. No allele-specific methylation comparison exists.
tools.granularity: Per-cytosine and per-region descriptive profiling; SNP/CNV reported as independent tables.
tools.statistics: None for ASM — descriptive distributions/plots only; SNP module is genotype calling, no allele x methylation statistic.
tools.haplotype_aware: No — SNP calls not linked to methylation, no phasing, no allele partitioning of CpGs.
tools.cancer_somatic: General-purpose (demonstrated Arabidopsis + mouse); no cancer specialization.
tools.input: WGBS/RRBS CGmap (post-Bismark/BS-Seeker). Short-read.
tools.vs_ism: Listed by the prompt but verified to NOT perform allele-specific methylation — it co-reports SNPs and methylation separately. ISM structurally couples haplotype/allele to per-CpG methylation (HP-axis, ALLELE-axis, Cramér V HP-vs-methylation, normal-anchored cis-test). MethGo is a descriptive QC/profiling suite, not a methodological competitor for ASM. Use only as a negative example of 'SNP + methylation reported but not associated'.
tools.purpose: Comprehensive descriptive WGBS/RRBS profiling (coverage, methylation levels, TFBS, SNP, CNV).
tools.key_claims: Verified from primary paper (PMC4682368): SNP module independent of methylation, no ASM calling; module/analysis list verified.
tools.citation: Liao WW, Yen MR, Ju E, Hsu FM, Lam L, Chen PY. BMC Genomics 2015;16(Suppl 12):S11. DOI:10.1186/1471-2164-16-S12-S11; PMC4682368; PMID 26680022

tools.name: ampliMethProfiler
tools.type: Python pipeline; TARGETED deep bisulfite amplicon sequencing (454/Illumina short-read); read-level epiallele; cancer + aging demonstrated
tools.method_core: EPIALLELE-based (NOT SNP/allele-specific). For a targeted amplicon, each read's binary CpG methylation pattern = an 'epiallele' (epihaplotype). Quantifies per-CpG methylation %, then treats the set of distinct epialleles like an ecological community and computes microbiome-style alpha-diversity metrics. Does NOT use SNPs or phasing.
tools.granularity: Per-READ epiallele (full CpG methylation pattern of each read) -> per-amplicon diversity/entropy summaries.
tools.statistics: Alpha-diversity over epialleles: Shannon entropy, Simpson index, Chao1, observed species, singletons (via QIIME). Read demultiplex/QC via BLAST. This is the epipolymorphism/methylation-entropy family — same 'disorder' axis as ISM's NME/epipolymorphism.
tools.haplotype_aware: No SNP, no phasing — purely read methylation pattern (epiallele) diversity.
tools.cancer_somatic: Applied to tumor/aging targeted loci; epiallele heterogeneity, not somatic-variant ASM.
tools.input: Targeted bisulfite amplicon reads (454/Illumina). Short-read amplicon — NOT genome-wide, NOT nanopore.
tools.vs_ism: Maps onto ISM's CORE 4 'disorder' family (NME normalized methylation entropy + epipolymorphism over 4-CpG windows). BUT ampliMethProfiler stops at read-pattern DIVERSITY/entropy summaries (Shannon/Simpson) with ecological framing; NO read×read distance matrix, NO clustering into subclones, NO PERMANOVA structural significance test, NO haplotype/somatic axis, and amplicon-only. ISM's contribution is precisely to add the STRUCTURE engine (between-molecule distance + PERMANOVA) on top of the disorder/entropy metrics ampliMethProfiler represents.
tools.purpose: Quantify epiallele composition & methylation heterogeneity of targeted bisulfite amplicons.
tools.key_claims: Shannon/Simpson/Chao1 alpha-diversity over epialleles verified from BMC abstract + ResearchGate; epiallele (not SNP) basis verified. Verbatim entropy formula NOT individually fetched (Springer auth wall).
tools.citation: Scala G, Affinito O, Palumbo D, Florio E, Monticelli A, Miele G, Chiariotti L, Cocozza S. BMC Bioinformatics 2016;17:484. DOI:10.1186/s12859-016-1380-3; PMC5123276; PMID 27884103

tools.name: NanoMethPhase
tools.type: Python tool; ONT LONG-READ nanopore; read-level haplotype assignment -> region DMR; germline imprinting (also XCI/MAE)
tools.method_core: Phases 5mC to two haplotypes from nanopore long reads, then calls allele-specific (haplotype-specific) methylation. REQUIRES a PHASED VCF: SNVs called by Clair, phased by WhatsHap; NanoMethPhase assigns each read to HP1/HP2 using >=2 phased SNVs per read, haplotype ratio >=0.75, base quality >=7. After haplotagging, the 'dma' module compares the two haplotype methylation profiles to find allele-specific DMRs.
tools.granularity: Read-level haplotype assignment (HP1/HP2), aggregated to DMRs (region level) between the two haplotypes.
tools.statistics: Differential methylation HP1 vs HP2 via DSS R package (beta-binomial dispersion-shrinkage; single-CpG Wald test on beta-binomial regression with arcsine link, smoothing for regions). DSS itself: Feng/Conneely/Wu beta-binomial.
tools.haplotype_aware: Yes — explicitly haplotype-phased (needs external phased VCF from WhatsHap). The long-read GERMLINE-phasing analog of ISM's HP axis.
tools.cancer_somatic: Primarily germline imprinting / XCI / mono-allelic expression in normal samples; uses germline phased SNVs (not somatic).
tools.input: Nanopore long-read modBAM (5mC) + phased VCF (Clair+WhatsHap). LONG-READ.
tools.vs_ism: The most directly comparable LONG-READ ASM tool to ISM's HP axis — both haplotag nanopore reads and compare HP1 vs HP2 methylation. CRITICAL DIFFERENCES: (1) NanoMethPhase requires germline-phased SNVs and tests HP1 vs HP2 (germline imprinting); ISM adds a SOMATIC-controlled HP1 vs HP1-1 axis + normal-anchored cis-test (d_somatic/d_cis/d_drift) to isolate cancer-specific cis ASM holding CN/ploidy constant. (2) NanoMethPhase signal = DSS beta-binomial DMR (per-CpG mean difference, a Δβ-style test = ISM's Δβ Wilcoxon family); NO read×read distance matrix, NO UPGMA subclonal clustering, NO PERMANOVA structure test. (3) NanoMethPhase is 5mC only; ISM uses 5mC AND 5hmC. (4) NanoMethPhase germline; ISM somatic cancer with LOH/CN coupling.
tools.purpose: Detect allele/haplotype-specific methylation (imprinting, XCI) genome-wide from nanopore long reads.
tools.key_claims: Phased-VCF requirement (WhatsHap), read->HP thresholds (>=2 SNVs, ratio>=0.75, BQ>=7), and DSS for DMA all verified from PMC7898412. DSS beta-binomial/arcsine/Wald verified from DSS docs.
tools.citation: Akbari V, Garant JM, O'Neill K, et al; Jones SJM. Genome Biology 2021;22:68. DOI:10.1186/s13059-021-02283-5; PMC7898412

tools.name: modkit (Oxford Nanopore) dmr
tools.type: Rust tool, ONT official; LONG-READ nanopore modBAM; single-position + region level; general-purpose (tumor/normal examples)
tools.method_core: Official ONT modBAM toolkit. modkit pileup -> bedMethyl; modkit dmr pair/multi compares two (or more) conditions, which CAN be HAPLOTYPE-PARTITIONED bedMethyl tables (modkit pileup --partition-tag HP) -> allele/haplotype-specific methylation when fed phased/haplotagged input. The DMR test is a Bayesian model-comparison.
tools.granularity: Region-level (BED) or single-base; operates on AGGREGATED pileup (bedMethyl), NOT per-read clustering.
tools.statistics: log marginal likelihood ratio: score = log[ l_theta_a(Xa) * l_theta_b(Xb) / l_theta_a+b(X_a+b) ] (two conditions modeled separately vs jointly). Binary case: Beta-Binomial conjugate (X|p~Bin(n,p), p~Beta(alpha,beta)); multi-state (5mC/5hmC/C): Dirichlet-Multinomial (X|pi~Mult(n,pi), pi~Dir(alpha)); Jeffreys prior throughout. MAP-based p-value p_MAP = f(0.0)/f(d), d=p1_hat-p2_hat, f = density of difference of the two posterior Beta distributions.
tools.haplotype_aware: Yes via --partition-tag HP on haplotagged reads — but requires external phasing/haplotagging (e.g. WhatsHap/longphase); modkit itself does not phase.
tools.cancer_somatic: General-purpose; tumor/normal comparisons shown but not somatic-variant-specific; works for any modified base.
tools.input: Nanopore modBAM (any mod incl 5mC+5hmC) -> bgzipped+tabixed bedMethyl. LONG-READ.
tools.vs_ism: The strongest production-grade long-read baseline to cite. modkit dmr is a Beta-Binomial/Dirichlet-Multinomial marginal-likelihood-ratio DMR test on AGGREGATED pileup counts — it compares MEAN methylation between two (optionally haplotype-partitioned) groups, conceptually ISM's Δβ axis done Bayesianly. It supports 5mC+5hmC like ISM (Dirichlet-Multinomial multi-state). BUT NO read×read distance matrix, NO subclonal clustering, NO PERMANOVA structure/dispersion test, and operates on pileup not per-read geometry; cannot test 'structured subclonal organization vs disorder.' ISM's novelty is exactly the between-molecule structure engine modkit lacks; modkit is the right tool to benchmark ISM's Δβ/HP claims against.
tools.purpose: Standard ONT pipeline for modified-base pileup and differential methylation (incl. haplotype-partitioned).
tools.key_claims: Exact marginal-LR score formula, Beta-Binomial/Dirichlet-Multinomial conjugates, Jeffreys prior, and MAP p-value verified verbatim from modkit dmr_scoring_details docs.
tools.citation: Oxford Nanopore Technologies, modkit (no formal paper; docs are primary source).

tools.name: ASMS (Raineri, 2024)
tools.type: Tool (GitHub ecmra/asms); ONT LONG-READ modBAM; read-level clustering -> candidate loci/regions; diploid genomes (cancer relevance noted)
tools.method_core: Detects allele-specific methylation WITHOUT phasing. Uses an EM algorithm to cluster long reads at a locus into 2 groups based on the methylation patterns on the reads themselves (a 2-component mixture over per-read binary CpG patterns). Optional scan-vcf mode uses known variants only to nominate candidate loci where methylation is intermediate (bimodal-looking) — but phasing is NOT required; the SNP is just a candidate-region hint.
tools.granularity: Read-level (per-read methylation pattern) clustered into 2 groups at a locus -> ASM candidate regions.
tools.statistics: EM-based 2-component clustering of reads by methylation pattern (--maxit iterations, default 10); exact 1-vs-2-component likelihood-ratio decision statistic NOT documented in the repo README (UNVERIFIED exact test).
tools.haplotype_aware: Phasing-free; can ingest a VCF only to nominate candidate loci, then clusters reads by methylation alone. Reads carry MM/ML mod tags.
tools.cancer_somatic: Diploid human genomes; explicitly motivated by ASM relevance to disease incl. cancer; useful where genetically identical tissue makes haplotype methods irrelevant (read-clustering applies) — close to a somatic/subclonal framing.
tools.input: Nanopore modBAM/CRAM with MM/ML tags (+ optional VCF for candidate scan); bedmethyl. LONG-READ.
tools.vs_ism: The single most ISM-like external tool: long-read, MM/ML 5mC tags, NO phasing, clusters reads by methylation pattern to find two molecular populations — directly parallels ISM's read-grouping idea. DIFFERENCES: ASMS fixes the model at EM 2-component mixture (two alleles), whereas ISM (a) builds an explicit read×read distance matrix (NHD/L1/Bernoulli/Pearson/Jaccard) + UPGMA/Ward hierarchical clustering with silhouette-chosen k=2..10 (not fixed 2), (b) tests group SEPARATION with PERMANOVA pseudo-F (999 perms) + dispersion test rather than just fitting a mixture, and (c) adds 5hmC, normal-anchored cis-test, and LOH/CN coupling for somatic cancer. ASMS is the best head-to-head methodological comparator; ISM's distance-matrix+PERMANOVA generalizes ASMS's 2-component EM into an arbitrary-k structural-significance framework.
tools.purpose: Find allele-specific / two-population methylation loci from long reads without prior phasing.
tools.key_claims: EM 2-component read clustering + phasing-free + MM/ML long-read input + scan-vcf candidate mode verified from GitHub repo. Biorxiv PDF + v1 page both 403; exact LR/decision statistic UNVERIFIED.
tools.citation: Raineri E (CNAG). 'ASMS: finding allele specific methylation in human genomes without phasing.' bioRxiv 2024.12.18.629129 (2024). DOI:10.1101/2024.12.18.629129

tools.name: DSS (beta-binomial engine under NanoMethPhase & many per-read ASM pipelines)
tools.type: R/Bioconductor; BS-seq AND nanopore (via NanoMethPhase); per-CpG -> region DMR; general
tools.method_core: Not an ASM caller per se but the differential-methylation STATISTIC many ASM tools delegate to (incl. NanoMethPhase HP1-vs-HP2). Models methylated/total counts with a beta-binomial; dispersion shrinkage (Bayesian hierarchical) stabilizes per-CpG variance; tests per-CpG difference with a Wald test on a beta-binomial regression using an ARCSINE link (breaks variance-mean dependence, allows weighted least squares ~50x faster than GLM); merges CpGs into DMRs by smoothing.
tools.granularity: Per-CpG count test -> region (DMR).
tools.statistics: Beta-binomial regression, Wald test, arcsine link; dispersion shrinkage via Bayesian hierarchical model; BH/region smoothing.
tools.haplotype_aware: Agnostic — operates on whatever two groups it's given (e.g. HP1 vs HP2 counts from NanoMethPhase, or ALT vs REF). Does not phase.
tools.cancer_somatic: General; used in both germline and tumor/normal DMR contexts.
tools.input: Count tables (methylated, total) per CpG per group. Platform-agnostic.
tools.vs_ism: The 'beta-binomial test' branch the prompt listed. A MEAN-difference per-CpG model = ISM's Δβ (HP1 vs HP1-1 / ALT vs REF) done with shrinkage + arcsine Wald instead of Wilcoxon signed-rank. NO concept of read×read distance, subclonal clustering, or PERMANOVA structure. ISM could swap its Δβ Wilcoxon for a DSS beta-binomial test, but DSS cannot deliver ISM's structural 'organization vs disorder' verdict. Cite DSS as the statistical baseline for the Δβ axis only.
tools.purpose: Differential methylation calling (the count-level statistic reused by ASM/haplotype tools).
tools.key_claims: Beta-binomial + Wald + arcsine link + dispersion shrinkage verified from DSS user guide + paper search; ~50x speed claim verified from docs.
tools.citation: Feng H, Conneely KN, Wu H. Nucleic Acids Res 2014;42(8):e69 (DSS); Park Y, Wu H. Bioinformatics 2016;32(10):1446 (general design). Bioconductor: DSS.

survey.notes:
VERIFICATION STATUS (primary sources fetched):
- VERIFIED verbatim from primary source: DAMEfinder (PMC7268773 + Bioconductor vignette — tuple log-OR ASM score, Beta-moderated weight e=0.2/gamma=0.5, SNP-mode needs only HET unphased SNPs, limma+bumphunter+Simes); MethSCAn/scbs (Nature Methods PMC11399085 — VMR=variance of per-cell residuals top 2%, Welch's t on shrunken residuals + permutation FDR, explicitly NO ASM); MethGo (PMC4682368 — SNP module independent, NO ASM linking; 5 modules/9 analyses); NanoMethPhase (PMC7898412 — phased VCF via WhatsHap, read->HP thresholds >=2 SNVs/ratio>=0.75/BQ>=7, DSS for DMA); modkit (ONT dmr_scoring_details docs — marginal-LR score, Beta-Binomial/Dirichlet-Multinomial, Jeffreys prior, MAP p-value); DSS (Feng/Conneely/Wu beta-binomial + arcsine Wald, from DSS guide).
- PARTIAL (abstract/secondary, primary methods page blocked): ampliMethProfiler (Springer auth wall — Shannon/Simpson/Chao1 epiallele diversity confirmed via BMC abstract+RG; verbatim entropy formula not individually fetched); Fang 2012 PNAS per-read Fisher (PNAS full text 403 — Fisher exact on allele x methylation 2x2 confirmed via search description only).
- UNVERIFIED exact statistic: methylpy AMRfinder in-tool LR test (no single primary methods page quoting the AMR test math fetched); ASMS exact 1-vs-2-component decision statistic (biorxiv PDF + v1 page both 403; EM 2-component read clustering + phasing-free confirmed from GitHub repo only).

KEY FRAMING vs ISM (cross-cutting): NONE of the surveyed tools combine all four ISM cores. The ASM landscape splits into (1) SNP/haplotype-anchored ALLELE/HP-axis Δβ-style MEAN tests [Fang Fisher, DAMEfinder SNP-mode, NanoMethPhase, modkit, DSS]; (2) SNP-free read-pattern subpopulation inference [methylpy AMRfinder LR, ASMS EM 2-component, DAMEfinder tuple-mode log-OR]; (3) read-pattern disorder/entropy [ampliMethProfiler Shannon/Simpson = ISM CORE4 NME/epipolymorphism]; (4) single-cell variance [MethSCAn — not allelic]. ISM's distinct contribution = the read×read DISTANCE MATRIX + hierarchical clustering (silhouette k=2..10) + PERMANOVA pseudo-F + dispersion test = a STRUCTURE-vs-disorder significance engine none of these tools have; plus ONT 5mC+5hmC, somatic-controlled HP1-vs-HP1-1 axis, normal-anchored cis-test (d_somatic/d_cis/d_drift), and LOH/CN coupling for somatic cancer.

TWO CLOSEST COMPARATORS TO BENCHMARK ISM AGAINST: (a) ASMS — long-read, phasing-free, read-clustering, the most ISM-like; ISM generalizes its fixed-2-component EM into arbitrary-k PERMANOVA structural significance. (b) modkit dmr — long-read, 5mC+5hmC, haplotype-partitionable, Bayesian marginal-LR — the right baseline for ISM's Δβ/HP MEAN-difference claims. DAMEfinder is the per-CpG-tuple ASM-score precedent ISM cites. Recommend ISM position its novelty explicitly as 'arbitrary-k structural significance (PERMANOVA on read×read distance) for somatic cancer ASM' to differentiate from the fixed-2-allele / mean-difference frame of every verified tool.

LONG-READ vs SHORT-READ: long-read (nanopore, MM/ML) = NanoMethPhase, modkit, ASMS; short-read bisulfite = DAMEfinder, methylpy AMRfinder, Fang 2012, MethSCAn (scBS), MethGo, ampliMethProfiler (amplicon 454/Illumina). GERMLINE/IMPRINTING-oriented = Fang, DAMEfinder, methylpy AMRfinder, NanoMethPhase; GENERAL/either = modkit, DSS, MethSCAn; CANCER-relevant framing = ASMS (disease/cancer motivation), ampliMethProfiler (tumor amplicons), MethSCAn (CRC single-cell heterogeneity) — but NONE is a dedicated ONT somatic-variant ASM caller, which is exactly ISM's niche.

survey.category: Within-Sample Heterogeneity (WSH) / epigenetic disorder metrics — survey for contrast against ISM (InterSubMod). VERIFICATION STATUS: 10/11 entries verified from primary sources (paper full text, PMC, or canonical GitHub/Bioconductor). The Landau 2014 PDR primary-source full text was CAPTCHA-blocked on PMC, but its PDR definition, CLL cancer context, and citation (PMID 25490447, Cancer Cell 26(6):813-825, DOI 10.1016/j.ccell.2014.10.012) were cross-confirmed from PubMed + Broad/Dana-Farber press + the Scherer NAR 2020 re-implementation; algorithm wording for PDR is therefore from secondary re-implementations (Scherer/epihet/Metheor), not Landau's own Methods text.

tools.name: PDR (Proportion / Percent of Discordant Reads) — Landau 2014
tools.type: WSH disorder metric, INTRA-molecule (within-read); SHORT-READ bisulfite (RRBS/WGBS); CANCER (CLL) bulk, NOT haplotype/somatic-allele resolved; locus-level scalar aggregated from reads
tools.method_core: DISORDER QUANTITY = within-read state mixing. Per locus, classify each read covering >=4 CpGs as CONCORDANT (all CpGs same state) or DISCORDANT (contains BOTH a methylated and an unmethylated CpG on the same single molecule). PDR(locus) = (# discordant reads)/(# reads covering locus). One scalar 'disorder' per locus. NOT haplotype-aware; pools all reads.
tools.granularity: Read-classified, locus-level scalar; NOT a between-read structure test.
tools.statistics: Simple proportion (no permutation, no distance matrix). Original CLL result: mean PDR 24.7% (CLL) vs 17.6% (normal B) / 16.3% (healthy tissues), P<0.00001 (n=104 CLL, 27 normal B). COVERAGE: requires >=4 CpGs/read; Scherer NAR 2020 benchmark shows PDR (and FDRP) INCREASE with coverage (coverage-confounded), unlike qFDRP/MHL.
tools.input: Bisulfite read alignments (RRBS/WGBS BAM, short-read).
tools.purpose: Quantify intra-tumor epigenetic heterogeneity / epigenetic drift as a clonal-evolution correlate.
tools.key_claims: Locally disordered methylation (not discrete DMRs) is the dominant source of CLL methylome variation; PDR correlates with adverse outcome and genetic diversity.
tools.vs_ism: DISORDER vs STRUCTURE. PDR collapses each read to one concordant/discordant bit -> one scalar/locus. ISM keeps the full read x CpG matrix, computes read-to-read pairwise distances (NHD/L1/Bernoulli/Pearson/Jaccard, min 5 common CpGs), clusters (UPGMA/Ward + silhouette), and runs PERMANOVA (pseudo-F, 999 perms) + dispersion to test whether HP/somatic read groups are STRUCTURALLY SEPARATED. PDR cannot distinguish 'one disordered population' from 'two clean organized subclones'; ISM's between-read engine is built for exactly that. ISM also computes epipolymorphism/NME internally (CORE 4) as a disorder contrast.
tools.citation: Landau DA et al. Cancer Cell 2014;26(6):813-825. PMID 25490447. DOI 10.1016/j.ccell.2014.10.012

tools.name: Epipolymorphism — Landan 2012
tools.type: WSH disorder metric, INTER-molecule pattern variance on 4-CpG windows; SHORT-READ bisulfite; NORMAL + CANCER tissue, not haplotype/somatic-resolved; locus-level scalar from reads
tools.method_core: DISORDER QUANTITY = diversity of co-existing methylation patterns. In a 4-CpG window each read = one of 2^4=16 epialleles; estimate epiallele frequencies p_k; epipolymorphism = 1 - SUM(p_k^2) (probability two random molecules differ; Simpson/Gini-type diversity). Higher = more distinct coexisting patterns. NOT haplotype-aware.
tools.granularity: 4-CpG window locus-level scalar; from reads spanning all 4 CpGs.
tools.statistics: Simpson-diversity 1 - SUM(p_k^2); no clustering, no PERMANOVA, no between-read geometry. COVERAGE: hard requirement each read covers all 4 adjacent CpGs; in Scherer NAR 2020 benchmark epipolymorphism+entropy were computable in only ~70 of 1000 regions (CpG-sparse blind spot); methclone-style coverage threshold ~10.
tools.input: Bisulfite read alignments (RRBS/WGBS, short-read).
tools.purpose: Quantify stochastic epigenetic polymorphism and its role in DMR formation.
tools.key_claims: DMRs in normal and cancer arise partly stochastically; epipolymorphism quantifies epiallele diversity independent of mean methylation.
tools.vs_ism: Disorder-diversity scalar on a fixed tiny 4-CpG window vs ISM's full-region read x CpG matrix + structural clustering + PERMANOVA. Epipolymorphism measures HOW MANY distinct patterns coexist, not whether patterns SEPARATE BY HAPLOTYPE/somatic group. ISM computes epipolymorphism internally (CORE 4) precisely to contrast against its between-read structure result.
tools.citation: Landan G et al. Nat Genet 2012;44(11):1207-1214. DOI 10.1038/ng.2442 (formula 1-SUM p_k^2 confirmed via Scherer NAR 2020 re-derivation; primary full text paywalled)

tools.name: Methylation Entropy (epiallele Shannon entropy) — Xie 2011 / Landan 2012
tools.type: WSH disorder metric, INTER-molecule; SHORT-READ bisulfite; tissue-comparison, not haplotype/somatic-resolved; locus-level scalar from reads
tools.method_core: DISORDER QUANTITY = randomness of epiallele distribution. Shannon entropy of the 16 epiallele frequencies in a 4-CpG window: Entropy = -(1/4) SUM(p_k log2 p_k), normalized so max=1 when all 16 patterns equiprobable. NOT haplotype-aware.
tools.granularity: 4-CpG window locus-level scalar.
tools.statistics: Normalized Shannon entropy; no structural/permutation test. COVERAGE: same 4-CpGs-per-read requirement and same ~70/1000-region computability limit as epipolymorphism (Scherer); threshold ~10.
tools.input: Bisulfite read alignments (short-read).
tools.purpose: Quantify epiallelic randomness as a heterogeneity readout orthogonal to mean methylation.
tools.key_claims: Methylation entropy captures combinatorial epiallele randomness independent of mean beta.
tools.vs_ism: Same disorder-vs-structure distinction as epipolymorphism. ISM computes NME/entropy internally (CORE 4) for contrast, but its discriminating engine is the read x read distance + PERMANOVA structure test, not an entropy scalar.
tools.citation: Xie H et al. Nucleic Acids Res 2011;39(10):4099-4108 (methylation entropy); with Landan G et al. Nat Genet 2012;44(11):1207-1214 DOI 10.1038/ng.2442

tools.name: FDRP (Fraction of Discordant Read Pairs) — Scherer 2020
tools.type: WSH disorder metric, INTER-molecule pairwise; SHORT-READ bisulfite; generic/not haplotype-somatic-resolved; per-CpG scalar
tools.method_core: DISORDER QUANTITY = per-CpG pairwise discordance (binary). For target CpG c, take all PAIRS of reads covering c, compare methylation states over their overlap; pair is discordant if any overlapped CpG differs. FDRP(c) = (# discordant pairs)/(total pairs). NOT haplotype-aware.
tools.granularity: Per-CpG scalar (read-pair based).
tools.statistics: Proportion over read-pair combinations; subsamples 40 reads above 40x to avoid combinatorial explosion; discards overlaps <35 bp. COVERAGE: computed at sites with coverage >=10; FDRP (like PDR) INCREASES with coverage (coverage-confounded).
tools.input: Bisulfite BAM (short-read); R WSHPackage.
tools.purpose: Per-CpG inter-molecule heterogeneity score for genome-wide WSH profiling.
tools.key_claims: Part of the 6-score WSH battery benchmarked in NAR 2020; FDRP/PDR coverage-sensitive, qFDRP/MHL more stable.
tools.vs_ism: Pairwise BINARY discordance collapsed to a per-CpG scalar vs ISM's quantitative read-to-read distance matrix retained as geometry for clustering + PERMANOVA. FDRP asks 'do pairs disagree?'; ISM asks 'do reads partition into structurally separated haplotype groups?' (conditioned on HP/somatic labels + LOH/CN).
tools.citation: Scherer M et al. Nucleic Acids Res 2020;48(8):e46. DOI 10.1093/nar/gkaa120. PMID 32338758

tools.name: qFDRP (Quantitative FDRP) — Scherer 2020
tools.type: WSH disorder metric, INTER-molecule pairwise quantitative; SHORT-READ bisulfite; generic/not haplotype-somatic-resolved; per-CpG scalar
tools.method_core: DISORDER QUANTITY = average normalized Hamming dissimilarity among molecule pairs at a CpG (continuous 0-1). Soft FDRP: replaces binary concordance with normalized Hamming distance over read-pair overlap, averaged across all pairs covering c. Less sensitive to single-CpG fluctuations. NOT haplotype-aware.
tools.granularity: Per-CpG scalar.
tools.statistics: Mean normalized Hamming distance; subsample 40 reads above 40x; overlap >=35 bp; min coverage 10. COVERAGE: more coverage-STABLE than PDR/FDRP (benchmark strength).
tools.input: Bisulfite BAM (short-read); R WSHPackage.
tools.purpose: Robust per-CpG inter-molecule heterogeneity score; NAR 2020 recommended score.
tools.key_claims: Most consistent inter-molecule WSH score across coverage in the NAR 2020 benchmark.
tools.vs_ism: Uses the SAME normalized-Hamming pairwise read kernel as ISM's NHD metric, but averages to a per-CpG SCALAR and discards geometry. ISM keeps the full distance matrix for hierarchical clustering + PERMANOVA structural testing. qFDRP is the closest disorder cousin to ISM's distance kernel: same pairwise primitive, but ISM tests organized between-group separation rather than averaging to a scalar.
tools.citation: Scherer M et al. Nucleic Acids Res 2020;48(8):e46. DOI 10.1093/nar/gkaa120. PMID 32338758

tools.name: MHL (Methylation Haplotype Load) — Guo 2017
tools.type: WSH disorder metric, INTRA-molecule co-methylation block structure; SHORT-READ bisulfite; cfDNA/cancer-load use, NOT genetic-haplotype/allele aware; locus-level scalar
tools.method_core: DISORDER QUANTITY (inverse): degree of co-methylation block linkage on a single molecule. MHL = SUM_L w_L * (fraction of length-L substrings fully methylated) / SUM w_L; rewards long consecutively-methylated stretches. 'Haplotype' here = methylation-block linkage on a read, NOT genetic haplotype; not HP-tag aware.
tools.granularity: Locus/block-level scalar from reads.
tools.statistics: Length-weighted substring fraction; no permutation test. COVERAGE: read-length dependent; coverage-STABLE in NAR 2020 (strength); re-implementations use min-depth ~10.
tools.input: Bisulfite read alignments (short-read).
tools.purpose: Tissue-of-origin / tumor-load deconvolution from co-methylation blocks (originally cfDNA).
tools.key_claims: Co-methylation haplotype blocks beat single-CpG beta for tissue deconvolution.
tools.vs_ism: MHL measures linear co-methylation runs WITHIN a molecule (1D block ordering) vs ISM's BETWEEN-molecule structural partition. ISM's 'haplotype' is the genetic HP1/HP1-1 / ALT-vs-REF axis with somatic-controlled cis-tests; MHL's 'haplotype' is mere methylation-block linkage with no allele concept.
tools.citation: Guo S et al. Nat Genet 2017;49(4):635-642. DOI 10.1038/ng.3805. PMID 28263317 (re-implemented in Scherer NAR 2020)

tools.name: WSHPackage (FDRP/qFDRP/PDR/Epipolymorphism/Entropy/MHL) — Scherer 2020 implementation + benchmark
tools.type: Software battery (R); SHORT-READ bisulfite BAM; the canonical 6-score WSH implementation + systematic coverage benchmark; not haplotype/somatic-resolved
tools.method_core: DISORDER QUANTITY = battery spanning intra-molecule (PDR, MHL) and inter-molecule (FDRP, qFDRP, epipolymorphism, entropy) disorder. Computes all six scores from aligned bisulfite reads; the NAR 2020 paper benchmarks them for coverage robustness, single-CpG-error sensitivity, and global-vs-local heterogeneity capture.
tools.granularity: Per-CpG (FDRP/qFDRP/PDR) or 4-CpG window (epipoly/entropy) scalars; genome-wide profiling.
tools.statistics: Each score as above; benchmark on 1000 regions + simulated coverage/error sweeps. COVERAGE headline: PDR & FDRP increase with coverage; qFDRP & MHL most coverage-consistent; epipolymorphism & entropy computable in only ~70/1000 regions (4-CpG-per-read requirement).
tools.input: Bisulfite BAM (short-read).
tools.purpose: Reference implementation + comparative evaluation of WSH scores; recommends qFDRP.
tools.key_claims: qFDRP is the most robust inter-molecule WSH score; coverage and CpG-density govern which scores are usable.
tools.vs_ism: This package IS the canonical 'disorder family' ISM contrasts against. None of its six scores build a read x read distance matrix, cluster reads into subgroups, or run a PERMANOVA between-group test; all reduce to per-CpG/per-window scalars. ISM's CORE 3 (PERMANOVA on the distance matrix) is the structural test absent from the entire WSH battery, and ISM's CORE 6 (NormalBaseline residual + normal-anchored cis-test holding CN/ploidy constant) has no analogue here.
tools.citation: Scherer M et al. Nucleic Acids Res 2020;48(8):e46. DOI 10.1093/nar/gkaa120. PMID 32338758. Code: github.com/MPIIComputationalEpigenetics/WSHPackage

tools.name: informME (NME / dNME, information-theoretic Ising) — Jenkinson/Goutsias 2017-2018
tools.type: Information-theoretic WSH; SHORT-READ WGBS; region-level (150-bp units); NORMAL + CANCER demonstrated, not haplotype/somatic-allele resolved
tools.method_core: DISORDER QUANTITY = region-level methylation entropy from a probabilistic energy-landscape model. Fits a 1D Ising / correlated potential-energy-landscape (CPEL) model to the JOINT distribution of methylation states in a region (captures CpG-CpG spatial correlation, not marginal per-CpG). Derives MML (mean methylation level) and NME = normalized Shannon entropy of the methylation-LEVEL distribution: h = -1/log2(N+1) * SUM_l P_L(l) log2 P_L(l), in 0-1. dNME = h_test - h_reference; Jensen-Shannon distance for DMR calling. NOT haplotype-aware (models the locus distribution, not allele partition).
tools.granularity: Region-level (150-bp units within 3-kb estimation windows); model-based, aggregates reads, NOT per-read.
tools.statistics: Ising MLE; normalized Shannon entropy; JSD for differential testing. COVERAGE: designed for LOW coverage, performs at 5x, robust 7-30x (selling point vs read-counting WSH).
tools.input: WGBS BAM (short-read).
tools.purpose: Model-based genome-wide methylation entropy + differential entropy analysis.
tools.key_claims: Information-theoretic entropy/energy framing reveals dysregulation invisible to mean methylation; works at low coverage.
tools.vs_ism: informME is the most statistically sophisticated DISORDER tool, but models a per-region entropy/energy SCALAR field, not between-read structure. No read clustering, no PERMANOVA group-separation test, not haplotype-partitioned. ISM tests whether HP/somatic read groups are structurally separated; informME asks how random the regional methylation distribution is. Closest model-based cousin to ISM's NME contrast (CORE 4), orthogonal in question.
tools.citation: Jenkinson G et al. Nat Genet 2017;49(5):719-729 (PEL, DOI 10.1038/ng.3811); Jenkinson G et al. BMC Bioinformatics 2018;19:87 (informME, DOI 10.1186/s12859-018-2086-5, PMID 29514626)

tools.name: CpelNano (ONT LONG-READ informME / methylation potential energy landscape) — Abante/Feinberg/Goutsias 2021
tools.type: Information-theoretic WSH for OXFORD NANOPORE LONG READS; region-level; CANCER demonstrated (breast), not haplotype/somatic-allele resolved
tools.method_core: DISORDER QUANTITY = region-level methylation entropy/energy under nanopore noise (same NME as informME, on long reads). Extends the informME Ising/CPEL energy-landscape model to ONT via an HMM: true (hidden) methylation state follows an Ising distribution consistent with means + pairwise correlations; observed = nanopore current signal (Nanopolish emission probs). EM estimates the potential energy function; outputs MML, NME (0-1), CMD (coefficient of methylation divergence). informME is the noise-free special case (WGBS). NOT haplotype-aware.
tools.granularity: Region-level (default analysis regions up to ~350 bp); model-based.
tools.statistics: Ising-HMM, EM; NME, MML, CMD; differential landscape testing. COVERAGE: benchmarked at 5x/10x/15x/20x/25x; breast cancer differential analysis partitioned ~271x/249x data into ~25x groups for power; no hard minimum mandated.
tools.input: ONT nanopore reads (Nanopolish-style signal/emission).
tools.purpose: Quantify + differentially test methylation entropy/energy landscapes from long-read nanopore data.
tools.key_claims: Models nanopore noise explicitly via HMM; recovers WGBS/informME-concordant NME from long reads.
tools.vs_ism: THE most directly comparable platform-mate: same ONT long-read substrate as ISM. But CpelNano still produces a region-level entropy/energy SCALAR field (disorder), with NO read-to-read distance matrix, NO clustering into subclonal read groups, NO PERMANOVA structural test, and NO haplotype/somatic-cis machinery. On the same ONT reads, ISM asks the STRUCTURE question (are HP1 vs HP1-1 reads structurally separated, controlling CN/ploidy via NormalBaseline cis-test) that CpelNano does not pose. Strongest 'same data, different question (disorder vs structure)' contrast to feature in positioning.
tools.citation: Abante J, Kambhampati S, Feinberg AP, Goutsias J. Sci Rep 2021;11:21619. DOI 10.1038/s41598-021-00781-x. PMID 34732768

tools.name: CAMDA (Concurrence of Active Methylation and De-methylation) — Shi & Li 2021
tools.type: Read-level methylation heterogeneity (concurrence) metric; SHORT-READ bisulfite; region-reported; transcription-regulation focus, not haplotype/somatic-allele resolved (DISTINCT from CAMDAC, a separate CN-aware deconvolution tool)
tools.method_core: DISORDER QUANTITY = within-read co-occurrence of methylated + unmethylated CpGs (a concurrence ratio, distinct from mean and from variance). Dissects each bisulfite read into 3 fragment classes (methylated, unmethylated, 'concurrence' = unmethylated CpGs within partially-methylated reads). Methylation concurrence ratio = (sum of C-fragment weights)/(sum of all fragment weights) per region, reflecting DNMT-vs-TET competition on the same molecule. NOT haplotype-aware.
tools.granularity: Read-level fragment classification, region-level reported.
tools.statistics: Weighted fragment ratio; no clustering/permutation structure test. COVERAGE: coverage-dependent (needs enough partially-methylated reads); no explicit minimum stated.
tools.input: Bisulfite read alignments (BSMAP, short-read).
tools.purpose: Quantify active methylation/demethylation concurrence and link to transcription regulation.
tools.key_claims: Concurrence captures regulatory dynamics that mean/variance methylation miss.
tools.vs_ism: Another within-read disorder/concurrence SCALAR (conceptually related to PDR, enzyme-process-framed). No between-read distance geometry, no subclonal clustering, no PERMANOVA, no haplotype/somatic axis. ISM's structural between-molecule test and LOH/CN-coupled somatic cis-test are absent.
tools.citation: Shi J et al. Nat Commun 2021;12:5285. DOI 10.1038/s41467-021-25521-7. Code: github.com/JiejunShi/CAMDA

tools.name: epiCHAOS — Kelly/Plass 2024
tools.type: SINGLE-CELL epigenomic heterogeneity metric; scATAC/sc-methylation/scChIP/scNMT/scTAM (NOT bulk long-read); per-cell-group score; cancer-applicable, not haplotype/somatic-allele resolved
tools.method_core: DISORDER QUANTITY = cell-to-cell epigenetic dissimilarity within a cell group (between-CELL heterogeneity). From a binarized single-cell (peaks/tiles x cells) matrix per cluster, compute pairwise CHANCE-CORRECTED Jaccard distances between all cells (controls for the proportion of 1s/0s), take the mean pairwise distance per cluster, regression-adjust for genome-wide sparsity/coverage, rescale to 0-1 and invert to a heterogeneity score. NOT haplotype-aware.
tools.granularity: Per cluster / cell-group scalar (can be restricted to region subsets); not per-read, not bulk-molecule.
tools.statistics: Chance-corrected Jaccard pairwise distances + mean + linear-regression sparsity correction; chance-centering. COVERAGE: explicitly sparsity/coverage-corrected via regression to avoid false heterogeneity from coverage differences (deliberate strength for sparse single-cell data).
tools.input: Single-cell epigenomics binarized matrices (scATAC etc.), NOT bulk long reads.
tools.purpose: Quantify intra-population epigenetic heterogeneity across single cells.
tools.key_claims: Chance-corrected Jaccard gives coverage-robust per-cluster heterogeneity; PRC2/CTCF/cohesin sites are heterogeneity hotspots.
tools.vs_ism: Closest in SPIRIT: also uses pairwise (Jaccard) distances + chance correction, parallel to ISM's read x read distance matrix (ISM offers Jaccard among its metrics). BUT epiCHAOS operates BETWEEN SINGLE CELLS (not between reads of one bulk molecule pool), outputs a single per-cluster scalar (no hierarchical clustering into subgroups, no PERMANOVA group-separation test), and is not haplotype/allele-aware or LOH/CN-coupled. ISM's contribution over an epiCHAOS-style mean-distance scalar is the explicit STRUCTURAL TEST (does the distance matrix partition into separated HP/somatic groups, PERMANOVA pseudo-F) plus somatic cis-anchoring.

survey.notes:
VERIFICATION SUMMARY (all from primary sources unless flagged):
- Scherer NAR 2020 (DOI 10.1093/nar/gkaa120) full text FETCHED — authoritative for FDRP/qFDRP/PDR/MHL/epipolymorphism/entropy definitions + the key coverage-sensitivity benchmark (PDR/FDRP increase with coverage; qFDRP/MHL stable; epipoly/entropy computable in only ~70/1000 regions).
- informME BMC Bioinformatics 2018 (PMC5842653) full text FETCHED — NME formula + 1D Ising model + 5-30x coverage. (Foundational PEL paper = Jenkinson Nat Genet 2017, DOI 10.1038/ng.3811.)
- CpelNano Sci Rep 2021 (PMC8566571) full text FETCHED — confirmed ONT LONG-READ, region-level, NME/MML/CMD via Ising+HMM, coverages 5-25x tested, breast cancer demo. Single most platform-comparable tool to ISM.
- epiCHAOS Genome Biol 2024 (PMC11613708) full text FETCHED — chance-corrected Jaccard, single-cell, regression sparsity correction.
- CAMDA GitHub FETCHED + Nat Commun 2021 (DOI 10.1038/s41467-021-25521-7) — concurrence ratio, read-level, BSMAP bisulfite. DISAMBIGUATED from CAMDAC (a separate copy-number-aware tumor methylation DECONVOLUTION tool, biorxiv 2020.11.03.366252 — do NOT conflate).
- Metheor (PLOS Comp Biol 2023, DOI 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1010946) GitHub README FETCHED — modern fast Rust re-implementation of the metric family (PM/PDR/LPMD/MHL/PM-epipolymorphism/ME/FDRP/qFDRP), input = Bismark BISULFITE BAM only (NOT native long-read), default --min-depth 10, --max-depth 40 for FDRP/qFDRP. NOT added as a separate row because it re-implements existing metrics; flagged here as the up-to-date engineering reference, including the up-to-300x speed / 60x memory claim vs original implementations.
- epihet (Sci Rep 2021;11:376, Chen et al., applied to AML CEBPA-silenced) is another implementation vehicle for PDR/epipolymorphism/entropy — noted but not a separate row.
- Landau Cancer Cell 2014 (PMID 25490447, DOI 10.1016/j.ccell.2014.10.012): citation + CLL cancer context + PDR numbers (24.7% vs 17.6%/16.3%, P<0.00001, n=104 CLL/27 normal B) confirmed via PubMed + Broad/Dana-Farber press + Scherer re-derivation. PMC full text was CAPTCHA-BLOCKED, so the PDR ALGORITHM wording is from the Scherer/epihet/Metheor re-implementations, not Landau's own Methods. Marked verified=true on citation/context; algorithm is secondary-sourced.

CENTRAL CONTRAST (DISORDER vs STRUCTURE) — load-bearing positioning point for the paper:
Every tool above reduces molecular methylation variation to a SCALAR disorder/diversity/entropy/concurrence value (per-CpG, per-4CpG-window, per-region, or per-cell-cluster). They answer 'HOW MUCH within-read or within-locus mixing/randomness?' NONE of them: (a) retain a read-to-read distance matrix as geometry, (b) hierarchically cluster reads into subgroups, (c) run a PERMANOVA pseudo-F between-group separation test, or (d) condition on a genetic haplotype/somatic-allele axis with normal-anchored cis-tests holding CN/ploidy constant. ISM's CORE 3 (PERMANOVA) + CORE 6 (NormalBaseline cis-test) + Delta-beta HP-axis (HP1 vs HP1-1 somatic-controlled) are the structural/somatic machinery the entire disorder literature lacks.

TWO CLOSEST COUSINS TO PRE-EMPT IN THE PAPER:
1) qFDRP — uses the SAME normalized-Hamming pairwise read kernel ISM uses (NHD), but averages it to a per-CpG scalar instead of testing structure. Sharpest 'same primitive, different objective' contrast.
2) CpelNano — SAME ONT long-read substrate as ISM, but produces a region-level entropy/energy scalar, not a between-read structural partition. Sharpest 'same data, different question' contrast.
epiCHAOS is the closest in algorithmic SPIRIT (pairwise chance-corrected distances) but operates between single CELLS and still outputs a per-cluster scalar with no group-separation test.

PLATFORM/DOMAIN MAP for a comparison table:
- Long-read/ONT: ONLY CpelNano (region-level entropy). ISM is read-level + structural + haplotype on the same ONT substrate.
- Single-cell: epiCHAOS only.
- Everything else: short-read bisulfite (RRBS/WGBS), bulk.
- Cancer-demonstrated: Landau PDR (CLL), informME/CpelNano (lung/breast), CAMDA, epiCHAOS, epihet (AML) — but NONE are somatic-allele/haplotype resolved the way ISM (tumor-normal paired or tumor-only, HP1-vs-HP1-1 somatic-controlled, LOH/CN-coupled, 5mC AND 5hmC from BAM MM/ML) is.
- Coverage points worth citing: PDR/FDRP increase with coverage (confounded); qFDRP/MHL coverage-stable; epipolymorphism/entropy need 4 CpGs/read and were computable in only ~70/1000 regions (Scherer); informME/CpelNano model-based, usable 5-25x; epiCHAOS regression-corrects sparsity.

survey.category: Methodology survey: quantifying a methylation DIFFERENCE / effect size (delta-beta and its statistical relatives), benchmarked against ISM's per-CpG haplotype Δβ + Wilcoxon signed-rank + Cohen d. Context = ONT long-read CANCER somatic 5mC/5hmC, haplotype-paired, read-level structure. All entries verified from primary sources (paper / Bioconductor / PMC); none from the local KB (KB has no docs on these external statistical methods).

tools.name: Beta-value vs M-value (Du et al. 2010)
tools.type: transform / metric-definition (array + sequencing-agnostic)
tools.method_core: Beta = M_intensity/(M+U+alpha), alpha=100 default -> bounded [0,1], 'fraction methylated'. M-value = log2((M+alpha)/(U+alpha)), alpha=1 -> unbounded real line. The two are related by a Logit/logistic function: Beta = 2^M/(2^M+1); M = log2(Beta/(1-Beta)). Verified exact formulas from PMC.
tools.granularity: per-CpG site-level (probe/locus). Not read-level, not haplotype-aware (array origin).
tools.statistics: Compared detection of group differences by a simple t-test on the two representations; M-value shown to have approximately homoscedastic (constant) variance across the methylation range, Beta-value does not.
tools.input: Illumina HumanMethylation BeadArray intensities (methylated + unmethylated probe pairs); concept generalizes to seq beta = meth_reads/total_reads.
tools.haplotype_aware: No
tools.cancer_somatic: Neither specifically; general methylation quantification (developed on arrays).
tools.vs_ism: ISM's Δβ is a difference of BETA-values (per-CpG mean methylation per haplotype group). Du 2010 is the canonical warning AGAINST testing on raw beta because of heteroscedasticity at the extremes; it recommends testing on M-values and REPORTING beta. ISM tests Δβ with a non-parametric Wilcoxon signed-rank (rank-based -> sidesteps the beta-variance assumption that a t-test would violate) and reports the interpretable mean Δβ + Cohen d. This is a defensible hybrid: report on the interpretable beta scale, test with a distribution-free statistic. Pitfall to note in the paper: still report whether tests were done on beta or M/logit.
tools.key_claims: VERIFIED exact quotes (PMC): 'The standard deviation of Beta-value is greatly compressed in the low (between 0 and 0.2) and high (between 0.8 and 1) ranges... Beta-value has significant heteroscedasticity in the low and high methylation range.' Recommendation (verbatim): 'We recommend using the M-value method for conducting differential methylation analysis and including the Beta-value statistics when reporting the results to investigators.'
tools.purpose: Defines the two effect-size scales for methylation and the statistical reason to prefer the logit/M scale for hypothesis testing while reporting on the beta (delta-beta) scale.
tools.citation: Du P, Zhang X, Huang CC, Jafari N, Kibbe WA, Hou L, Lin SM. BMC Bioinformatics 2010;11:587. DOI:10.1186/1471-2105-11-587. PMID:21118553. PMC3012676.

tools.name: Raw delta-beta (Δβ) + minimum effect-size threshold
tools.type: metric / reporting convention (platform-agnostic)
tools.method_core: Δβ = (mean beta group A) - (mean beta group B), per CpG. Reported alongside a significance test. Widely-used practical biological-relevance filter: |Δβ| >= 0.1 (10 percentage points). methylKit's default percent-methylation-difference filter is the same idea at 25% (>25 percentage points).
tools.granularity: per-CpG site-level; can be aggregated to region (DMR) by averaging.
tools.statistics: No test of its own; Δβ is the EFFECT SIZE that accompanies a p-value from t/Wilcoxon/logistic/beta-binomial. Best-practice literature: report Δβ + CI, do not gate on p alone (statistical vs biological significance).
tools.input: beta/fraction-methylated per group.
tools.haplotype_aware: Only if the two groups are haplotypes (as in ISM HP1 vs HP1-1). Generically it is case-vs-control.
tools.cancer_somatic: Used in both; the 0.1 cutoff comes mostly from array/EWAS short-read.
tools.vs_ism: ISM's Δβ IS exactly this metric, but (a) groups = haplotypes/alleles not case-control, (b) ISM pairs by CpG and applies Wilcoxon signed-rank (paired non-parametric) rather than an unpaired filter, and (c) adds Cohen d as a standardized companion. The |Δβ|>=0.1 / Cohen ribbon convention is the right external yardstick to cite when ISM reports e.g. BRCA2 Δβ = -0.122 (above the 0.1 threshold) vs sub-threshold drift. Note ISM's own memory shows median |Δβ| genome-wide <0.10, i.e. most somatic ASM is below this conventional cutoff -> excess-over-null framing is what carries signal, not raw Δβ.
tools.key_claims: VERIFIED: '|Δβ| >= ±0.1 considered differentially methylated' is a common EWAS convention (search-confirmed, not from a single canonical methods paper - flag as convention not theorem). methylKit default 'q-value <0.01 and %methylation difference >25%' VERIFIED from PMC3491415. Effect-size+CI-over-p best practice VERIFIED (Xie 2019 + general effect-size guidance).
tools.purpose: The interpretable biological effect size; the thing ISM's Δβ should be benchmarked against numerically.
tools.citation: Threshold convention is community practice (no single primary theorem). Anchor reporting norm to Xie et al. 2019 (below) + Du 2010. methylKit 25% default: Akalin 2012 (below).

tools.name: Xie et al. 2019 - reporting Δβ from M-value models
tools.type: methodology / reporting-norm paper (array-oriented, generalizable)
tools.method_core: Resolves the inconsistency in standard practice where investigators SELECT CpGs and get p-values from an M-value (logit) regression but then report Δβ from a SEPARATE beta-value regression. Shows the latter is biased at extremes; gives 'M-model-coef' and 'M-model-M-mean' methods to back-transform a consistent Δβ from the M-value model fit.
tools.granularity: per-CpG site-level.
tools.statistics: Linear regression on M-values for inference; derives Δβ as a back-transformed reported effect size. Demonstrates bias when M not in (-2,2) / beta not in (0.2,0.8).
tools.input: beta and M-value per CpG per sample.
tools.haplotype_aware: No
tools.cancer_somatic: Array/EWAS framing; mechanism-agnostic.
tools.vs_ism: Directly relevant to HOW ISM should report Δβ: it warns that test-scale (logit/M, or rank-based) and report-scale (beta) must be made consistent, and that naive beta-scale estimates are biased exactly where ISM operates (highly meth / unmeth CpGs near 0/1). ISM partly sidesteps this by using Wilcoxon on paired beta differences + Cohen d rather than a beta-scale linear coefficient, but the paper should cite Xie to justify that the reported mean Δβ is an honest effect size and acknowledge extreme-value bias.
tools.key_claims: VERIFIED quotes: beta-value 'much more biologically interpretable... corresponds roughly to the percentage of a site that is methylated'; 'Δβ directly obtained from β-value linear regression model can give very biased results, especially when M-values are not in (−2, 2) or β-values are not in (0.2, 0.8).' Authors: Xie C, Leung YK, Chen A, Long DX, Hoyo C, Ho SM. Does NOT recommend a numeric threshold.
tools.purpose: Best-practice for reporting a consistent, unbiased delta-beta when significance is assessed on the logit/M scale.
tools.citation: Xie C, et al. 'Differential methylation values in differential methylation analysis.' Bioinformatics 2019;35(7):1094-1099. DOI:10.1093/bioinformatics/bty778.

tools.name: BSmooth (Hansen, Langmead, Irizarry 2012; bsseq)
tools.type: smoothed regional methylation-difference + signal-to-noise t-statistic (SHORT-READ WGBS)
tools.method_core: Local-likelihood smoothing of the methylation profile: within a window (default 70 CpGs, min 2 kb) fit a 2nd-degree polynomial to logit(f(l)) via a weighted GLM, weights inversely proportional to standard errors, tricube kernel in genomic distance. Produces a smoothed methylation estimate even at low coverage.
tools.granularity: region-level (DMR) from smoothed per-CpG estimates; SITE-LEVEL smoothing -> regional calls. Not read-level, not haplotype-aware natively.
tools.statistics: BSmooth.tstat = signal-to-noise t-statistic t(l) = beta_hat(l) / [ sigma_hat(l) * sqrt(1/n1 + 1/n2) ], beta_hat = smoothed group difference, sigma_hat = smoothed across-replicate SD. DMRs = runs of consecutive CpGs with t > c or t < -c (cutoff from the marginal t distribution); CpGs >300 bp apart cannot join. REQUIRES biological replicates.
tools.input: WGBS methylated/total counts per CpG per sample, multiple replicates per group.
tools.haplotype_aware: No
tools.cancer_somatic: Designed for group-vs-group (developed on tissue/normal); not somatic-caller-aware.
tools.vs_ism: Contrast in philosophy. BSmooth smooths the methylation LEVEL spatially along the genome and tests a per-position SMOOTHED-difference t-statistic across REPLICATES -> it answers 'is the average methylation level shifted in this region'. ISM has no biological replicates (single tumor, two haplotypes within one sample) so the BSmooth replicate-variance denominator does not apply; ISM instead derives its 'noise' from a HP-shuffle null / NormalBaseline residual and tests STRUCTURE (PERMANOVA on a read-to-read distance matrix), not a smoothed mean. Cite BSmooth as the canonical 'low-coverage -> smooth before testing' answer and explain ISM's null-permutation substitute for the missing replicate variance.
tools.key_claims: VERIFIED (PMC3491411): 70-CpG/2kb window, 2nd-degree polynomial weighted GLM, tricube weights; t = beta_hat/(sigma_hat*sqrt(1/n1+1/n2)); DMRs = consecutive CpGs all |t|>c; 300 bp join limit; requires replicates ('regions that are inherently variable can easily be confused with regions that differ consistently between groups when few replicates are available'); short-read WGBS, ~4x coverage usable after smoothing.
tools.purpose: Low-coverage-robust regional differential methylation via spatial smoothing + replicate-based signal-to-noise.
tools.citation: Hansen KD, Langmead B, Irizarry RA. Genome Biology 2012;13(10):R83. DOI:10.1186/gb-2012-13-10-r83. PMID:23034175. PMC3491411. Bioconductor pkg: bsseq.

tools.name: DSS - dispersion-shrunken beta-binomial Wald (Feng/Conneely/Wu 2014; Park/Wu 2016)
tools.type: per-CpG beta-binomial test on COUNT data (SHORT-READ BS-seq)
tools.method_core: Models methylated counts as lognormal-beta-binomial hierarchical: M_ijk ~ Binomial(n, p), p ~ Beta(mu, phi); a LOG-NORMAL PRIOR on the dispersion phi enables empirical-Bayes SHRINKAGE of per-CpG dispersion (borrowing strength across sites). Without replicates, neighboring CpGs are treated as pseudo-replicates via moving-average smoothing so dispersion is still estimable.
tools.granularity: per-CpG DML; DMRs assembled by callDMR (min length, min #CpG, % significant, then merge). Site-level / count-based, not read-level, not haplotype-aware.
tools.statistics: WALD TEST per CpG on the beta-binomial mean difference, with the variance driven by the shrunken dispersion AND coverage depth. CONFIRMED there is NO arcsine link function in the original DSS DML paper (that is a confusion with a different beta-binomial regression tool). General-design extension (Park & Wu 2016) adds a beta-binomial regression / GLM with arcsine-transformed responses for arbitrary covariates - distinct from the 2014 DML test.
tools.input: BS-seq (meth, total) counts per CpG per sample; works with or without replicates.
tools.haplotype_aware: No (but it IS the engine NanoMethPhase calls for allele DMA - see below).
tools.cancer_somatic: Generic group comparison; not somatic-caller-aware.
tools.vs_ism: This is the rigorous count-based answer to the SAME instability problem ISM faces at low haplotype coverage: DSS shrinks per-CpG dispersion and folds coverage into the Wald variance, so a Δβ from 6 reads is down-weighted vs one from 60. ISM currently uses a non-parametric Wilcoxon on per-CpG mean differences + Cohen d, which does NOT explicitly model count overdispersion or weight by depth. Strong methods-section move: cite DSS as the gold-standard for 'how a difference between two read groups should be tested when coverage is uneven', and either (a) justify why ISM's rank-based + permutation approach is adequate for read-level structure, or (b) note DSS-style beta-binomial weighting as future work. Also: NanoMethPhase (long-read ASM) literally delegates its allele DMA to DSS.
tools.key_claims: VERIFIED (PMC4005660 + Bioconductor DSS guide): 'lognormal-beta-binomial hierarchical model'; 'a log-normal prior is imposed on the dispersion parameters... shrinkage estimation of the dispersion parameters'; 'A Wald test is developed for hypothesis testing at each CpG site'; without replicates 'neighboring CpG sites can be viewed as pseudo-replicates' via moving average; NO arcsine link in the 2014 DML model (confirmed by direct fetch).
tools.purpose: Coverage-aware, overdispersion-aware per-CpG differential methylation; the canonical beta-binomial Wald baseline.
tools.citation: Feng H, Conneely KN, Wu H. Nucleic Acids Res 2014;42(8):e69. DOI:10.1093/nar/gku154. PMID:24561809. PMC4005660. General design: Park Y, Wu H. Bioinformatics 2016;32(10):1446-1453. DOI:10.1093/bioinformatics/btw026.

tools.name: methylKit (Akalin et al. 2012) - logistic regression / Fisher exact
tools.type: per-base & per-region differential methylation (SHORT-READ RRBS/WGBS)
tools.method_core: Models per-base methylation proportion P_i with LOGISTIC REGRESSION (methylated vs unmethylated read counts ~ group) when >=1 sample per group with replicates; falls back to FISHER'S EXACT TEST comparing fraction of methylated Cs when there is only ONE sample per group. Reports percent-methylation-difference as the effect size.
tools.granularity: per-base CpG AND per-region (user regions or tiling windows). Site/region-level, not read-level, not haplotype-aware.
tools.statistics: Logistic regression null H0: beta1=0; OR Fisher exact (single sample/group). Multiple testing via SLIM (sliding linear model) -> q-values. Default call filter: q<0.01 AND %methylation difference >25%. (Optional overdispersion correction added in later versions; not in the 2012 paper.)
tools.input: Bisulfite/RRBS per-base counts (numCs, numTs) per sample.
tools.haplotype_aware: No
tools.cancer_somatic: Generic; widely used in cancer EWAS but mechanism-agnostic.
tools.vs_ism: methylKit's single-sample-per-group Fisher exact on (meth, unmeth) counts is the closest classical analogue to ISM's per-CpG Fisher exact + BH-FDR (ISM CORE 4, the 'disorder' contrast family). The key divergence: methylKit's effect size is a per-site %methylation difference (a Δβ in percent), tested per site; ISM additionally builds a read-to-read distance matrix + PERMANOVA to test STRUCTURE rather than only per-site mean shift. When the paper says 'ISM does per-CpG Fisher exact', cite methylKit as the standard implementation of exactly that test, and position ISM's PERMANOVA/clustering as the extra read-level structural layer methylKit lacks.
tools.key_claims: VERIFIED (PMC3491415): logistic regression vs Fisher exact selection rule ('If there are multiple samples per group... logistic regression... Otherwise, when there is one sample per group, Fisher's exact test'); SLIM -> q-values; default 'q-value <0.01 and %methylation difference >25%'; per-base + tiling windows; RRBS/bisulfite short-read.
tools.purpose: Standard short-read per-base/region differential methylation with Fisher/logistic + percent-difference effect size.
tools.citation: Akalin A, Kormaksson M, Li S, Garrett-Bakelman FE, Figueroa ME, Melnick A, Mason CE. Genome Biology 2012;13(10):R87. DOI:10.1186/gb-2012-13-10-r87. PMID:23034086. PMC3491415.

tools.name: limma moderated-t on M-values (Smyth 2004; eBayes)
tools.type: empirical-Bayes linear model on logit/M-values (ARRAY-origin; applied to seq M-values)
tools.method_core: Fit a linear model per CpG to M-values; eBayes shrinks the per-CpG residual variances toward a common value (empirical Bayes), producing a MODERATED t-statistic with augmented degrees of freedom. Effect size = the model coefficient on the M scale (back-transform to Δβ per Xie 2019).
tools.granularity: per-CpG site-level; designed for arrays, also used on WGBS/EPIC M-values. Not read-level, not haplotype-aware.
tools.statistics: Moderated t = coefficient / shrunken-SE; borrows variance information across CpGs (the variance-shrinkage analogue of what DSS does for dispersion). Requires replicates for the variance model.
tools.input: M-value matrix (CpG x sample); typically EPIC/450k arrays.
tools.haplotype_aware: No
tools.cancer_somatic: Generic EWAS; widely used in cancer cohorts.
tools.vs_ism: limma is the variance-shrinkage gold standard on the CONTINUOUS logit scale, complementary to DSS's dispersion shrinkage on COUNTS. Both solve 'few replicates -> unstable variance' by borrowing strength across CpGs. ISM has no biological replicates, so limma's eBayes denominator (across-sample residual variance) is not directly available; ISM substitutes a HP-shuffle permutation null. Cite limma in the methods to acknowledge that the field stabilizes the per-CpG variance estimate before testing - and state that ISM's permutation/PERMANOVA pseudo-F is its replicate-free substitute.
tools.key_claims: VERIFIED (concept, Smyth 2004 + limma docs): 'empirical Bayes... squeezes the genewise residual variances towards a common value, and the degrees of freedom for the individual variances are increased.' Application to methylation M-values is standard practice (Du 2010 + Xie 2019 recommend M-scale modeling). NOTE: not fetched from the primary 2004 SAGMB paper full text - concept verified via limma official docs and secondary; mark the 2004 citation as concept-verified, exact-quote UNVERIFIED.
tools.purpose: Variance-shrunken differential methylation testing on the M/logit scale; the array-side counterpart to DSS.
tools.citation: Smyth GK. 'Linear models and empirical Bayes methods for assessing differential expression in microarray experiments.' Stat Appl Genet Mol Biol 2004;3:Article3. DOI:10.2202/1544-6115.1027. PMID:16646809. (limma Bioconductor package.)

tools.name: Arcsine sqrt vs logit transform for proportions (Warton & Hui 2011)
tools.type: variance-stabilizing transform debate (general statistics)
tools.method_core: Two classical variance-stabilizing transforms for a proportion p: arcsine(sqrt(p)) (asymptotic SD = sigma/(2*sqrt(p(1-p)))) and logit(p)=log(p/(1-p)). Warton & Hui argue arcsine 'is asinine' and that for binomial/proportion data one should prefer logistic (GLM/logit) modeling, checking and accounting for overdispersion via random effects.
tools.granularity: applies to any proportion (per-CpG beta is a proportion). Transform-level, not a tool.
tools.statistics: Arcsine stabilizes variance to depend only on n (no continuity correction needed) but breaks under extra-binomial overdispersion; logit + GLM has higher power and interpretability. This is the theoretical backbone of WHY Du 2010 / limma / DSS work on logit/M rather than raw beta.
tools.input: any proportion / fraction-methylated.
tools.haplotype_aware: No
tools.cancer_somatic: n/a (general)
tools.vs_ism: Provides the first-principles justification for the heteroscedasticity ISM must handle: raw beta differences (Δβ) have mean-dependent variance, smallest near 0 and 1 where most CpGs sit. ISM's choice of a RANK-based Wilcoxon signed-rank (no variance-homogeneity assumption) is a legitimate third option alongside arcsine/logit. The paper should state explicitly: 'we report Δβ on the interpretable beta scale but test with a distribution-free signed-rank statistic, avoiding both the heteroscedasticity of a beta t-test (Du 2010, Warton & Hui 2011) and the interpretability loss of testing on the logit scale.' That is a clean, defensible methodological stance.
tools.key_claims: VERIFIED: arcsine asymptotic SD = sigma/(2*sqrt(p(1-p))); Warton & Hui recommend logit/GLM over arcsine ('the arcsine is asinine'); arcsine fails under overdispersion (litter-to-litter / biological overdispersion). Source: Warton & Hui, Ecology 2011.
tools.purpose: Theoretical basis for transforming proportions before testing; explains beta heteroscedasticity at extremes.
tools.citation: Warton DI, Hui FKC. 'The arcsine is asinine: the analysis of proportions in ecology.' Ecology 2011;92(1):3-10. DOI:10.1890/10-0340.1. PMID:21560670.

tools.name: Allele-specific methylation difference - CPEL / Ising model (Abante et al. 2020)
tools.type: read-level haplotype/allele methylation-pattern difference (SHORT-READ WGBS)
tools.method_core: Models the joint methylation PATTERN across linked CpGs within a haplotype using a 1-D Ising (correlated potential energy landscape, CPEL) model; maximum-likelihood fit by simulated annealing. Compares two homologous alleles via three effect sizes: MML (mean methylation level) imbalance, NME (normalized methylation entropy) difference, and JSD (Jensen-Shannon distance) between the two alleles' pattern distributions. Significance via bootstrap-based empirical one-sided hypothesis test.
tools.granularity: READ-LEVEL, multi-CpG joint pattern within haplotype (NOT independent per-CpG). Allele/haplotype-aware by construction.
tools.statistics: Likelihood-based pattern model + bootstrap empirical null; reliable at low coverage (good at 10-50 reads). Effect sizes are distributional (MML/NME/JSD), not a single Δβ.
tools.input: Short-read WGBS reads spanning SNP + multiple CpGs, partitioned by allele.
tools.haplotype_aware: Yes (core design)
tools.cancer_somatic: Germline / imprinting focus (ICRs, imprinted genes); NOT cancer somatic.
tools.vs_ism: This is the closest conceptual sibling to ISM and the single most important external comparator. SHARED idea: methylation is a read-level MULTI-CpG PATTERN, not just a per-site mean; both compare two haplotypes' pattern DISTRIBUTIONS. ISM's NME and epipolymorphism (CORE 4) map almost 1:1 onto CPEL's NME; ISM's PERMANOVA/distance-matrix structure test parallels CPEL's JSD between allele distributions; ISM's Δβ parallels CPEL's MML imbalance. KEY DIFFERENCES to claim in the paper: (1) ISM is ONT LONG-READ (one read natively spans many CpGs - no Ising reconstruction of linkage needed), CPEL is short-read WGBS (must model linkage statistically); (2) ISM targets CANCER SOMATIC haplotypes (HP1 vs HP1-1, NormalBaseline-residualized, LOH/CN-coupled), CPEL targets GERMLINE IMPRINTING; (3) ISM uses distance-matrix + UPGMA clustering + PERMANOVA pseudo-F, CPEL uses an explicit Ising generative model. So ISM = 'CPEL-class read-level allele pattern analysis, ported to long-read somatic cancer with a non-parametric structural engine'. This framing is publishable positioning.
tools.key_claims: VERIFIED (PMC7567826): tool = 'correlated potential energy landscape (CPEL) method'; '1-D Ising model of statistical physics'; three metrics MML/NME/JSD; 'reliably, even at low coverage' (10-50 reads); imprinting/ICR focus; short-read WGBS; read-level joint pattern.
tools.purpose: Read-level, multi-CpG, allele-specific methylation difference with distributional effect sizes - the methodological mirror of ISM in the germline/short-read world.
tools.citation: Abante J, Fang Y, Feinberg AP, Goutsias J. 'Detection of haplotype-dependent allele-specific DNA methylation in WGBS data.' Nature Communications 2020;11:5238. DOI:10.1038/s41467-020-19077-1. PMID:33067453. PMC7567826.

tools.name: NanoMethPhase - long-read haplotype methylation ASM (Akbari et al. 2021)
tools.type: long-read phased methylation + allele DMA (LONG-READ NANOPORE)
tools.method_core: Phases 5mC nanopore reads to two haplotypes using SNVs (Clair calls, SNVoter filter, min base quality 7, haplotype ratio 0.75), then runs differential methylation analysis between the two haplotypes by DELEGATING TO THE DSS R PACKAGE to call mono-allelic methylated regions.
tools.granularity: region-level ASM (mono-allelic methylated regions) from read-phased per-CpG; haplotype-aware.
tools.statistics: Statistics are DSS's beta-binomial dispersion-shrunken Wald (it does not invent its own test). Works at ~10x coverage.
tools.input: ONT long reads with 5mC calls + SNVs for phasing.
tools.haplotype_aware: Yes
tools.cancer_somatic: Germline / imprinting focus (detected 42 novel imprinted regions in normal cell lines); NOT cancer somatic.
tools.vs_ism: The most direct LONG-READ comparator and the right citation for 'what other people do with ONT haplotype methylation'. SAME platform (ONT long-read), SAME phasing-then-compare-haplotypes skeleton as ISM. CRITICAL contrasts for the paper: (1) NanoMethPhase outsources its difference test to DSS (per-CpG beta-binomial Wald, site-level mean shift) - ISM instead computes a read-to-read DISTANCE MATRIX + PERMANOVA structural test plus Δβ/Wilcoxon, i.e. ISM tests between-molecule ORGANIZATION not just per-site mean; (2) NanoMethPhase is built for GERMLINE imprinting, ISM is built for CANCER SOMATIC (NormalBaseline residual, normal-anchored cis-test separating somatic vs cis vs drift, LOH/CN coupling) - that somatic-control machinery is ISM's novelty and NanoMethPhase has no analogue; (3) both use ~10x-feasible coverage. Position: 'long-read ASM exists (NanoMethPhase) but uses germline imprinting logic + a per-site DSS test; ISM adds somatic controls + a read-level structural test'.
tools.key_claims: VERIFIED (PMC7898412): 'It uses the DSS R package for DMA'; phasing via Clair+SNVoter, min base quality 7, haplotype ratio 0.75; '~10x' coverage; imprinting focus (42 novel imprinted regions); ONT long-read.
tools.purpose: Long-read phased ASM detection; shows the field's standard long-read haplotype-methylation comparison delegates effect testing to DSS.
tools.citation: Akbari V, Garant JM, O'Neill K, et al. 'Megabase-scale methylation phasing using nanopore long reads and NanoMethPhase.' Genome Biology 2021;22:68. DOI:10.1186/s13059-021-02283-5. PMID:33618748. PMC7898412.

tools.name: Cohen's d (paired d_z) effect-size reporting norm
tools.type: standardized effect-size convention (general statistics)
tools.method_core: Standardized mean difference = mean difference / SD. Paired form d_z = mean(paired differences) / SD(differences) - exactly what pairs with a Wilcoxon signed-rank / paired test. Benchmarks: d=0.2 small, 0.5 medium, 0.8 large.
tools.granularity: summary statistic over the paired per-CpG Δβ set; not spatial.
tools.statistics: Unit-free; complements (does not replace) the p-value. For rank tests an alternative is r = Z/sqrt(n).
tools.input: paired per-CpG methylation differences (the Δβ vector).
tools.haplotype_aware: n/a
tools.cancer_somatic: n/a (general)
tools.vs_ism: ISM reports Cohen d alongside mean Δβ and Wilcoxon signed-rank - this matches best practice (report magnitude + precision, not just p). Since ISM pairs by CpG, the correct flavor is the PAIRED d_z (mean of CpG-wise differences / SD of those differences), and the paper should say so explicitly to avoid the common ambiguity between pooled-SD d and paired d_z. The 0.2/0.5/0.8 ribbon is the standard interpretive scale to put on ISM's reported d values. Best-practice literature also asks for a CI on Δβ - recommend ISM add a bootstrap/normal CI on the mean Δβ next to d.
tools.key_claims: VERIFIED: paired Cohen's d_z = mean paired difference / SD of differences; benchmarks 0.2/0.5/0.8 (Cohen). Wilcoxon effect size r = Z/sqrt(n). Effect-size+CI > p-value-alone is consensus reporting guidance.
tools.purpose: Standardized effect-size + interpretive thresholds to accompany Δβ and the rank test.
tools.citation: Cohen J. 'Statistical Power Analysis for the Behavioral Sciences' (2nd ed, 1988). Paired d_z: Lakens D. Front Psychol 2013;4:863. DOI:10.3389/fpsyg.2013.00863.

survey.notes:
VERIFICATION STATUS: 10/11 entries fully verified from PRIMARY sources via WebFetch of the paper/PMC/Bioconductor. Two flags: (1) limma 2004 SAGMB - eBayes/moderated-t concept verified via limma official Bioconductor docs and Du/Xie corroboration, but the exact 2004 primary-paper full text was NOT fetched -> citation is concept-verified, exact-quote UNVERIFIED. (2) The |Δβ|>=0.1 cutoff is a COMMUNITY CONVENTION (search-confirmed as widely used) with NO single canonical primary theorem - do not cite it as a derived threshold; methylKit's 25% default IS primary-verified.

CORRECTED ERROR: an early WebSearch snippet claimed DSS uses an 'arcsine link function'. Direct fetch of the DSS NAR 2014 paper (PMC4005660) CONFIRMED this is FALSE - the 2014 DML model is a lognormal-beta-binomial hierarchical model with a Wald test and NO arcsine link. (Arcsine-transformed response appears in the SEPARATE Park & Wu 2016 general-design GLM and in methylSig-style beta-binomial regression - do not attribute it to the core DSS DML test.)

KEY SYNTHESIS FOR THE PAPER (ISM positioning):
1. Two-axis taxonomy of external methods. AXIS A = effect-size SCALE & test: raw Δβ (interpretable, heteroscedastic - Du 2010, Warton-Hui) vs logit/M (limma eBayes moderated-t) vs count beta-binomial (DSS Wald, dispersion-shrunken; methylKit logistic/Fisher) vs rank-based (ISM's Wilcoxon signed-rank). AXIS B = granularity: per-CpG site (Du/limma/DSS/methylKit) vs smoothed region (BSmooth) vs READ-LEVEL multi-CpG PATTERN (CPEL/Abante, and ISM).
2. ISM's true peers are CPEL (Abante 2020) and NanoMethPhase (Akbari 2021) - the only read-level/haplotype-aware methods. BUT both are GERMLINE IMPRINTING + (CPEL) SHORT-READ / (NanoMethPhase) delegates testing to per-site DSS. ISM is the only one that is (a) ONT long-read, (b) CANCER SOMATIC with NormalBaseline-residual + normal-anchored cis-test, AND (c) tests STRUCTURE via PERMANOVA on a read-to-read distance matrix rather than per-site mean shift. That triad is the defensible novelty claim.
3. The replicate problem. limma (variance shrinkage on M) and DSS (dispersion shrinkage on counts) both solve 'unstable per-CpG variance with few replicates' by borrowing strength across CpGs; BSmooth solves it by spatial smoothing + replicate SD. ISM has NO biological replicates (single tumor, within-sample haplotypes) so it substitutes a HP-shuffle permutation null + PERMANOVA pseudo-F. The paper should state this substitution explicitly as the answer to the reviewer question 'where is your variance/null model'.
4. Reporting recommendations to adopt (all primary-sourced): (a) report Δβ on the interpretable beta scale (Du 2010 / Xie 2019) but justify testing with a distribution-free signed-rank to dodge beta heteroscedasticity at extremes (Warton-Hui); (b) state Cohen's d is the PAIRED d_z and put the 0.2/0.5/0.8 ribbon on it; (c) ADD a CI (bootstrap) on mean Δβ next to d - current ISM reports d but a CI on Δβ is the missing best-practice piece; (d) acknowledge low-coverage instability of Δβ (binomial sampling at few reads) and report min-coverage (ISM uses min common CpG=5; consider stating a min per-haplotype read depth, as DSS/NanoMethPhase use ~10x).
5. PITFALL most relevant to ISM's own data: ISM memory shows genome-wide median |Δβ| < 0.10, i.e. BELOW the conventional 0.1 biological-relevance cutoff; raw Δβ alone would call almost nothing 'relevant'. ISM's excess-over-HP-shuffle-null framing is what rescues signal - the paper must lead with the null-relative effect, not raw Δβ magnitude, exactly because the conventional threshold (methylKit 25%, EWAS 10%) would reject most somatic ASM as too small.

deep.tool: ONT modkit v0.4.x — `modkit dmr` (subcommands `pair` / `multi`) and `modkit entropy`. Long-read (ONT mod-BAM, MM/ML tags), reference-anchored. Designed primarily for germline/general 5mC|5hmC vs C differential methylation and epiallele randomness; NOT a cancer-specific or tumor-normal-paired tool, NOT short-read/array. Region-level (DMR) or within-read/within-window (entropy); haplotype handling is done UPSTREAM in `modkit pileup`, not inside `dmr`/`entropy`.
deep.method_detail:
=== modkit dmr — EXACT method (all verbatim-confirmed from primary docs) ===

INPUT: two or more bedMethyl files produced by `modkit pileup` (must be bgzip-compressed + tabix-indexed). dmr operates on AGGREGATED per-genomic-position counts (methylated count / valid coverage), NOT on individual reads. Subcommands: `pair` (two conditions A vs B; single sites if `--regions/-r` omitted, or regions if BED given) and `multi` (all pairwise comparisons across ≥3 samples; regions only; needs `-o` output dir + per-sample names).

CORE STATISTIC (verbatim): score = log( l_{θa}(X_a) · l_{θb}(X_b) / l_{θ_{a+b}}(X_{a+b}) ). This is a LOG MARGINAL LIKELIHOOD RATIO comparing two models: (model 1) the two conditions a,b have separate methylation parameters θa, θb; (model 2) they share one joint parameter θ_{a+b}. Positive score = data better explained by the two groups differing.

PROBABILITY MODEL (verbatim):
- Binary case (5mC vs C, or 6mA vs A): "we use the binomial distribution and model the probability of methylation p as a beta-distributed random variable" → BETA-BINOMIAL marginal likelihood.
- Multi-state case (e.g. 5hmC, 5mC, unmodified C ≥3 states): "we use a multinomial distribution and a Dirichlet as the base distribution" → DIRICHLET-MULTINOMIAL.
