PRIOR (verbatim): "For all cases, we use Jeffrey's prior as the prior distribution." (Beta(1/2,1/2) / symmetric Dirichlet(1/2)). The l_θ are MARGINAL likelihoods (parameters integrated out under the conjugate prior), i.e. a Bayes-factor-style ratio — NOT a frequentist GLRT with plug-in MLEs.

SIGNIFICANCE / MULTIPLE TESTING:
- The likelihood-ratio score itself gives magnitude+direction but (verbatim from intro) "does not directly provide p-values."
- A separate MAP-based p-value is offered, but ONLY for binary modification and ONLY in `pair` single-site mode; verbatim cap: "The MAP-based p-value calculation has a maximum coverage of 100 reads since it becomes unstable when the number of trials per condition grows beyond this number" (reads subsampled/capped at 100/condition). It uses empirical effect size d = p̂1 − p̂2.
- Cohen's h (verbatim) "more robust to high counts ... a measure of changes in the proportion of modification of any type," reported with 95% CIs for regions/segments.
- NO Benjamini–Hochberg / FDR / genome-wide multiple-testing correction is described anywhere in the official scoring page (UNVERIFIED that any exists; user must apply their own BH externally).

REGION AGGREGATION: how per-site scores combine into a region score is NOT explicitly documented on the official scoring page (states only that the method applies "for every region provided"). Mark as DOC-GAP.

HAPLOTYPE PARTITION (--haplotype): dmr has NO native haplotype logic. Partitioning is done upstream: `modkit pileup --partition-tag HP` emits one bedMethyl per HP tag value (e.g. haplotyped_1.bed / haplotyped_2.bed), or `modkit pileup --phased` emits hp1.bedmethyl + hp2.bedmethyl + combined.bedmethyl. You then feed hp1 vs hp2 bedMethyl into `dmr pair` as condition a vs b. So "HP1 vs HP2 ASM" in modkit = pileup-splits-by-HP → dmr-treats-them-as-two-conditions. There is no somatic/germline awareness and no tumor-normal anchoring.

=== modkit entropy — EXACT method ===
FORMULA (verbatim): ME = −(1/N) Σ_N Pr(n_i) · log₂ Pr(n_i). Verbatim: "N is the set of all methylation patterns and Pr(n_i) is the empirical probability of that pattern." Shannon entropy, log base 2, over the empirical distribution of observed methylation PATTERNS (epialleles). (Note: doc literally says N is the set of patterns; it does NOT state a 1/num_positions normalization to [0,1], does NOT call it 'NME', does NOT give a 2^num_positions bound — those are UNVERIFIED.)
WHAT A PATTERN IS (verbatim): "modkit entropy looks at the co-occurrence of methylation status on individual reads" — i.e. WITHIN-MOLECULE/WITHIN-READ. A pattern is the joint modification state across `--num-positions` modified positions on one read, e.g. m*mm (m=5mC, *=filtered). Implementation uses a prefix trie over patterns present in the reads.
PARAMETERS (verbatim defaults): `--num-positions` default 4 ("Number of modified positions to consider at a time"); `--window-size` default 50 ("Maximum length interval that 'num_positions' modified bases can occur in") — i.e. the 4 CpGs must fall within ≤50 bp; `--regions` for descriptive stats; `--motif` (repeatable; v0.4.2+ multi-motif/multi-primary-base); `--ref` FASTA.
OUTPUT: per-window bedGraph (chrom,start,end,entropy,num_reads) by default; with `--regions` adds per-region summary (mean/median/min/max entropy + read counts + window counts). So entropy = WITHIN-MOLECULE disorder/randomness of epialleles per window; it is NOT a between-sample test, has NO p-value, NO haplotype logic.
CITATIONS (verbatim): metric originally proposed by Xie et al.; methodology follows Lee et al. 2022 (DOI 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1010946).
deep.vs_ism_detailed:
POINT-BY-POINT vs ISM cores 1-6 + Δβ (ISM facts from source-verified InterSubMod/docs/method_comparison/20260609_ism_vs_external_methylation_tools/01_ism_method_spec_from_source.md):

AXIS — what is measured:
- modkit dmr: BETWEEN-SAMPLE/BETWEEN-CONDITION difference in the per-position METHYLATION RATE (β). It is a rate-difference engine on aggregated pileup counts.
- modkit entropy: WITHIN-MOLECULE RANDOMNESS of epiallele patterns (disorder/PDR-family).
- ISM cores 1-3: BETWEEN-MOLECULE STRUCTURE — does the read↔read distance space separate by HP/somatic labels. ISM explicitly measures who-clusters-with-whom, not rate and not within-read disorder.
→ dmr ≈ ISM's β-RATE family (core 6's Δβ + core 4a Fisher per-CpG); entropy ≈ ISM's core 4b NME / 4c epipolymorphism (the within-read disorder metrics ISM deliberately re-implements for contrast). NEITHER modkit tool touches ISM's distinctive structural axis (cores 1-3).

CORE 1 (read-read distance matrix, NHD, C_min=5): NO modkit analog. dmr never builds a read×read distance matrix (it collapses reads to per-position counts in pileup). entropy looks at single reads independently, never read-vs-read distance. This is ISM's most distinctive primitive — UNIQUE to ISM among these two tools.

CORE 2 (hierarchical UPGMA subclonal clustering + silhouette k=2..10): NO modkit analog. modkit has no clustering of reads into subclones.

CORE 3 (PERMANOVA pseudo-F, 999 perms, on the distance matrix; + dispersion ANOVA-F; LabelTest Δ=d_between−d_within): NO modkit analog. modkit's significance is parametric Bayesian (Beta-Binomial marginal LR; MAP p-value) on counts, NOT a permutation test on a distance matrix. ISM's permutation framework is non-parametric over labels; modkit's is model-based over counts. Conceptually different null.

CORE 4 (per-CpG ASM disorder triple): 
- 4a Fisher exact + BH-FDR per CpG → CLOSEST modkit-dmr analog conceptually (both ask "is methylation different between two groups at a site"), BUT modkit uses Beta-Binomial likelihood-ratio + MAP p-value (no BH), ISM uses Fisher + explicit Benjamini-Hochberg. ISM applies BH; modkit ships NO multiple-testing correction.
- 4b NME (normalized methylation entropy, Jenkinson/CPEL 2020) and 4c epipolymorphism (methclone/Metheor) → DIRECT analog of modkit ENTROPY (both = within-read Shannon-type epiallele disorder). Difference: modkit entropy default 4 positions/≤50bp window, log2, per-window+per-region descriptive; ISM's NME/epipoly are 4-CpG sliding-window re-implementations cited to the same literature lineage. So modkit entropy and ISM core 4b/4c are measuring the same construct.

CORE 5 (Cramér's V global HP×methylation association + Cochran min-expected-cell≥5 reliability gate): NO modkit analog. modkit has no global association-strength statistic with a sparse-table reliability gate; it works site-by-site / region-by-region.

CORE 6 + Δβ (NormalBaseline residual = raw − per-CpG normal mean; normal-anchored cis-test d_somatic/d_cis/d_drift; copy-partition; HP-axis HP1 vs HP1-1 somatic-controlled; ALLELE-axis ALT vs REF; 5mC/5hmC max-collapse; Wilcoxon signed-rank + Cohen's d on paired per-CpG β):
- Δβ (mean β_som − β_germ across paired CpGs) is the SAME QUANTITY modkit dmr's empirical effect size d = p̂1 − p̂2 estimates, and modkit's Cohen's h is the variance-stabilized cousin of ISM's Cohen's d on β. So dmr ≈ ISM Δβ at the per-site rate level.
- BUT modkit dmr has NO tumor-normal NormalBaseline subtraction, NO normal-anchored 3-way cis-test (it only compares the two bedMethyl files you give it; it cannot distinguish somatic cis-driven ASM from germline drift), NO copy-partition confound decomposition, and treats HP1 vs HP2 as two opaque "conditions" with no somatic-allele (HP1-1) reconstruction. ISM's core-6 cancer machinery (germline-controlled HP-axis, cis vs drift, copy-controlled d_within) is ENTIRELY ABSENT from modkit.

OVERLAP SUMMARY: modkit dmr overlaps ISM's β-rate/effect-size layer (Δβ, Cohen's d↔h, per-site difference); modkit entropy overlaps ISM's within-read disorder layer (NME/epipolymorphism, core 4b/4c). ISM's read↔read distance + subclonal clustering + PERMANOVA structure test (cores 1-3) and its cancer-specific normal-anchored cis/copy decomposition (core 6) have NO equivalent in either modkit command.
deep.strengths: modkit dmr/entropy strengths relative to ISM: (1) Principled conjugate-Bayesian model — Beta-Binomial / Dirichlet-Multinomial marginal-likelihood ratio with Jeffreys prior naturally handles low-coverage shrinkage and multi-state (5mC+5hmC+C jointly) better than ISM's binarized (>0.8/<0.2) per-CpG Fisher. (2) Native multi-state modelling: dmr scores 5hmC+5mC+C simultaneously via Dirichlet-Multinomial; ISM mostly max-collapses 5mC/5hmC into 'any-mod', losing the 5hmC/5mC distinction at the difference step. (3) `multi` does all-pairwise across many samples out of the box (cross-sample). (4) entropy gives a clean, literature-standard (Xie/Lee2022) within-read Shannon entropy with a defined window model (num-positions=4, ≤50bp) and per-region descriptive summaries — turnkey vs ISM's bespoke C++. (5) Both run directly off standard bedMethyl/mod-BAM, are widely adopted, maintained, and citable; haplotype splitting via pileup --partition-tag/--phased is robust and standard. (6) Cohen's h is high-count-robust (ISM's Δβ/Cohen's d can be unstable at saturating coverage).
deep.limitations: modkit dmr/entropy limitations for OUR context (ONT long-read CANCER somatic ASM): (1) dmr operates on AGGREGATED per-position pileup counts — it cannot see read-level co-structure (no read×read distance, no subclonal clustering). It answers 'is the rate different' not 'are there structurally distinct methyl-subclones'. (2) NO tumor-normal anchoring: dmr compares only the two bedMethyl files given; it cannot separate somatic cis-driven ASM from germline allelic methylation / drift — exactly the confound ISM core-6 normal-anchored cis-test was built for. (3) NO copy-number / ploidy confound decomposition (critical in cancer LOH/cnLOH regions). (4) NO multiple-testing correction shipped (no BH/FDR); MAP p-value is binary-only, pair-single-site-only, and capped at 100 reads/condition (loses power/precision at the high coverage typical of targeted cancer data). (5) HP1 vs HP2 treated as opaque conditions — no HP1 vs HP1-1 (germline-tag vs somatic-reconstructed-tag) somatic-controlled axis. (6) Region-score aggregation from per-site is undocumented (reproducibility gap). (7) entropy is within-molecule disorder only — no between-sample test, no p-value, no haplotype logic; it measures epiallele randomness (which ISM already found NEGATIVE for TP/FP discrimination once coverage-corrected: O11 epipolymorphism AUC 0.845→0.530). (8) Tool is general/germline-oriented; nothing in it is cancer- or somatic-aware.
deep.what_ism_could_learn: Concrete adoptions ISM could make from modkit: (1) Replace binarized per-CpG Fisher (core 4a) with the Beta-Binomial marginal-likelihood-ratio + Jeffreys-prior shrinkage for the per-CpG/Δβ difference test — gives better small-count behaviour and a coherent Bayes-factor magnitude alongside the existing Cohen's d. (2) Adopt Cohen's h (variance-stabilized arcsine) as a high-count-robust companion to ISM's Δβ Cohen's d, since targeted cancer loci often hit saturating coverage where raw β-difference is unstable. (3) For the 5mC vs 5hmC question ISM currently sidesteps via max-collapse, adopt modkit's Dirichlet-Multinomial multi-state model so the difference step keeps 5hmC and 5mC as distinct states instead of merging them. (4) Use modkit entropy directly as an external, literature-standard cross-check of ISM's in-house NME/epipolymorphism (core 4b/4c) — same construct, independent implementation = good validation. (5) Borrow the explicit window model (num-positions + max bp window) to standardize ISM's 4-CpG sliding-window disorder definition. BUT: ISM should NOT replace cores 1-3 (read×read distance + UPGMA + PERMANOVA) or core 6 (normal-anchored cis-test, copy-partition) — these are exactly the cancer-somatic-structural capabilities modkit lacks and are ISM's differentiation. The right framing for the paper: modkit dmr/entropy = the rate-difference + within-read-disorder baselines; ISM adds the between-molecule structural axis and tumor-normal cis machinery on top.
deep.granularity: modkit dmr: REGION-level (BED) or SINGLE-SITE, computed on AGGREGATED per-genomic-position counts from pileup (reads collapsed to counts; NOT read-level). modkit entropy: WITHIN-READ / WITHIN-MOLECULE patterns summarized per genomic WINDOW (default ≤50bp containing 4 modified positions), optionally per-region. Haplotype: HANDLED UPSTREAM in pileup (--partition-tag HP / --phased → hp1/hp2 bedMethyl), then dmr compares the two HP bedMethyl files as conditions a vs b — dmr/entropy themselves have no HP logic. Contrast: ISM cores 1-3 are genuinely READ-LEVEL/BETWEEN-MOLECULE (read×read distance → clustering → PERMANOVA); ISM core 6 is HP-aware AND somatic-allele-aware (HP1 vs HP1-1) AND tumor-normal-anchored.
deep.input_output: modkit dmr INPUT: ≥2 bgzip+tabix bedMethyl files from `modkit pileup` (+ optional BED regions, sample names, ref FASTA). OUTPUT: BED-like rows with likelihood-ratio score (magnitude+direction of methylation difference); for pair single-site binary mode also MAP-based p-value + effect size d=p̂1−p̂2; for regions/segments Cohen's h + 95% CI. `multi` writes all-pairwise results to an output dir. modkit entropy INPUT: mod-BAM(s) (--in-bam, repeatable) + --ref FASTA + --motif(s) (+ optional --regions). OUTPUT: per-window bedGraph (chrom,start,end,entropy,num_reads); with --regions also per-region mean/median/min/max entropy + read/window counts. Defaults: --num-positions 4, --window-size 50, log base 2.
deep.statistics_detail: dmr STATISTICS: (a) primary = log marginal likelihood ratio score = log[ l_{θa}(X_a)·l_{θb}(X_b) / l_{θ_{a+b}}(X_{a+b}) ], a Bayes-factor-style comparison of separate-vs-shared methylation parameter models; marginal likelihoods integrate the parameter out under the conjugate prior (so NOT a plug-in MLE GLRT). (b) likelihood model = Beta-Binomial (binary 5mC/C, 6mA/A) or Dirichlet-Multinomial (≥3 states e.g. 5hmC/5mC/C), Jeffreys prior in all cases. (c) MAP-based p-value: binary-only, pair single-site only, coverage capped at 100 reads/condition (unstable beyond), built on empirical d=p̂1−p̂2. (d) Cohen's h with 95% CI for high-count robustness. (e) NO FDR/BH/genome-wide correction documented. entropy STATISTICS: Shannon entropy ME=−(1/N)Σ Pr(n_i)log₂Pr(n_i) over empirical epiallele-pattern distribution per window; descriptive only, no inferential test, no p-value, no correction.

deep.tool: pycoMeth v2.2.2 (Snajder, Leger, Stegle, Bonder 2023, Genome Biology 24:83). A Python toolbox for differential methylation testing on ONT long-read methylation calls, downstream of Nanopolish call-methylation. LONG-READ, READ-LEVEL storage (MetH5 HDF5), but the differential test and the segmentation both REDUCE to region/interval-level units. GERMLINE-oriented by design (benchmarks: GIAB trio chr20 parent-of-origin / imprinting; tumor-vs-normal is supported via read-groups but not the validation focus). Two modules: Meth_Comp (differential test) + Meth_Seg (Bayesian HMM consensus segmentation). Verified against the PMC full text AND the actual source on github.com/PMBio/pycoMeth@main (Meth_Comp.py, meth_seg/hmm.py, meth_seg/emissions.py).
deep.method_detail:
VERIFIED FROM SOURCE (Meth_Comp.py, hmm.py, emissions.py on main) + PMC10120131.

== Meth_Comp differential test ==
Input is an aggregated interval (from CpG_Aggregate / Interval_Aggregate / Meth_Seg segments), NOT a raw read pile. Three hypotheses, each picking a scipy test via pvalue_method:
1. llr_diff: pools every per-read CpG log-likelihood-ratio (LLR) across reads in the interval into one vector per sample; two-sided Mann-Whitney-U (MW, 2 samples) or Kruskal-Wallis (KW, >2). This is the only mode that uses raw per-call LLR (so it 'draws power from segment size + read depth + call uncertainty'). It is read-level-derived but operates on a POOLED 1-D LLR distribution, not per-read or read x read.
2. bs_diff: collapses to a per-READ beta-score = (#methylated CpG with LLR>thr) / (#non-ambiguous CpG with |LLR|>thr) for that read (compute_read_betascores), then MW/KW on the per-read beta-score distribution; or 'paired' -> scipy.stats.wilcoxon. Power 'derives only from read depth'. This is the closest pycoMeth gets to a read-level distribution test, but each read is reduced to ONE scalar methylation fraction.
3. count_dependency: scipy fisher_exact (2 samples) or chi2_contingency (>2) on a samples x {methylated,unmethylated} contingency table built by thresholding LLRs.
KW/chi2 significant -> post-hoc one-vs-others MW/Fisher (compute_posthoc_test). Multiple testing: statsmodels multipletests default fdr_bh (BH), with optional IHW where weight = standard deviation of per-group methylation rates (compute_ihw_weight, the '1-centered scaled SD'). Output TSV: raw p, adjusted p, per-sample median LLR, methylation-rate difference (effect size), coverage. Filters: MIN_NUM_READS_PER_INTERVAL=10, MAX_MISSING=0.

== Meth_Seg Bayesian changepoint segmentation ==
SegmentationHMM (hmm.py): a left-to-right HMM over CpG sites within a window (WINDOW_SIZE=300 CpGs, MAX_SEGMENTS_PER_WINDOW=10). States = segment indices; transitions are t_move/t_stay/t_end with a per-segment seg_penalty that grows with segment index (Bayesian-style penalty on adding segments, i.e. a prior favoring fewer changepoints). Emission (emissions.py BernoulliPosterior): a Bernoulli likelihood with UNCERTAIN observations -- each observation is p(methylated) derived from the call LLR (not a hard 0/1), combined with a per-segment, per-read-group methylation parameter mu_{s,g}; a Beta(prior_a,prior_a) prior is placed on mu (scipy.stats.beta). Inference = baum_welch (EM): forward/backward to get site x segment posteriors, ML update of segment mu, then MAP/viterbi to read off segment boundaries. Post-processing merges adjacent segments whose mu differ by <0.2 across ALL read-groups.

== Consensus / haplotype-aware ==
'Haplotype-aware' is concrete and simple: haplotypes (or samples) are stored as separate READ-GROUPS in the MetH5 file; the HMM fits a SHARED segmentation (one set of changepoints) but a SEPARATE mu_{s,g} per read-group per segment. So a boundary is called where ANY read-group changes -> a single consensus segmentation that is sensitive to haplotype/sample-specific methylation shifts. Region/haplotype-level output, not read x read.

== MetH5 ==
Read-level, reference-anchored HDF5 store of per-CpG LLRs keyed by genomic coordinate + read ID, with categorical read-group annotations (haplotype/sample) and read-name maps; indexed for 5-90x faster random access than BAM/CRAM (storage ~165-1400 MB range cited).
deep.vs_ism_detailed:
POINT-BY-POINT vs ISM (InterSubMod), grounded in our project memory (5mCG read-level subclonal, read x read distance matrix, normal-anchored cis-test, MSA Level-1 5mC/5hmC, ARI/PERMANOVA HP-group structure).

1) UNIT OF ANALYSIS / read x read distance matrix:
- pycoMeth has NO read x read distance matrix. Even its most read-aware mode (bs_diff) collapses each read to a single scalar beta-score, then compares two/three SCALAR DISTRIBUTIONS with MW/KW. llr_diff pools all CpG LLRs into one vector. count_dependency is a 2x2 count table. None preserves the read x read or read x CpG matrix.
- ISM keeps the full read x CpG methylation matrix and builds a read-read distance matrix (distance_matrix_[METRIC].csv per region), then tests structure with PERMANOVA / clustering / ARI. ISM asks 'are reads partitioned into sub-populations?' pycoMeth asks 'do two predefined groups differ in mean/distribution?'. Different question class: ISM = unsupervised within-locus structure discovery; pycoMeth = supervised 2/N-group hypothesis test on a pre-defined grouping.

2) SOMATIC NORMAL-ANCHORED cis-test:
- pycoMeth has NO somatic, no normal-anchoring, no cis/trans logic. It is symmetric group-A-vs-group-B (or trio parent-of-origin). It cannot, by construction, separate 'somatic-specific allelic methylation' from 'baseline germline allelic methylation' -- exactly the confound our project flagged (ALLELE-axis baseline confound; needs germline-het null). pycoMeth would report any A-vs-B shift, including pure germline imprinting (which is in fact what its GIAB benchmark validates on).
- ISM's normal-anchored cis-test (normal HP1 / tumor HP1 / tumor HP1-1 three-way) is a somatic-causality control pycoMeth lacks entirely.

3) 5mC / 5hmC SPLIT:
- pycoMeth is Nanopolish-era, single-modification (5mC at CpG) only. A CpG call is one LLR (methylated vs unmethylated). No 5hmC channel.
- ISM/MSA carries MM/ML for 5mCG + 5hmCG (the Level-1 dual-channel; our buggy double-count artifact came from exactly this 2-modification stacking). pycoMeth would silently merge or be blind to 5hmC.

4) STATISTICAL MODEL FOR HAPLOTYPE:
- Overlap: both are haplotype-aware via read-groups. pycoMeth's consensus-HMM (shared boundaries, per-haplotype mu) is a principled generative model for 'where along the genome do haplotypes diverge in methylation'. ISM works WITHIN a fixed locus/variant window and asks whether reads cluster by latent sub-haplotype (ARI vs HP tags), incl. sub-clones beyond the two germline haplotypes (HP1 -> HP1-1/HP1-2).
- pycoMeth segments the genome into methylation domains; ISM characterizes a single somatic-variant locus. Complementary scopes.

5) READ-LEVEL CLAIM:
- Both store read-level data. But pycoMeth's TESTS are interval/region-level (everything reduces to a group statistic per segment). ISM is the one actually operating in read x read space. So 'read-level' means storage in pycoMeth, but analysis in ISM.
deep.strengths: (a) pycoMeth's emission model is genuinely better than naive binarization: BernoulliPosterior uses the soft p(methylated) from the LLR rather than a hard 0/1 call, propagating call uncertainty into both segmentation and llr_diff -- ISM's Level-1 binary/thresholded matrices discard this. (b) The consensus-HMM (shared changepoints, per-read-group mu, Beta prior, seg_penalty growing with #segments) is a clean Bayesian way to do MULTI-SAMPLE joint segmentation -- more principled than per-sample then intersect. (c) MetH5 (reference-anchored read-level HDF5, 5-90x faster random access than BAM) is a real engineering win for read-level methylation at scale. (d) IHW weighting by methylation-rate SD is a thoughtful power-recovery trick for the BH stage. (e) Three orthogonal test modes (LLR-pool / per-read beta / count) let the user trade off uncertainty-awareness vs robustness.
deep.limitations: (a) GERMLINE-CENTRIC: validated on GIAB trio parent-of-origin / imprinting; NO somatic model, NO tumor-vs-normal causal control, NO normal-anchoring -> cannot separate somatic ASM from baseline germline allelic methylation (the exact confound our project requires germline-het nulls for). (b) SINGLE MODIFICATION: Nanopolish 5mC-only; no 5hmC channel -- a blind spot for modern Dorado MM/ML dual-mod ONT cancer data. (c) NO read x read structure: all tests reduce reads to group-level scalars; cannot discover latent within-locus sub-populations/sub-clones (no clustering, no ARI/PERMANOVA). (d) SUPERVISED ONLY: needs a predefined grouping (sample or haplotype read-group); cannot ask 'is this locus internally heterogeneous?' unsupervised. (e) Nanopolish-LLR dependency: input format is Nanopolish-shaped; modern callers need conversion. (f) Effect-size = mean methylation-rate difference; no multivariate read-pattern effect size. (g) The 'read-level' label refers to storage; the statistics are interval/region-level.
deep.what_ism_could_learn: (1) ADOPT THE SOFT-CALL EMISSION: ISM Level-1 thresholds CpGs to binary; pycoMeth's BernoulliPosterior keeps p(methylated) from the LLR/ML probability. ISM's read x CpG matrix and distance metrics could be built on soft probabilities (expected methylation) instead of hard 0/1, propagating ML uncertainty -- likely improves the read-read distance matrix and reduces low-coverage noise. (2) JOINT MULTI-SAMPLE/HAPLOTYPE SEGMENTATION: pycoMeth's shared-changepoint, per-group-mu consensus HMM is a template for principled cross-haplotype boundary detection ISM currently does per-locus. (3) IHW-style power weighting at the FDR stage when ISM does genome-wide multiple testing. (4) MetH5-style reference-anchored read-level store if ISM ever needs fast random access at scale. CAVEAT (must keep): pycoMeth would IMPORT pycoMeth's germline confound -- any borrowed segmentation/test must still be wrapped in ISM's normal-anchored somatic cis-control, or it will flag germline imprinting/allelic methylation as 'signal' (precisely pycoMeth's GIAB use case). The borrow is methodological (soft emissions, joint segmentation, IHW), NOT the experimental design.
deep.statistics_detail: VERIFIED scipy/statsmodels calls in Meth_Comp.py (line 15 import; lines ~189-251): from scipy.stats import kruskal, mannwhitneyu, wilcoxon, fisher_exact, chi2_contingency; from statsmodels.stats.multitest import multipletests. pvalue_method enum: 'MW' -> mannwhitneyu(...,alternative='two-sided'); 'KW' -> kruskal(*test_values) + post-hoc one-vs-others mannwhitneyu; 'paired' -> wilcoxon(); 'fisher_exact' -> fisher_exact(); 'chi_squared' -> chi2_contingency() + post-hoc fisher. Three hypotheses: llr_diff (pooled per-CpG LLR vector per sample), bs_diff (per-read beta-score = met/non-ambiguous via compute_read_betascores; also a per-site variant compute_site_betascores), count_dependency (compute_contingency_table thresholding LLR). IHW weight (compute_ihw_weight) = sample standard deviation of pooled methylation values. Defaults: MIN_NUM_READS_PER_INTERVAL=10, MAX_MISSING=0, correction default 'fdr_bh'. Meth_Seg defaults: WINDOW_SIZE=300 CpGs, MAX_SEGMENTS_PER_WINDOW=10, merge threshold 0.2 methylation-rate difference, BernoulliPosterior segment_p initialized log(1/5) and log(4/5) for alternating un/methylated states, Beta(prior_a,prior_a) prior. Benchmarks (PMC): simulated high-coverage DMR segmentation = 72.2% full boundary match / 24.1% partial / 3.6% no match, F1=0.868 (bs-difference test + IHW); GIAB chr20 parent comparison pycoMeth 156,584 CpGs-in-DMRs vs MethCP 92,435; MetH5 5-90x faster random access vs BAM/CRAM, ~165-1400 MB storage range. NOTE: F1=0.868 and the 72.2/24.1/3.6 split are from the PMC text via WebFetch summary, cross-consistent with two independent fetches but NOT independently re-derived; treat exact decimals as paper-reported.
deep.granularity: pycoMeth STORAGE = read-level (MetH5, per-read per-CpG LLR). pycoMeth ANALYSIS = region/interval-level + haplotype-level (read-group). Meth_Comp tests a PREDEFINED 2/N-group difference per interval. Meth_Seg produces consensus genomic SEGMENTS (region-level) with per-haplotype methylation rates. NO read x read matrix, NO within-locus latent sub-population discovery. ISM = within-locus read x read distance matrix + unsupervised structure (clustering/ARI/PERMANOVA) + normal-anchored somatic cis-test + 5mC/5hmC dual channel. Domain: pycoMeth = long-read, germline/imprinting-validated, single-modification; ISM = long-read, somatic-cancer, dual-modification.
deep.input_output: INPUT: Nanopolish call-methylation TSV -> MetH5 read-level HDF5 (per-CpG LLR, read ID, read-group=haplotype/sample). Meth_Comp also accepts CpG_Aggregate / Interval_Aggregate / Meth_Seg segment intervals. OUTPUT: Meth_Comp -> BED + TSV of DMRs (raw p, BH-adjusted p, per-sample median LLR, methylation-rate difference effect size, coverage) + interactive HTML report. Versus ISM whose output is per-region read x CpG methylation.csv + distance_matrix_[METRIC].csv + significance_summary.csv.

deep.tool: cvlr (Raineri, Alberola i Pla, Dabad, Heath — CNAG-CRG / CRG Barcelona). "cvlr: finding heterogeneously methylated genomic regions using ONT reads." Bioinformatics Advances 3(1):vbac101, published 2023-01-23. DOI 10.1093/bioadv/vbac101; PMID 36726731. A command-line tool that clusters individual ONT long reads by their methylation pattern using a mixture of multivariate Bernoulli distributions fit by EM, WITHOUT a prior phasing step. Three executables: cvlr-cluster, cvlr-meth-of-bam, cvlr-stats. SCOPE TAGS: long-read ONT-specific (tested on NA12878 lymphoblastoid line, Nanopore Consortium); GERMLINE-demonstrated (imprinting / allele-specific benchmark) — cancer/somatic NOT demonstrated; operates READ-level (clusters reads) but reports aggregated to genomic windows/regions (5 kb genome scans). NOTE: the GitHub repo cited in the paper (github.com/EmanueleRaineri/cvlr) is NOT publicly reachable as of 2026-06-10 (404; author account shows public_repos:0) — implementation language and exact CLI flags could NOT be verified from primary source and are marked UNVERIFIED.
deep.method_detail: ALGORITHM (verified from PMC9887406 full text + Oxford Academic article page). Data: binary matrix X with n reads (rows) x d genomic CpG positions (columns); each X_ij in {0,1,-1}, where -1 = missing methylation call (read does not cover that CpG, or call below confidence). MODEL: mixture of k multivariate Bernoulli distributions. Parameters: (a) mixing proportions pi_l, l=1..k, with sum pi_l = 1; (b) a k x d matrix mu, where row mu_l gives the per-cluster per-CpG methylation probability ('average methylation for each cluster at each position'). Per-read likelihood is the standard mixture: sum_l pi_l * product_j [ mu_lj^x_ij (1-mu_lj)^(1-x_ij) ] over OBSERVED positions (independence across CpGs assumed within a cluster — a naive-Bernoulli factorization; the exact product form is stated in the preprint methods which I could NOT fetch [bioRxiv PDF 403], but the journal text confirms 'mixture of multivariate Bernoulli distributions'). The model also yields a covariance matrix of methylation across positions accounting for the mixture: Cov = sum_l pi_l { Sigma_l + mu_l mu_l^T } - E[x]E[x]^T, with Sigma_l = diag(mu_l (1 - mu_l)) (verbatim from PMC). EM: E-step computes the posterior probability (responsibility) that each read belongs to each cluster; M-step updates mu (and pi), and crucially handles MISSING data by 'replacing missing data with a weighted sum of the corresponding positions in the old mu' — i.e. soft imputation of -1 entries from the current cluster means rather than dropping CpGs. INITIALIZATION: random; multiple restarts with different seeds; the run with the best likelihood is kept (guards against local optima). Convergence: user-specifiable maximum number of EM iterations (default not stated; no explicit convergence tolerance reported). MODEL SELECTION FOR k: NONE — k is user-specified (examples and the chromosome-15 scan use k=2). The paper reports NO BIC/AIC/likelihood-ratio mechanism to choose k; this is the model's main statistical gap. INPUTS: BAM with methylation annotation, parsed by cvlr-meth-of-bam; users can also adapt output from Nanopolish or Megalodon. (MM/ML-tag handling is implied via BAM methylation annotation but the tag mechanics are not spelled out in the text → that detail UNVERIFIED.) OUTPUTS: per-read cluster assignments; per-cluster methylation profiles (Fig 1b); covariance matrices (Fig 1c); median absolute methylation difference between clusters (Delta m); posterior P-values for the methylation difference. BENCHMARKS (verified, PMC Table 1 + text): 8 known imprinted genes all gave P(Delta m) < 1e-3 — e.g. GNAS (chr20:58,830,000-58,870,000) Delta m = 0.667, P(Delta m) < 1e-3, phasing P = 8.2e-30; H19DMR Delta m = 0.609, P(Delta m) < 1e-3, phasing P = 0.0079. Chromosome-15 scan, 5 kb windows, k=2: threshold = 95th percentile of methylation difference = 0.53; 909 windows ('peaks') exceeded threshold; WhatsHap could phase-analyze only ~40 windows, so cvlr covered 905 windows where phasing gave no result; all-but-one imprinted control region fell into peaks; 55/909 peaks overlapped NA12878 enhancers (randomization P < 1%). Total reads on chr15 = 329,353, of which WhatsHap left 130,963 (~40%) unassigned to a haplotype (no informative SNPs) — the motivating no-phasing statistic. Simulation: error rate ~=2% across tests with 100 reads x 1000 positions under uniform and alternating methylation patterns. NOT reported: runtime, sensitivity/specificity, ARI.
deep.vs_ism_detailed: DIRECT COMPARISON — both cluster individual long reads by methylation pattern with NO prior phasing, on ONT data; the difference is the clustering ENGINE and the statistical treatment of uncertainty. (1) CLUSTERING PARADIGM. cvlr = generative model-based: a finite mixture of multivariate Bernoulli distributions fit by EM; every read gets a SOFT posterior responsibility (probability of cluster membership) and the model produces interpretable per-cluster per-CpG methylation probabilities mu_l. ISM = distance-based agglomerative: it first builds a read x read distance matrix (verified from source include/core/Types.hpp enum {NHD, L1, L2, CORR, JACCARD, BERNOULLI}; Config.hpp default = BERNOULLI distance; CLI --distance-metric default NHD) then runs hierarchical clustering (HierarchicalClustering.cpp; default LinkageMethod::UPGMA = unweighted average linkage via Lance-Williams O(N^3), merge height = min_dist/2 with monotonicity enforcement; alternatives WARD/SINGLE/COMPLETE). ISM assigns each read to exactly ONE leaf cluster (HARD assignment) by cutting the dendrogram. (2) NOTE ON 'BERNOULLI': both tools invoke Bernoulli, but differently — cvlr uses a Bernoulli LIKELIHOOD inside a generative mixture; ISM's BERNOULLI is one of several DISTANCE metrics feeding UPGMA (verified in enum), i.e. a pairwise dissimilarity, not a fitted model. So ISM does not estimate cluster-level methylation probabilities or mixing proportions at all. (3) MISSING DATA. cvlr models missing CpG calls (-1) explicitly and imputes them in the M-step via current cluster means (principled under the mixture). ISM handles missing CpGs at the DISTANCE level via NanDistanceStrategy {MAX_DIST, SKIP} (verified Types.hpp) plus min_cov thresholds — a heuristic at the pairwise stage, not a model-based imputation. (4) CLUSTER-COUNT SELECTION. cvlr: k is fixed/user-specified, NO data-driven selection. ISM: ACTUALLY HAS automatic selection — HierarchicalClustering.cpp:~488-543 computes a SILHOUETTE score across candidate cuts and picks the best (also supports cut_by_distance threshold or cut_by_num_clusters). So on 'choosing the number of clusters' ISM is arguably MORE automated than cvlr — but its criterion is geometric (silhouette on the distance matrix), not likelihood-based. (5) UNCERTAINTY. cvlr's soft posteriors expose ambiguous reads and let downstream stats weight by membership confidence; ISM's hard UPGMA assignment discards that, though ISM adds its own significance layer (PERMANOVA / CramersV gating, per repo memory) on top of the hard clusters. (6) SCOPE MATCH TO OUR CONTEXT. Both are ONT long-read and phasing-free, which fits our setting. But cvlr is benchmarked on GERMLINE imprinting (allele-specific), while ISM is applied to CANCER somatic methylation (TP/FP somatic-variant neighborhoods, subclonal structure) — neither tool's published validation covers the other's domain, so cvlr's imprinting benchmark does NOT transfer as evidence for somatic subclone resolution.
deep.what_ism_could_learn: Three concrete, defensible borrowings — with the caveat that ISM already covers part of what the prompt assumed it lacked. (A) SOFT PROBABILISTIC MEMBERSHIP (highest value). cvlr's EM gives each read a posterior probability of cluster membership; this directly surfaces 'ambiguous' reads near a subclone boundary, which in a cancer somatic-methylation context is exactly where read-misassignment corrupts downstream TP/FP / subclonal calls. ISM's hard UPGMA cut throws this away. Adding a model-based (or even a fuzzy-clustering) layer that emits per-read soft weights would let ISM (i) report assignment confidence, (ii) down-weight low-confidence reads in significance tests, and (iii) detect subclones that are mixtures rather than clean splits. (B) GENERATIVE PER-CLUSTER METHYLATION PROFILES. cvlr's mu_l (per-cluster per-CpG methylation probability) is an interpretable, directly reportable object — 'cluster 1 is hypomethylated at these CpGs.' ISM's distance+UPGMA never estimates such profiles; it only has pairwise distances and a dendrogram. A Bernoulli-mixture (or post-hoc per-cluster mean) view would make ISM clusters biologically narratable for a paper/PI, not just 'tree branch A vs B.' (C) MODEL-BASED MISSING-DATA HANDLING. cvlr imputes uncovered CpGs through the mixture (M-step weighted mean) rather than at the pairwise-distance stage; for sparse ONT methylation matrices this is more principled than ISM's MAX_DIST/SKIP heuristics and would reduce distance-metric artifacts in low-coverage windows. CAVEAT on the prompt's framing: the prompt suggested 'BIC model selection' as the thing ISM could learn — but (i) ISM ALREADY auto-selects k via silhouette (verified in source), and (ii) cvlr itself does NOT use BIC (k is user-fixed). So 'add BIC' is NOT a learn-from-cvlr item; if anything, ISM could ADD a likelihood-based criterion (BIC/ICL) ONLY IF it first adopts a generative mixture (A) — BIC requires a likelihood, which the current distance+UPGMA pipeline does not have. That is the real dependency: probabilistic model first, then BIC becomes possible. Net recommendation: pilot a multivariate-Bernoulli-mixture-EM clustering path inside ISM as an OPTION alongside UPGMA, compare soft-vs-hard assignment on a known subclonal cancer region, and only then consider BIC/ICL for k — do not bolt BIC onto the distance pipeline where it has no likelihood to score.

deep.statistics_detail: k-cluster mixture of multivariate Bernoulli fit by EM. Parameters: pi (k mixing weights, sum=1) and mu (k x d per-cluster per-CpG methylation probabilities). E-step = posterior cluster responsibilities per read; M-step = update pi, mu with missing (-1) entries imputed by weighted current cluster means. Random init + multiple seeds, keep best likelihood. k user-specified, NO BIC/AIC/model selection. Covariance: sum_l pi_l{Sigma_l + mu_l mu_l^T} - E[x]E[x]^T, Sigma_l=diag(mu_l(1-mu_l)). Reported stats: per-cluster Delta m (median abs methylation difference) with posterior P-value; imprinting benchmark P(Delta m)<1e-3 for all 8 genes (GNAS Delta m=0.667; H19DMR Delta m=0.609); chr15 peak threshold=0.53 (95th pct), 909 peaks, enhancer overlap 55/909 (rand P<1%); simulation error ~2% (100 reads x 1000 positions). No ARI/sensitivity/specificity/runtime reported.
deep.granularity: Read-level clustering (each ONT read assigned to a cluster) with results aggregated to genomic windows/regions (5 kb windows in genome scans; gene-sized regions for known imprinted loci). Phasing-free (no haplotype prior), so it operates on raw read methylation patterns rather than HP-tagged reads.
deep.input_output: INPUT: BAM with methylation annotation (parsed by cvlr-meth-of-bam); can also consume Nanopolish or Megalodon methylation output. Internally a binary read x CpG matrix with -1 for missing calls. (Exact MM/ML tag mechanics not detailed in text → UNVERIFIED.) OUTPUT: per-read cluster assignments; per-cluster methylation profiles (mu_l); covariance matrices; median absolute methylation difference between clusters (Delta m) with posterior P-values. Three executables: cvlr-cluster (the EM clustering), cvlr-meth-of-bam (extract methylation matrix from BAM), cvlr-stats (covariance / difference statistics).
deep.strengths: Principled generative model: soft posterior read-membership (exposes ambiguous reads + confidence weighting); interpretable per-cluster per-CpG methylation probabilities mu_l; model-based handling of missing/uncovered CpGs via M-step imputation (well-suited to sparse ONT matrices); multiple random restarts to avoid EM local optima; phasing-free so it recovers heterogeneity for the ~40% of reads (130,963/329,353 on chr15) that WhatsHap cannot phase due to lacking informative SNPs; covariance output captures cross-CpG structure while accounting for the mixture. Clean germline/imprinting benchmark with strong separations (Delta m up to 0.667, P<1e-3).
deep.limitations: No data-driven selection of k — user must fix the number of clusters (examples use k=2); no BIC/AIC/likelihood-ratio criterion reported. No reported ARI, sensitivity/specificity, or runtime. Bernoulli mixture assumes within-cluster CpG independence (factorized likelihood) — real methylation has spatial CpG correlation, which the model captures only through the cluster structure, not within a cluster. Benchmarked only on GERMLINE imprinting in a single lymphoblastoid line (NA12878); NO somatic/cancer validation, so applicability to tumor subclonal methylation is unproven. EM is sensitive to initialization (mitigated by restarts but not eliminated). Convergence tolerance not specified (only a max-iteration cap). The published GitHub repo is currently unreachable (2026-06-10), limiting reproducibility verification.

deep.tool: DAMEfinder — Orjuela, Machlab, Menigatti, Marra & Robinson. Journal = Epigenetics & Chromatin (NOT NAR Genomics & Bioinformatics as the task prompt stated — corrected from primary source). 2020, vol 13, article 25. DOI 10.1186/s13072-020-00346-8; PMID 32487212; PMCID PMC7268773. Bioconductor R/BioC package (markrobinsonuzh/DAMEfinder). NOTE: the ISM C++ source cites it as "De Waele 2020" in PerCpgAsm.cpp:6 / PerCpgAsm.hpp:8 — that author attribution is ALSO wrong; the DAMEfinder authors are Orjuela et al. (De Waele 2020 is a different methylation paper). Both the task prompt's journal and the ISM source's author tag are mis-cited.
deep.method_detail:
DAMEfinder is a short-read bisulfite-sequencing (WGBS / targeted BS-seq; bismark + Bowtie2 alignment) tool with TWO ASM modes that converge at the differential-testing stage.

(A) SNP-based / "exhaustive" mode (needs a VCF of heterozygous SNPs; pipeline extract_bams() -> calc_derivedasm()). For each CpG covered by reads spanning a het SNP, reads are split by allele and the ASMsnp score (Eq.1) is the difference in methylated-read fraction between ref and alt alleles: ASMsnp_i = (XM_ir / X_ir) - (XM_ia / X_ia), range 0 (equal) to 1 (full asymmetry). XM = methylated reads on that allele, X = total reads on that allele.

(B) Tuple-based / "fast" mode (SNP-FREE; needs methtuple output of CpG-pair MM/MU/UM/UU counts; pipeline read_tuples() -> calc_asm()). For each CpG PAIR (tuple, default max 150 bp apart) the ASMtuple score (Eq.2) is a weighted log-odds ratio: ASMtuple_i = log10[ (XMM_i+c)(XUU_i+c) / (XMU_i+c)(XUM_i+c) ] * w_i. MM=both CpGs methylated on a read, UU=both unmethylated, MU/UM=discordant. The score is HIGH when reads are bimodal (lots of MM and UU on different reads = allele-specific), LOW when methylation is random/intermediate. The weight w_i = P(0.5-eps < theta < 0.5+eps | XMM, XUU, gamma) with theta ~ Beta(gamma+XMM, gamma+XUU) (Eqs.3-4; defaults gamma=0.5, eps=0.2, pseudocount c). This down-weights tuples that are fully MM or fully UU (which show NO allele-specificity even though the raw log-odds would be large) and rewards a roughly 50:50 MM:UU split. The SNP-free assumption: intermediate bulk methylation = ASM signature.

(C) Differential ASM test — find_dames(). The per-site/per-tuple ASMtuple scores are sqrt-transformed (variance stabilization), then limma lmFit() fits a linear model per CpG/tuple and eBayes() computes a MODERATED t-statistic (empirical-Bayes shrinkage of variance, borrowing strength across loci — the key win over a per-locus standalone test). Regions (DAMEs) are then called two ways: (default) Simes cluster p-value p_c = min{ n*p_(i)/i } aggregating ordered within-cluster p-values; OR bumphunter regionFinder() summing |coefficient| over a region into area A and assigning empirical permutation p-values by shuffling group labels.

ISM per-CpG ASM (verified in /big7_disk/liaoyoyo2001/InterSubMod/src/core/PerCpgAsm.cpp): for each CpG, builds a 2x2 of (meth, unmeth) counts for HP1-family reads (hp tag 1/HP1/1-1) vs HP2-family reads (2/HP2/2-1), thresholding per-read methyl prob at >0.5 to binarize (PerCpgAsm.cpp:282-290), runs Fisher's exact test (FisherExact, seed 42), records delta = HP1 meth-fraction minus HP2 meth-fraction, then BH-FDR across all CpGs in the region (bh_fdr_correction, PerCpgAsm.cpp:26-66, standard Benjamini-Hochberg with right-to-left monotonicity). Summary stats per region: fisher_n_sig (CpGs FDR<0.05), fisher_frac_sig, fisher_n_tested, fisher_max_neg_log_fdr. Companion metrics NME (normalized methylation entropy, per HP group) and epipolymorphism (4-CpG sliding window, 1 - sum p^2) are computed separately, NOT folded into one ASM score.
deep.vs_ism_detailed:
UNIT OF TEST: DAMEfinder tuple mode scores CpG-PAIRS (read concordance across two CpGs on the same read = on-read epigenetic linkage); ISM scores SINGLE CpGs independently (a 2x2 per site). DAMEfinder's whole premise is the on-read MM/UU vs MU/UM pattern; ISM's per-CpG Fisher throws away the cross-CpG read pattern at the Fisher stage (it captures on-read structure separately, in NME/epipolymorphism). So ISM's "per-CpG Fisher" is genuinely analogous to a per-site DM test, NOT to DAMEfinder's signature tuple log-odds.

GROUPING / ALLELE AXIS: DAMEfinder splits reads by ALLELE — either explicit SNP allele (ref vs alt, SNP-based mode) or implicit bimodality (tuple mode infers allele-specificity from MM/UU split without phasing). ISM splits reads by HAPLOTYPE TAG (HP1-family vs HP2-family from longphase), which is a phased-haplotype axis, not a per-locus allele axis. This is the deepest difference: ISM already has genome-wide read-backed phasing (long-read advantage), so it does not need DAMEfinder's SNP-tuple trick to recover allele identity — but it also means ISM's groups are haplotype-level, conflating multiple SNPs, whereas DAMEfinder SNP-mode is anchored to one het SNP at a time.

STATISTIC: DAMEfinder = moderated t (limma eBayes, variance shrinkage across loci) + multi-sample design matrix + region aggregation (Simes / bumphunter) + permutation/empirical FDR. ISM = per-CpG Fisher exact (exact small-count test, single sample, no variance borrowing) + BH-FDR over CpGs within ONE region. ISM has NO cross-sample moderated model and NO region-level aggregation statistic — each region is tested in isolation, single-sample.

TECHNOLOGY: DAMEfinder = short-read BS-seq ONLY (bismark/methtuple/Bis-SNP), no ONT/long-read support confirmed. ISM = ONT long-read, native HP tags. DAMEfinder's tuple-distance cap (150 bp) and need for paired-end concordance is a short-read limitation that long reads dissolve.

DISEASE CONTEXT: DAMEfinder validated on colorectal cancer (targeted) + normal blood monocytes — designed for differential ASM BETWEEN CONDITIONS (multi-sample case/control), largely germline/imprinting + tumor-vs-normal framing. ISM = somatic single-tumor read-level, HP1 vs HP2 WITHIN one cancer sample. DAMEfinder is fundamentally a between-sample differential tool; ISM per-CpG is a within-sample, within-region characterization. They answer different questions.

SCALE: DAMEfinder = region/DAME level (genome-wide region discovery); ISM per-CpG ASM = within-region per-CpG, aggregated to a region summary, but feeding a read-level/locus-level TP/FP characterization. ISM is read-level + haplotype; DAMEfinder is region-level + allele.
deep.what_ism_could_learn:
RANKED, honest about whether each fits ONT long-read somatic single-tumor context:

1. ADOPT THE TUPLE (CpG-PAIR) LOG-ODDS as a complement to per-CpG Fisher — HIGH FIT, HIGH VALUE. DAMEfinder's core insight is that on-read MM/UU vs MU/UM concordance carries allele-specificity that single-CpG tests miss. ISM has the IDEAL substrate for this (full read x CpG methylation matrix already in MethylationMatrix; long reads span many CpGs >> 150 bp cap, so ISM can compute tuples at arbitrary distance with no paired-end limitation). Currently ISM captures on-read structure only via NME/epipolymorphism (unsupervised entropy) — it does NOT have a directed HP1-vs-HP2 tuple-concordance score. Adding the weighted log-odds per CpG-pair, stratified by HP group, would give a haplotype-aware analogue of ASMtuple that exploits the long-read advantage DAMEfinder lacks. This is the single most transferable idea.

2. THE BETA-WEIGHT IDEA (attenuate fully-MM or fully-UU loci) — MEDIUM FIT. The conceptual lesson is real even at single-CpG level: a CpG that is ~100% methylated in BOTH HP groups gives a non-significant Fisher p, so ISM already handles the trivial case — but the weight formalizes "intermediate/balanced = informative" which could improve ranking of borderline loci. Worth porting as a score weight, not as a gate.

3. MODERATED / SHRINKAGE STATISTIC FOR CROSS-SAMPLE — MEDIUM FIT but only when ISM goes multi-sample. ISM's per-region Fisher is single-sample and isolated. DAMEfinder's limma eBayes borrows variance across loci/samples. Given the project's repeated single-sample-circularity failures (LOSO negatives, n=1 tier caps at star-3), an empirical-Bayes moderated statistic across the 6+ tumor samples would directly address the "single-pipeline / single-sample" tier ceiling. This is methodologically the most rigorous upgrade, but requires the multi-sample matrix to exist first.

4. REGION-LEVEL AGGREGATION (Simes / bumphunter area) — LOW-MEDIUM FIT. ISM already aggregates CpG p-values into region summaries (fisher_n_sig / frac_sig / max_neg_log_fdr) which is a cruder aggregation than Simes. Adopting Simes cluster p-value would give a single calibrated region-level p instead of ad-hoc counts — cheap, principled, low risk. But ISM's region boundaries come from variant anchoring, not bumphunting, so the full bumphunter machinery is overkill.

DO NOT ADOPT: the SNP-based exhaustive mode and Bis-SNP allele-splitting — ISM already has superior phased HP tags from long reads; re-deriving alleles per-SNP would be a regression. The 150 bp tuple-distance cap is a short-read artifact ISM should explicitly NOT inherit.

CRITICAL CAVEAT for this project: any tuple/ASM score upgrade is a CHARACTERIZATION improvement, not a TP/FP filter — prior memory (filter-DEAD, strong-ASM enriched in FP not TP, ASM real but not usable as somatic filter) means a better ASM score will sharpen WHERE ASM exists, but the team's own evidence says ASM does not discriminate TP from FP. Adopt for descriptive power, not for a filter direction.

OUTPUT: PerCpgAsmResult per region (fisher_n_sig/frac_sig/n_tested/max_neg_log_fdr + NME_hp1/hp2 + epipoly_hp1/hp2 + deltas), feeding TP/FP/FN characterization.
deep.granularity: DAMEfinder: CpG-PAIR (tuple) or single-CpG-with-SNP scoring -> region/DAME level discovery, ALLELE axis (ref/alt or implicit bimodality), MULTI-SAMPLE between-conditions. ISM: single-CpG Fisher -> region summary, HAPLOTYPE axis (HP1-family vs HP2-family phased tags), WITHIN single tumor sample, read-level/locus-level downstream.
deep.strengths: DAMEfinder strengths worth borrowing: (1) on-read CpG-pair concordance log-odds (MM/UU vs MU/UM) directly models allele-specificity that single-CpG tests miss; (2) Beta-weight that attenuates uninformative fully-MM/fully-UU loci and rewards balanced bimodality; (3) limma empirical-Bayes moderated t = variance shrinkage across loci/samples, far more robust than isolated per-locus tests for multi-sample designs; (4) principled region-level p aggregation (Simes / bumphunter).
deep.limitations: DAMEfinder limits for THIS project: short-read BS-seq only (no ONT/long-read), 150bp tuple-distance cap (short-read paired-end artifact), SNP mode re-derives alleles per-SNP via Bis-SNP (inferior to ISM's existing phased long-read HP tags), designed for between-condition differential ASM (germline/imprinting + tumor-vs-normal) not within-sample somatic. UNVERIFIED: exact current Bioconductor package version number was not surfaced on README (multiple BioC releases 3.16-3.23 listed; rdrr.io referenced v1.2.0 but I did not pin the live version). The 'De Waele 2020' attribution in ISM source is a mis-citation of DAMEfinder (authors are Orjuela et al.) — flagged but the De Waele paper itself was not separately fetched, so whether De Waele 2020 is a real distinct methylation paper is UNVERIFIED. PROJECT CAVEAT: per existing memory, ASM is real but NOT a usable TP/FP filter (filter-DEAD; strong-ASM enriched in FP) — any DAMEfinder-inspired score upgrade is for characterization, not filtering.

deep.tool: DSS (Dispersion Shrinkage for Sequencing data) — Bioconductor R package, v2.60.0, maintained by Hao Wu (Emory) & Hao Feng (Case Western). Gold-standard SHORT-READ bisulfite-sequencing (WGBS/RRBS) DML/DMR statistic. Three foundational methodology papers verified from primary sources: (1) Feng, Conneely & Wu 2014, Nucleic Acids Res 42(8):e69, DOI 10.1093/nar/gku154, PMID 24561809 — beta-binomial + lognormal dispersion shrinkage + per-CpG Wald (DML, two-group); (2) Wu, Xu, Feng, Chen, Li, Yao, Qin, Jin & Conneely 2015, Nucleic Acids Res 43(21):e141, DOI 10.1093/nar/gkv715, PMID 26184873 — smoothing + empirical-Bayes dispersion WITHOUT replicates (DMR); (3) Park & Wu 2016, Bioinformatics 32(10):1446-1453, DOI 10.1093/bioinformatics/btw026 — beta-binomial regression with arcsine link for general experimental design (DMLtest.multiFactor). Package biocViews: DNAMethylation, DifferentialMethylation; covers DE genes (RNA-seq) + DML/DMR (BS-seq). PLATFORM CONTEXT (critical): built/validated for SHORT-READ count-based bisulfite data; NO long-read/nanopore (ONT MM/ML) support. Compares GROUPS OF SAMPLES (germline/case-control) at REGION level, not read-groups/haplotypes within one sample; not designed for single-sample somatic clonal/allele-specific structure. So for our context (ONT long-read, somatic cancer, read-level/haplotype Delta-beta) DSS is a STATISTICS BLUEPRINT and citation/benchmark, NOT a drop-in tool.
deep.method_detail:
DSS pipeline = 4 statistical stages, all verified:

1) BETA-BINOMIAL COUNT MODEL (2014; 2016). Methylated read count Y_id ~ beta-binomial(m_id, pi_id, phi_i): m_id=coverage, pi_id=methylation proportion, phi_i=CpG-site-specific dispersion (over-dispersion beyond binomial). Captures BOTH technical (binomial sampling) AND biological (between-replicate) variation; a plain binomial/Fisher assumes phi=0 and underestimates variance.

2) BAYESIAN/EMPIRICAL-BAYES DISPERSION SHRINKAGE (the namesake; 2014). Per-site phi_i is poorly estimated with few replicates, so DSS imposes a LOG-NORMAL prior on dispersions (2014 Fig 1: dispersion is approximately log-normal) and SHRINKS each site's raw dispersion toward the genome-wide prior mean via a lognormal-beta-binomial hierarchical / penalized-likelihood model, borrowing information across all CpG sites. The 2015 paper extends this to NO REPLICATES by treating nearby CpG sites as pseudo-replicates (EB procedure exploiting spatial correlation).

3) PER-CpG WALD TEST (all three papers). With shrunk dispersion plugged in, a Wald statistic tests H0 of equal mean methylation between groups at each CpG; statistic ~ N(0,1) -> p-value. Two-group = DMLtest(); general design = DMLtest.multiFactor() using beta-binomial REGRESSION with ARCSINE link arcsin(2*pi_id - 1) = x_d * beta_i. Arcsine transform is variance-stabilizing (variance ~depends only on dispersion not mean) enabling fast GLS estimation: Z_id=arcsin(2Y/m-1), dispersion via Pearson chi-square (not iterative MLE) -> reported 40x faster than RADMeth, 166x faster than BiSeq.

4) SMOOTHING + DMR MERGING (2015 + User's Guide). DMLtest(smoothing=TRUE) applies a simple MOVING-AVERAGE over collapsed counts within smoothing.span = 500 bp default; Wald variance is modified to account for smoothing. The 2015 paper notes this simple moving average performs nearly as well as BSmooth spline smoothing but is far faster. callDMR() merges adjacent significant CpGs into regions via parameters: p.threshold (per-CpG p cutoff), delta (min methylation-difference magnitude), minlen (min region bp), minCG (min #CpG/region), dis.merge (merge nearby DMRs), pct.sig (% of CpGs in region significant). DMRs ranked by areaStat = sum of per-CpG Wald statistics in the region.

GRANULARITY: region-level + per-CpG-locus level — NOT read-level/haplotype-level. INPUT: per-sample/CpG count rows (chr,pos,N,X) from short-read BS-seq + design. OUTPUT: per-CpG table (mu1,mu2,diff.Methy,Wald stat,p,FDR) from DMLtest; DMR table (chr,start,end,length,nCG,meanMethy1/2,diff.Methy,areaStat) from callDMR.

UNVERIFIED: did not re-run DSS source; the User's Guide page surfaced callDMR parameter NAMES but not every numeric default (minlen/minCG/dis.merge numbers) — check installed man pages before quoting numbers. smoothing.span=500bp and areaStat definition ARE confirmed from the vignette.
deep.vs_ism_detailed:
ISM uses Delta-beta (difference in mean methylation fraction between two read groups) + per-CpG Fisher exact, with NO dispersion shrinkage, NO smoothing. Head-to-head:

A) VARIANCE MODEL (biggest gap). Fisher on a 2x2 (methylated/unmethylated x group) assumes each read is an independent Bernoulli draw = binomial with phi=0. DSS's beta-binomial adds over-dispersion phi_i. In ONT long-read SOMATIC data, reads from the same haplotype/clone are NOT independent (epipolymorphism, clonal structure, allele-specific methylation) -> true biological over-dispersion >0 -> Fisher UNDERESTIMATES variance -> p-values too small -> inflated significant-CpG calls.

B) DISPERSION SHRINKAGE. DSS stabilizes per-site dispersion by borrowing across sites (and neighbors when no replicates). ISM per-CpG Fisher has zero cross-site stabilization; low-coverage CpGs get extreme/unstable estimates. A single somatic tumor (n=1) has no replicate structure — exactly the regime the 2015 DSS paper solves with neighbor pseudo-replicates.

C) SMOOTHING / SPATIAL CORRELATION. Methylation is spatially autocorrelated (the harness already flags spatial-autocorr confound). DSS pools neighbors within 500bp to denoise; ISM Delta-beta + Fisher treats each CpG independently, leaving spatial info unused and per-CpG noise high.

D) EFFECT SIZE + CI. DSS gives a model-based effect (diff.Methy / arcsine-scale beta) WITH a Wald SE -> confidence interval. ISM Delta-beta is a raw proportion difference with no SE/CI/shrinkage — a Delta-beta from 5 reads looks identical in magnitude to one from 200 reads.

E) MULTIPLE TESTING / REGION AGGREGATION. DSS callDMR merges CpGs into regions ranked by areaStat (aggregated evidence), partly mitigating multiplicity and giving region-level effect sizes. ISM per-CpG Fisher yields a flood of independent p-values needing separate FDR and has no principled region object.

F) AXIS / UNIT MISMATCH (caveat, not a defect to copy). DSS compares GROUPS OF SAMPLES (germline/case-control) at REGION level on SHORT-READ data; ISM compares READ GROUPS/HAPLOTYPES (HP1 vs HP1-1) within ONE somatic ONT sample at READ level. DSS's replicate-based dispersion model maps onto ISM read-level over-dispersion ONLY by analogy (reads-as-units, not samples-as-units). The 2015 pseudo-replicate idea is the closest fit for single-sample ONT.

STRENGTHS DSS brings: honest over-dispersion modeling; variance stabilization with few/no replicates; model-based SE/CI + region-level effect (areaStat); arcsine-GLS speed and extensibility to covariates (could adjust for coverage/CN confounds). LIMITATIONS vs our context: short-read only (no ONT MM/ML), sample-group/region unit (not read/haplotype), 2-group population contrast (not single-sample somatic clonal). Net: blueprint + benchmark, not runtime tool.

verified_claims.claim: DSS uses a beta-binomial model: Y_id ~ beta-binomial(m_id, pi_id, phi_i) with phi_i a CpG-site-specific dispersion capturing biological + technical variation.
verified_claims.source: Park & Wu 2016, Bioinformatics 32(10):1446-1453, DOI 10.1093/bioinformatics/btw026 (verified via academic.oup.com/bioinformatics/article/32/10/1446/1743267); Wu et al. 2015 NAR e141

verified_claims.claim: Dispersion is modeled with a LOG-NORMAL prior and shrunk via a lognormal-beta-binomial Bayesian hierarchical model that borrows information across CpG sites; Figure 1 shows dispersion approximately log-normal.
verified_claims.source: Feng, Conneely & Wu 2014, Nucleic Acids Res 42(8):e69, DOI 10.1093/nar/gku154, PMID 24561809 (verified via pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24561809)

verified_claims.claim: DML detection uses a per-CpG Wald test (statistic ~ N(0,1)) after plugging in shrunk dispersion.

The 2016 general-design model uses a beta-binomial REGRESSION with an ARCSINE link arcsin(2*pi_id-1)=x_d*beta_i; arcsine stabilizes variance enabling GLS estimation, dispersion via Pearson chi-square; ~40x faster than RADMeth and 166x faster than BiSeq.

DSS can detect DMRs WITHOUT replicates via local moving-average smoothing (500bp default) + empirical-Bayes dispersion using nearby CpGs as pseudo-replicates; Wald variance modified for smoothing; simple moving average performs nearly as well as BSmooth spline smoothing but far faster.
verified_claims.source: Wu, Xu, Feng, Chen, Li, Yao, Qin, Jin & Conneely 2015, Nucleic Acids Res 43(21):e141, DOI 10.1093/nar/gkv715, PMID 26184873 (verified via pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4666378)
