deep.what_ism_could_learn:
Prioritized transfers to make ISM Delta-beta effect sizes/CIs robust (ranked by ROI for ONT single-sample somatic read-level work):

1) [HIGHEST] REPLACE Fisher with a per-CpG BETA-BINOMIAL model. Fit Y ~ beta-binomial(coverage, pi_group, phi) so over-dispersion among reads of the same group is explicitly absorbed. Directly fixes the false-positive inflation from treating non-independent long reads as independent Bernoulli draws. Note: prior O11 epipolymorphism NEGATIVE was 'all n_reads confound' — a beta-binomial that models coverage explicitly is exactly the tool to separate true over-dispersion from coverage artifact.

2) [HIGH] ADD DISPERSION SHRINKAGE across CpGs (DSS 2014). Single-sample tumors have no biological replicates, so shrink each CpG's dispersion toward a genome-wide / per-region log-normal prior. Stabilizes the SE used to build a CI on Delta-beta, so a Delta-beta from 5 reads no longer looks as confident as one from 200. This is what converts a raw Delta-beta into an effect size WITH a defensible CI.

3) [HIGH] BORROW THE NO-REPLICATE / PSEUDO-REPLICATE TRICK (DSS 2015) — best fit for single ONT samples. Use neighboring CpGs (within ~500bp) as pseudo-replicates to estimate dispersion and smooth pi via moving average. Denoises Delta-beta AND exploits the spatial autocorrelation the harness otherwise flags as a confound (turning a confound into signal-pooling).

4) [MEDIUM] PRODUCE A WALD-STYLE SE/CI: report Delta-beta +/- 1.96*SE instead of a bare point difference + p-value. This is the robust effect size with CI the task asks for, comparable across loci/coverage.

5) [MEDIUM] REGION AGGREGATION analogous to callDMR/areaStat: aggregate per-CpG statistics over a locus into one region-level effect + rank, instead of a flood of independent per-CpG p-values needing separate FDR.

IMPLEMENTATION PATH: DSS is R/Bioconductor and short-read-oriented — do NOT pipe ONT data through DSS directly. Re-implement the beta-binomial + lognormal-shrinkage estimator (2014/2015 math) in the ISM stack at the READ-group level (HP1 vs HP1-1), validate against the HP-shuffle null already in use, and keep DSS as the methods CITATION/benchmark. A short-read DSS run on a matched WGBS region (if available) could serve as a positive control.

deep.tool: Guo et al. 2017, "Identification of methylation haplotype blocks aids in deconvolution of heterogeneous tissue samples and tumor tissue-of-origin mapping from plasma DNA." Nature Genetics 49(4):635-642. DOI 10.1038/ng.3805, PMID 28263317. Companion software: MONOD2 (github.com/dinhdiep/MONOD2). SHORT-READ bisulfite sequencing (WGBS / RRBS / 450K array). GERMLINE/cell-mixture deconvolution + cancer cfDNA tissue-of-origin (NOT somatic-variant-level, NOT long-read). Region/locus level summary statistic computed FROM read-level co-methylation.
deep.method_detail:
VERIFIED ALGORITHM (primary sources below):

(1) MHB DEFINITION — "linkage disequilibrium of methylation" between ADJACENT CpG sites on the SAME read. A read covering CpG_a and CpG_b gives a 2x2 contingency of methylated/unmethylated states across reads; r2 is the standard population-genetics LD r2 applied to binary methylation states (treating M/U like two alleles). MONOD2 README (official): "an algorithm greedily selects the largest possible continuous region with a minimum linkage disequilibrium score" → blocks grow as long as every adjacent CpG pair stays above the r2 cutoff; a pair below cutoff breaks the block. THRESHOLDS (verified across sources): Guo 2017 reported the genome-wide catalog of 147,888 MHBs; the stringent coupling illustrated uses r2 > 0.9; the operational minimum to seed a block is ">=2 adjacent CpG sites with r2 > 0.5" (restated verbatim in JCEM/Oxford 2021 follow-up that uses the identical Guo method). Block = a contiguous run of CpGs all pairwise-adjacent-coupled above threshold.

(2) MHL = methylation haplotype load. CONCEPT VERIFIED verbatim from multiple sources: "the weighted mean of the fraction of fully methylated (and unmethylated) haplotypes and their substrings at different lengths." Mechanics: for an MHB of length L, enumerate all sub-strings of length i = 1..L (capped at 10 for long blocks). For each i, P(MH_i) = (# fully-methylated substrings of length i observed across reads) / (total # substrings of length i). MHL = SUM_i [ w_i * P(MH_i) ] / SUM_i w_i, where w_i is a length-increasing weight ("giving more weights to longer methylated stretches heuristically worked well" — author's words). The EXACT analytic form of w_i (whether w_i = i exactly) lives only in the paywalled Online Methods/supplement — see limitations; the weighted-mean-of-fully-methylated-substrings structure and the longer=heavier weighting are confirmed. Key property: MHL discriminates blocks with IDENTICAL mean methylation but DIFFERENT coordination (the whole point vs mean-beta).

(3) DECONVOLUTION / tissue-of-origin: select an informative subset of MHBs whose MHL is tissue-specific; model a mixture sample's MHL vector as a non-negative linear combination of reference-tissue MHL profiles and solve for fractions (non-negative least-squares-type deconvolution). Applied to cfDNA of 59 lung/colorectal cancer patients for tumor-load quantification + tissue-of-origin. (Solver form NNLS/QP — see limitations, not verbatim-confirmed.)

PLATFORM/SCOPE FLAGS for our context: SHORT-READ bisulfite (WGBS/RRBS/450K), GERMLINE-tissue + cfDNA cancer, summary computed per-region from read-level co-methylation. NOT ONT long-read native; NOT somatic-SNV-anchored; the haplotype here = epigenetic co-methylation haplotype, NOT a genetic HP1/HP2 phased haplotype.
deep.vs_ism_detailed:
PRECISE AXIS DISTINCTION — this is the load-bearing answer:

MHB/MHL operates on the WITHIN-READ, ALONG-THE-GENOME axis (intra-molecular, CpG-vs-CpG). The unit of linkage is a PAIR OF CpG POSITIONS measured down a single read; r2 asks "do CpG_a and CpG_b tend to share the same methylation state within the same molecule?" The output is a per-LOCUS/per-BLOCK scalar (MHL) summarizing how tightly co-methylated neighboring CpGs are. Reads are the OBSERVATIONS used to estimate pairwise CpG coupling; the reads themselves are never compared to each other. Axis = "horizontal" along genomic coordinate, collapsed over reads.

ISM read-read distance operates on the BETWEEN-READ axis (inter-molecular). The unit is a PAIR OF READS; the metric is a distance between the full methylation vector of read_i and read_j (over the CpGs in a region), assembled into a Read x Read distance matrix (distance_matrix_[METRIC].csv per output-structure.md). The question is "are these two molecules epigenetically different from each other?" — i.e. subclonal / haplotype-level structure AMONG molecules, tested via PERMANOVA / clustering / HP-group separation. Axis = "vertical" across reads, for a fixed set of CpGs.

ONE-LINE CONTRAST: MHB/MHL = co-methylation linkage DOWN a read (CpG_i vs CpG_j, reads are samples) → region summary. ISM read-read = dissimilarity ACROSS reads (read_i vs read_j, CpGs are features) → read-partition / subclone structure. They are literal transposes of the same Read x CpG matrix: MHB summarizes COLUMNS-coupling (CpG-CpG), ISM summarizes ROW-distance (read-read).

WHY THEY ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE: A region can have HIGH MHL (CpGs strongly co-methylated within every read) yet TWO well-separated read clusters (e.g. one fully-methylated haplotype + one fully-unmethylated haplotype) → large ISM read-read distance. Conversely a region with bimodal-but-position-independent methylation can show large ISM separation with modest pairwise-adjacent r2. MHL is blind to read-partition; ISM read-read distance is the quantity that actually captures the HP1/HP2 or subclonal split InterSubMod targets. The shared substrate is the per-read CpG methylation string ("each read = one methylation haplotype," verified verbatim in the mHap format paper) — both methods consume it, but MHB contracts it along CpG-pairs while ISM contracts it along read-pairs.

PLATFORM CAVEAT: MHB/MHL was built for short bisulfite reads (few CpGs/read, no native phasing). ONT long reads give ISM far more CpGs per molecule and let read-read distance be combined with genetic HP tags — a capability MHL never had.

verified_claims.claim: Guo, Diep, Plongthongkum, Fung, Zhang K, Zhang K. Nature Genetics 2017, 49(4):635-642, DOI 10.1038/ng.3805, PMID 28263317.
147,888 methylation haplotype blocks identified across the genome; built from 61 WGBS datasets, validated with 101 RRBS + 637 methylation-array datasets (short-read bisulfite / array, NOT long-read).
MHBs defined by methylation linkage disequilibrium between adjacent CpG sites; stringent coupling illustrated at r2 > 0.9.
verified_claims.source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28263317/ (PubMed/Nature abstract); r2>0.9 figure-level detail per Nature ng.3805

verified_claims.claim: Operational MHB seed = a minimum of 2 adjacent CpG sites with linkage disequilibrium r2 > 0.5 (restated verbatim from the identical Guo 2017 method).
MONOD2 (Guo 2017 official toolkit): block-finder 'greedily selects the largest possible continuous region with a minimum linkage disequilibrium score'.

MHL = weighted mean of the fraction of fully methylated/unmethylated haplotypes and their substrings at different lengths; for a block of length L (>=10) substrings length 1..10 used; longer methylated stretches given more weight (heuristic, author's words). Discriminates blocks with equal mean methylation but different coordination.
A methylation haplotype = the CpG methylation-state pattern on a single read fragment, guaranteed to come from one chromosome of one cell (the shared read-level substrate both MHB and ISM consume).
Application: MHL-based deconvolution + tissue-of-origin on cfDNA of 59 lung/colorectal cancer patients for tumor-load estimation and origin mapping.

deep.source_fetched: PRIMARY/CONFIRMED: PubMed PMID 28263317 (full bib + abstract: 147,888 blocks, r2 LD between adjacent CpGs, MHL, 59-patient cfDNA ToO) — FETCHED. MONOD2 official GitHub repo (greedy-LD block algorithm, Guo 2017 toolkit) — FETCHED. JCEM/Oxford PMC7993581 follow-up using identical Guo method (verbatim: MHB = >=2 adjacent CpG r2>0.5; MHL = weighted mean of fully-methylated substrings, substrings 1..10, optional w_i/P(MH_i)) — FETCHED. mHap format paper, Bioinformatics 37(24):4892 (read = one mHap; MHL quantifies coordinated methylation; PDR/epipolymorphism/CHALM context) — FETCHED. mHapTk Bioinformatics 38(22):5141 (lists 8 mHap statistics incl signed LD R2, no verbatim formula) — FETCHED. NOT FETCHED (blocked/paywalled): nature.com/articles/ng.3805 (303 auth redirect), escholarship 0nj3h020 (empty body), biorxiv 237024 + Metheor 500893 (403 Forbidden).
deep.statistics_detail: LD r2 here = the standard squared correlation of two binary states applied to methylation. For two CpG positions covered by the same set of reads, build allele-like frequencies p_A=fraction methylated at site A, p_B at site B, p_AB=fraction of reads methylated at BOTH; D = p_AB - p_A*p_B; r2 = D^2 / [p_A(1-p_A) p_B(1-p_B)]. Thresholds: seed >=2 adjacent CpG with r2>0.5; stringent illustrative coupling r2>0.9. MHL is a weighted average bounded [0,1]: SUM_i w_i*P(MH_i) / SUM_i w_i, i over substring lengths 1..min(L,10), P(MH_i)=count(fully-methylated i-mers)/count(all i-mers across reads), w_i increasing in i. MHL's discriminating power: it separates the FIVE distinct fully/partially-methylated haplotype configurations that share the same mean-beta (the abstract's claim that MHL is the metric that resolves them). For deconvolution: non-negative linear mixture of reference tissue MHL vectors solved for fractions (NNLS-type), on an informative MHB subset. Statistical framing is region-level descriptive + mixture-regression, NOT a TP/FP classifier and NOT permutation-tested read-partitioning (contrast with ISM's PERMANOVA on read-read distance).
deep.granularity: Three nested levels. (a) INPUT granularity = read-level: each read contributes its CpG methylation string. (b) LINKAGE granularity = CpG-pair (adjacent positions, within-read) — this is the axis. (c) OUTPUT granularity = REGION/BLOCK-level scalar (one MHL per MHB), then aggregated genome-wide (147,888 blocks) into a per-sample MHL vector for deconvolution. So MHB/MHL is fundamentally a REGION-level summary statistic that is ESTIMATED from read-level data but DISCARDS read identity. ISM, by contrast, keeps output at READ-PARTITION granularity (a Read x Read matrix / read clusters within a region), never collapsing to a single regional scalar. Same raw Read x CpG matrix, opposite contraction axis.
deep.input_output: INPUT: bisulfite reads (short-read WGBS/RRBS originally; could be ONT). Each read -> binary CpG methylation vector. INTERMEDIATE: pairwise adjacent-CpG r2 -> greedy block boundaries -> set of MHBs. OUTPUT: per-block MHL scalar -> per-sample genome-wide MHL vector -> NNLS-type deconvolution into tissue/tumor fractions + tissue-of-origin call. Contrast ISM I/O: same per-read CpG vectors -> Read x Read distance matrix per region -> read clustering / HP-group separation / PERMANOVA -> subclonal-structure verdict (no tissue mixture model).
deep.strengths: (1) MHL is the right tool when the goal is a stable per-region SUMMARY robust to coverage and read identity — it captures coordinated (processive) methylation that mean-beta misses, and is genome-wide-catalogued (147,888 reusable blocks). (2) The LD-block construction is a principled, data-driven way to define co-methylated functional units (analogous to genetic haplotype blocks) rather than fixed windows. (3) Proven downstream value: cfDNA tumor-load + tissue-of-origin on real cancer patients — a deconvolution/mixture use case. (4) Bounded, interpretable [0,1] metric with a clear discriminating property (resolves equal-mean/different-coordination cases).
deep.limitations: (1) EXACT w_i NOT VERBATIM-VERIFIED: the precise analytic weight (is w_i=i exactly, or another increasing function?) and the exact substring-cap rule appear only in the paywalled Online Methods/supplement of ng.3805; secondary sources confirm structure + 'longer=heavier' heuristic but not the closed form — treat the SUM_i w_i*P(MH_i)/SUM_i w_i form as reconstructed, w_i UNVERIFIED-exact. (2) Deconvolution solver named as NNLS/QP-type by inference, not a verbatim quote from a fetched source — UNVERIFIED-exact. (3) r2>0.5 vs r2>0.9: 0.5 is the minimal block-seed (verified from JCEM restatement), 0.9 is the stringent illustrative coupling (abstract/figure level) — the genome-wide 147,888-block catalog's operative cutoff details are in the paywalled methods. (4) Could not fetch the Nature page (auth redirect), escholarship (empty), or two bioRxiv PDFs (403) — so all verbatim equation hunting bottomed out at secondary restatements. (5) PLATFORM MISMATCH for our use: designed for SHORT bisulfite reads (sparse CpG/read, no genetic phasing, germline/cfDNA) — not ONT long-read somatic; MHL has no notion of HP1/HP2 genetic haplotype or somatic-SNV anchoring.
deep.what_ism_could_learn: (1) The MHB block-finder is directly adoptable: ISM could replace fixed regions with LD-r2 greedy co-methylation blocks to define analysis windows in a data-driven way (co-methylated functional units), then run read-read distance WITHIN each block — combining MHB's column-axis block definition with ISM's row-axis read partitioning. (2) MHL is a cheap, coverage-robust per-region scalar that could serve as a FIRST-PASS screen: regions with high MHL coordination are candidates where read-read structure is worth the expensive PERMANOVA. (3) MHL's 'equal-mean / different-coordination' discriminating property is a reminder to never reduce a region to mean-beta — ISM already honors this with full read vectors, but MHL gives a one-number sanity metric. (4) The orthogonality is the key insight to state in any paper: MHB (within-read CpG-CpG LD, region summary) and ISM read-read distance (between-read dissimilarity, subclone structure) are TRANSPOSE views of the Read x CpG matrix; reporting both gives reviewers a complete co-methylation picture (coordination AND partition). CAUTION: do NOT claim MHL captures subclonal/HP structure — it provably cannot (high MHL is compatible with both one and two read clusters); that gap is exactly ISM's contribution. Also keep the platform/germline-vs-somatic flags explicit when citing Guo: it is short-read, germline-tissue + cfDNA, region-level — our setting is ONT long-read, somatic, read-level/haplotype.

deep.tool: Metheor — Lee, Lee & Yu, "Metheor: Ultrafast DNA methylation heterogeneity calculation from bisulfite read alignments", PLOS Computational Biology 2023 Mar 20;19(3):e1010946. DOI: 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1010946. PMID/PMCID: PMC10062925. Source code: https://github.com/dohlee/metheor (GPL-3.0, Rust, distributed via conda). bioRxiv preprint: 10.1101/2022.07.20.500893. NOTE on provenance: this tool is short-read BISULFITE sequencing (Bismark-aligned, XM tags), GERMLINE/cell-line heterogeneity context (CCLE, Ewing sarcoma RRBS) — NOT ONT long-read, NOT somatic-caller-aware, NOT haplotype-aware. Every claim below is verified against the primary source noted; bioRxiv HTML+PDF returned HTTP 403 so a handful of exact LaTeX equations could not be lifted verbatim and are reconstructed from PMC + the canonical WSHPackage/Scherer reference and marked accordingly.
deep.method_detail:
CORE ALGORITHM — "one-sweep" / read-centric. Metheor's central efficiency claim (VERIFIED, PMC10062925): it is a read-centric algorithm that iterates over the aligned reads exactly ONCE, accumulating per-locus heterogeneity tallies as it goes. This contrasts with the CpG-centric design of the reference R implementation (WSHPackage), which for every CpG re-fetches all reads covering that CpG via the indexed BAM. Stated complexity: Metheor needs ~n read accesses (n = number of aligned reads); CpG-centric tools need ~λ·n accesses where λ = average number of CpGs per read. Because RRBS/bisulfite preferentially targets CpG-dense regions, λ>1, so the read-centric sweep wins. Input = bisulfite read alignment carrying Bismark methylation-call strings (XM tag); a `metheor tag --input --output --genome` subcommand re-tags non-Bismark BAMs. Output = TSV / bedGraph-compatible per-locus values.

THE SEVEN METRICS (6 reimplemented + 1 novel):
(A) PDR — Proportion of Discordant Reads. A read is included only if it covers >=4 CpGs (VERIFIED, Scherer NAR 2020 def reused); a read is "discordant" if it carries BOTH methylated and unmethylated CpGs (i.e. is not all-M or all-U). PDR = (#discordant reads)/(#qualifying reads) at a locus. Known LIMITATION the paper highlights: PDR has a clear read-length bias — it scales ~linearly with read length because longer reads have more CpG pairs and more chance to be mixed. Metheor CLI: `metheor pdr` with --min-depth 10, --min-cpgs 10, --min-qual 10, --cpg-set BED (VERIFIED, GitHub README).
(B) LPMD — Local Pairwise Methylation Discordance (THE NOVEL CONTRIBUTION). See vs_ism_detailed + statistics_detail for the full algorithm. Formula (VERIFIED from GitHub docs): LPMD = n_discordant / (n_concordant + n_discordant), counted over CpG PAIRS that lie a fixed genomic distance apart, on the SAME read. Defaults --min-distance 2, --max-distance 16 (bp). Designed explicitly to remove PDR's read-length bias because it conditions on distance, not on read length.
(C) FDRP — Fraction of Discordant Read Pairs. At a target CpG, sample read PAIRS covering it; a pair is discordant if at any CpG in their overlap the two reads' methylation states differ; FDRP = fraction of discordant pairs. Params (VERIFIED Scherer + Metheor README): 50bp window around target, overlap >=35bp (--min-overlap 35), subsample to 40 reads at high coverage (--max-depth 40). Binary per-pair.
(D) qFDRP — quantitative FDRP. Same read-pair construction but replaces the binary discordant/concordant call with the NORMALIZED HAMMING DISTANCE over the overlapping CpG vector, then averages → continuous 0-1, less sensitive to single-CpG noise (VERIFIED Scherer NAR 2020).
(E) Epipolymorphism (PM) — over 4-CpG windows ("quartets"/"epialleles"). PM = 1 - Σ_i p_i^2 where p_i is the frequency of epiallele pattern i among the up-to-2^4=16 possible 4-CpG patterns (VERIFIED Scherer). Interpreted as probability two random molecules differ in pattern (Gini-style). CLI `metheor pm`.
(F) ME — Methylation Entropy. Shannon entropy over the up-to-16 4-CpG epiallele patterns: ME = -(1/N) Σ_i p_i log2(p_i), N a normalizer (VERIFIED Scherer). CLI `metheor me`.
(G) MHL — Methylation Haplotype Load. Weighted fraction of fully-methylated CpG substrings over all possible substrings (VERIFIED concept; exact weight scheme is in the original Guo et al. paper, NOT re-derived here → see limitations). CLI `metheor mhl`.

All seven share one structural property (load-bearing for the ISM comparison): they read methylation states that CO-OCCUR WITHIN A SINGLE READ/MOLECULE and compare CpG POSITIONS to each other (between-position, within-read). Even FDRP/qFDRP, despite the name "read pairs", compare two reads only to score a single genomic POSITION's local concordance — the unit of analysis is a locus's intra-molecular CpG-CpG relationship, not a molecule-vs-molecule clustering.
deep.vs_ism_detailed:
THE AXIS DISTINCTION (the user's central question) — CONFIRMED and sharpened.

Metheor distance = WITHIN-READ, BETWEEN-POSITION (CpG_i vs CpG_j on the same molecule, j-i = fixed genomic bp gap). LPMD's pair is "two CpGs at distance d on the same read"; discordance = the two CpGs have different methylation states. The genomic-distance axis is the x-axis. It answers: "at this locus, how locally disordered is the methylation comb WITHIN single molecules?"

ISM distance = BETWEEN-MOLECULE, READ-READ (read_a vs read_b across the SAME set of CpG positions). ISM's distance_matrix_[METRIC].csv (per output-structure.md) is Read × Read; the methylation.csv is Read × CpG and the distance collapses the CpG axis to compare whole molecules to each other. It answers: "do these reads fall into distinct subclonal/haplotype methylation groups?" — i.e. clustering of molecules.

So the two are ORTHOGONAL projections of the same Read×CpG matrix:
  - Metheor / LPMD collapses the READ axis (aggregates over molecules) and keeps the POSITION-pair axis → a per-locus disorder scalar.
  - ISM collapses the POSITION axis (into a molecule-molecule distance) and keeps the READ axis → a molecule-clustering structure (the HPFineNGroups / PERMANOVA / ARI machinery).

Concrete consequence for our cancer ONT work: a locus can have HIGH within-read disorder (high LPMD/epipolymorphism — methylation comb is internally ragged on every read) yet LOW between-molecule structure (all reads equally ragged → no two clean subclones → low ISM read-read separation), and vice versa (every read internally clean but two distinct clean haplotype/subclone groups → low LPMD, high ISM ARI). This maps directly onto our own findings: the project's "epipolymorphism AUC all confounded by n_reads" (O11 NEGATIVE) was exactly a within-read-disorder metric failing, whereas the live ASM/HP-axis signal is a between-molecule (HP1 vs HP1-1) phenomenon. They are not redundant — they are complementary, and the within-read axis is one ISM does NOT currently expose as a first-class per-locus feature.

CRITICAL CAVEATS before any borrowing (our context = ONT long-read somatic cancer):
1. Long-read INVERTS Metheor's design premise. Metheor exists because bisulfite reads are SHORT (CCLE RRBS = 29nt reads cited in paper), so PDR's read-length bias and the need for distance-conditioning are acute, and 4-CpG quartet windows fit a short read. ONT reads span kilobases and hundreds of CpGs — read-length bias is a different regime, quartet windows are trivially satisfied, and "local within 16bp" is a tiny fraction of what a long read sees. LPMD's distance-conditioning is still meaningful and arguably MORE useful on long reads (you can sweep distance far beyond 16bp), but the default 2-16bp is short-read-tuned.
2. Bisulfite XM tag vs ONT MM/ML. Metheor reads Bismark binary methylation strings; ONT gives probabilistic 5mC/5hmC (MM/ML), and our pipeline distinguishes 5mC vs 5hmC (the MSA Level-1 double-row artifact bit us before). Any LPMD-style port must binarize ML probabilities with an explicit threshold and decide 5mC-only vs any-mod — a modeling choice Metheor never had to make.
3. Germline/cell-line vs somatic. Metheor's heterogeneity is population/epiallele diversity in a (largely clonal or bulk) sample; it has NO somatic-vs-germline, NO tumor-normal, NO HP/haplotype awareness. Our discriminative target is TP-vs-FP somatic calls and HP-axis ASM. Metheor metrics are descriptive disorder scalars, not classifiers — consistent with our repeated finding that pure within-sample methylation-disorder features are characterization-only, not usable filters.
deep.statistics_detail:
LPMD ALGORITHM, precise (VERIFIED GitHub docs + PMC):
- Iterate each read once. On a read, enumerate all CpG pairs (i,j) whose genomic separation d = pos_j - pos_i satisfies min_distance <= d <= max_distance (defaults 2bp..16bp).
- For each such pair, both CpGs have a binary state (M/U from the Bismark XM string). The pair is CONCORDANT if states equal (MM or UU), DISCORDANT if unequal (MU or UM).
- Accumulate genome-wide (or per-locus / per region with --pairs and --cpg-set): n_concordant, n_discordant.
- LPMD = n_discordant / (n_concordant + n_discordant). Range 0..1; higher = more local methylation disorder.
- Because the pair is conditioned on genomic distance and NOT on how many CpGs a read happens to span, LPMD is read-length-INVARIANT — the explicit fix for PDR's length bias (VERIFIED: paper states LPMD "is not dependent on the length of sequencing reads").

PERFORMANCE (VERIFIED PMC10062925):
- Speedup "up to 300-fold" depending on measure and data size, benchmarked against THREE references: methclone, WSHPackage (R), and Perl scripts from prior publications. Hardware: Intel Xeon E7-4850 @2.10GHz, 512GB RAM. Data: a simulated RRBS dataset + an Ewing sarcoma RRBS dataset. Strong specific number: single-threaded Metheor beat 32-threaded WSHPackage by 13.7×–175.8× for PDR/FDRP/qFDRP on 20M simulated reads.
- Memory "up to 60-fold" smaller than the reference implementations, same benchmark scenarios.
- Correctness: produces "identical results" / values matching the original implementations (VERIFIED claim — Metheor is a faithful reimplementation of the WSHPackage/methclone metrics plus LPMD).

CONFOUND / STATS NOTES relevant to us:
- All these are per-locus scalars with NO built-in confound control. In our hands within-sample disorder metrics were confounded by n_reads/coverage (O11) — LPMD's ratio form partially normalizes coverage (it is a fraction) but the VARIANCE of the estimate still depends on pair count, so low-coverage loci give noisy LPMD. Any port needs the same auc-confound-guard discipline (within-group OLS over coverage, permutation null) before any AUC>0.58 claim.
- FDRP/qFDRP subsample to 40 reads at high coverage to avoid combinatorial explosion — a sampling choice that itself injects coverage-dependence.
deep.input_output: INPUT (VERIFIED GitHub README): BAM aligned with Bismark, carrying XM methylation-call tags. Non-Bismark BAMs supported via `metheor tag --input in.bam --output out.bam --genome genome.fa`. This is BISULFITE short-read data; nothing in the tool consumes ONT MM/ML probabilistic mod tags natively — porting to our data requires a binarization layer. OUTPUT: per-locus TSV, bedGraph-compatible for most metrics; `lpmd --pairs` emits detailed pair-wise statistics. CLI defaults verified: pdr (--min-depth 10, --min-cpgs 10, --min-qual 10); lpmd (--min-distance 2, --max-distance 16, --min-qual 10); fdrp/qfdrp (--max-depth 40, --min-overlap 35, --min-qual 10); me/pm/mhl (--min-depth 10, --min-qual 10). All accept --cpg-set BED to restrict to a predefined CpG set.
deep.granularity: Per-locus / per-region within-sample scalar (region-level when --cpg-set or genome-wide aggregate). It is NEITHER read-level (it aggregates over reads) NOR haplotype-level (no HP awareness). In our taxonomy: a region-level descriptive disorder metric. ISM, by contrast, is read-level → molecule-clustering → optionally HP-axis. The complementary value is precisely that Metheor occupies the per-locus within-read cell that ISM does not surface as a feature.

(2) Metheor GitHub README https://github.com/dohlee/metheor/blob/master/README.md — exact CLI subcommands, flags, defaults. (3) Metheor GitHub docs/wiki landing — LPMD ratio formula n_discordant/(n_concordant+n_discordant), distance range. (4) Scherer et al. NAR 2020 PMC7192612 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7192612/ — canonical FDRP/qFDRP/PDR/epipolymorphism/entropy equations that Metheor reimplements. deep.strengths: (1) The one-sweep read-centric architecture is genuinely the right speed pattern and directly portable in spirit: ISM C++ already does a single pass over reads in a region — accumulating an LPMD-style within-read pair tally during that existing sweep is near-free (no second pass, no re-fetch). (2) LPMD's distance-conditioning is a clean, coverage-fraction-normalized, read-length-invariant scalar — a good template for a per-locus within-read disorder FEATURE to sit alongside the existing read-read distance matrix. (3) Rust + conda + identical-results reimplementation is a model of reproducible tool engineering. (4) The within-read axis is demonstrably orthogonal to ISM's between-molecule axis → real complementary information, not overlap.
deep.limitations: (1) Could not fetch bioRxiv verbatim equations (403) — LPMD/ME formulas are reconstructed from PMC prose + Scherer canonical defs, marked UNVERIFIED at the LaTeX level (the ratio form and entropy/epipolymorphism forms are high-confidence; any exact normalization constant N in ME is not verbatim). (2) MHL exact weight scheme not independently verified against Guo et al. (3) The 300×/60× numbers are the paper's own benchmark on bisulfite RRBS — they do NOT transfer to ONT long-read regimes and should not be quoted as expected speedup for our data. (4) Tool is short-read bisulfite, germline/cell-line, region-level, no HP/somatic awareness — borrowing is conceptual (the within-read axis + sweep pattern), not a drop-in: our prior O11 NEGATIVE shows naive within-sample disorder metrics get confounded by coverage and are characterization-only, not TP/FP filters. (5) I verified definitions, not runtime behavior on our BAMs — no empirical run was performed (consistent with this being a literature deep-read task, not a pilot).
deep.what_ism_could_learn:
CONCRETE, RANKED BY ROI:
(1) BORROW THE WITHIN-READ AXIS AS A COMPLEMENTARY PER-LOCUS FEATURE (highest value). Add an LPMD-style scalar — fraction of discordant within-read CpG pairs at distance d, swept over several d bins (on long reads you can go well past 16bp: e.g. 2-16, 16-100, 100-500bp) — computed during ISM's existing single-pass read sweep. This gives ISM a within-read disorder feature that is mathematically orthogonal to its read-read clustering, directly addressing "what does intra-molecule raggedness add beyond between-molecule structure?". Pair it with the existing HP-axis: LPMD computed WITHIN HP1 vs WITHIN HP1-1 separates "haplotype-level clean but subclone-ragged" from "uniformly disordered" — a distinction the current pipeline cannot express.
(2) BORROW THE SWEEP/COMPLEXITY DISCIPLINE (free win). Confirm ISM accumulates per-locus heterogeneity in one read pass (n, not λ·n) rather than re-fetching reads per CpG — Metheor's headline lesson is architectural, and it costs nothing to adopt if not already done.
(3) DO NOT borrow the metrics as classifiers or the 300× number as a promise. Our own O11/epipolymorphism-NEGATIVE history says within-sample disorder is coverage-confounded and characterization-only; treat any borrowed LPMD feature as a candidate that MUST pass auc-confound-guard (within-group OLS on coverage + permutation null) before any discriminative claim. The realistic framing for the paper is: ISM = between-molecule (subclone/haplotype) axis; LPMD-style = within-molecule (local disorder) axis; report them as two complementary projections, not competitors. (4) DON'T port the 4-CpG quartet windows literally (epipolymorphism/entropy) — they are short-read-tuned and ISM already captures pattern diversity via read-read distance; the distance-conditioned PAIR metric (LPMD) is the part that adds genuinely new, long-read-amenable information.

deep.tool: Long-Read POG advanced-cancer cohort paper — O'Neill, Pleasance, ... Jones (senior); "Long-read sequencing of an advanced cancer cohort resolves rearrangements, unravels haplotypes, and reveals methylation landscapes." Cell Genomics 4(11):100674, 2024. PMID 39406235, DOI 10.1016/j.xgen.2024.100674. Long-read ONT (PromethION), CANCER (advanced/metastatic), region-level + haplotype-level allelic methylation. The "tool" is actually a multi-component PIPELINE, not one binary: Clair3/WhatsHap (SNV phasing) -> NanoMethPhase (haplotag + methylation phasing) -> DSS (region DMR calling). All three verified from primary sources below.
deep.method_detail: ALGORITHM (verified, primary sources): (1) PHASING — SNVs phased with WhatsHap "as included with clair3" (Clair3 caller); plus NanoMethPhase's own read+methylation phasing. NanoMethPhase (Akbari et al., Genome Biol 2021, GitHub vahidAK/NanoMethPhase) takes a WhatsHap phased VCF (0|1 / 1|0) + per-read 5mC calls and assigns reads/CpG methylation to HP1/HP2. (2) METHYLATION CALLING — 5-methylcytosine (5mC) ONLY, called with nanopolish 0.13.3. NO 5hmC analysis (contrast: our ISM/MSA reads MM/ML and can separate 5mC vs 5hmC — and a known MSA bug double-counted 5mC+5hmC). (3) aDMR DETECTION — NanoMethPhase 'dma' module is a WRAPPER around the DSS Bioconductor package ("Dispersion Shrinkage for Sequencing data"). DSS fits a Beta-Binomial / Gamma-Poisson model with empirical-Bayes dispersion shrinkage, runs DMLtest per-CpG then callDMR to join significant loci into regions. aDMR DEFINITION (verified): clusters of CpG sites with allele methylation difference >= 0.1 (delta >=0.1), per-locus p<0.001 (NanoMethPhase default), DMR min length 100 bp, min 15 CpG sites (defaults). STATISTICS for downstream associations (aDMR vs expression, vs CNV): Wilcoxon rank-sum test throughout. So it is REGION-LEVEL allelic DMR calling on two pseudo-bulk haplotype methylation-frequency tracks — NOT read-level clustering.
deep.vs_ism_detailed: PEER, NOT COMPETITOR — different granularity, same biology. WHAT THEY CAN DO THAT ISM CANNOT: (A) RECURRENCE / cohort power — 189 tumors/181 patients let them call 2,854 genes (8,511 transcripts) with RECURRENT promoter aDMRs (RET in 26 samples = intragenic CGI alternate promoter; CDKN2A in 9 samples). Our work is single-sample (HCC1395) or 6-sample A-pilot where cross-sample somatic recurrence was 0/38 same-locus (mutations are private) — we structurally cannot establish gene-level recurrence at this scale. (B) CNV/LOH-AWARE genome-wide aDMR RATE — they quantify 4.46M aDMRs, mean 23.61K/tumor (SD 14.64K), ~5x the matched-normal rate (4.7K, SD 876), and show 79% map to heterozygous CNV/LOH. This is exactly the confound our memory flags (ASM ALLELE-axis baseline confound; strong-ASM FP-enriched in LOH) — they characterize the LOH-dominated landscape descriptively across a cohort; we can only do it on 1-6 samples. (C) Phaseability denominator — 84% of CpG phaseable (median 86%, SD 7.1%) genome-wide, gene haplotypes resolved promoter-to-3' for median 85% of genes; this matches our methyl-phasing-assist line (~84% phaseable) but is established cohort-wide. WHAT ISM ADDS (the gap they leave): their aDMR is pseudo-bulk per-haplotype methylation-FREQUENCY comparison via DSS — it collapses individual reads into two HP1/HP2 frequency tracks. ISM is READ-LEVEL: it keeps the read x CpG matrix and can resolve (i) intra-haplotype SUBCLONAL methylation structure / epipolymorphism (DSS region-frequency cannot see within-haplotype heterogeneity), (ii) read-level distance/PERMANOVA on latent groups (our 487 latent-structure loci gated CV=0 but PERMANOVA-significant), (iii) somatic HP1-vs-HP1-1 cis-test that holds CN/ploidy/alignment constant (germline-haplotype-controlled), which their ALLELE-axis aDMR cannot disambiguate from baseline allelic methylation. They answer 'IS there allelic methylation here, and is it recurrent across a cohort' (existence + recurrence, region-level); ISM answers 'WHAT is the read-level subclonal structure within a haplotype at one locus' (mechanism, read-level). Their own conclusion is that aDMRs are overwhelmingly LOH/CNV-driven, which aligns with our filter-DEAD finding (allelic methylation is real and widespread but not a usable somatic-variant TP/FP filter).

cross.dimension: Δβ / methylation-difference effect-size methodology — is ISM's raw per-CpG mean Δβ (max-collapse any-mod, Fisher exact, no dispersion shrinkage, no smoothing) sound vs the field standard (DSS, BSmooth, M-value, modkit dmr, MeConcord)?
cross.external_findings:
The field has converged on variance-stabilized, dispersion-aware, model-based difference estimation rather than raw per-CpG mean differences. Five anchors, all primary-source verified:

1) DSS (beta-binomial GLM, Feng/Wu): reparameterizes counts by MEAN + DISPERSION; the dispersion is SHRUNK via a Bayesian hierarchical model pooling information across CpGs; DM tested by a Wald test per CpG; callDML supports a `delta` effect-size threshold (posterior P that |mean diff| > delta). The DSS vignette EXPLICITLY states "using Fisher's exact ignores the biological variations" — i.e. Fisher exact treats all reads as exchangeable Bernoulli draws and conflates technical depth with biological/molecular variance. (NOTE: the specific log-normal-prior claim is in the original Feng 2014 NAR paper which I could NOT fetch — marked UNVERIFIED here; the hierarchical-shrinkage fact IS verified from PMC8171293 + Bioconductor vignette.)

2) Du et al. 2010 (BMC Bioinformatics, M-value): M = log2(β/(1−β)); raw beta-value (= what Δβ differences are computed on) has SEVERE heteroscedasticity in the [0,0.2] and [0.8,1] ranges, while M-value is approximately homoscedastic across the whole range. Recommendation: use M-value for differential testing, report beta-value (Δβ) to investigators for interpretability. (No absolute TPR/DR numbers; comparative curves only.)

3) BSmooth/bsseq (Hansen 2012, PMID 23034175): local-likelihood SMOOTHING borrows strength across neighbouring CpGs to compensate for LOW COVERAGE before computing a signal-to-noise (t-like) DMR statistic.

4) modkit dmr (Oxford Nanopore NATIVE — the closest direct comparator, long-read, supports haplotype-partitioned bedMethyl): models methylation prob as Beta(α,β) (Jeffrey's prior), scores by log marginal LIKELIHOOD RATIO, MAP-based p-value p_MAP=f(0)/f(d) on empirical effect size d=p̂1−p̂2; a MULTINOMIAL-DIRICHLET variant handles 5hmC + 5mC + unmodified SIMULTANEOUSLY (does NOT force a max-collapse). No dispersion shrinkage / no smoothing — so on the model-complexity axis modkit is actually CLOSER to ISM than DSS/BSmooth are.

5) MeConcord (Oxford Bioinformatics 2022) — closest published analog to ISM's read-to-read engine: pairwise HAMMING distance across reads (Reads Concordance) and across CpGs (CpGs Concordance), with random-expectation NORMALIZATION + binomial test, explicitly to remove methylation-level bias; classifies Identical/Uniform/Disordered. Short-read bisulfite. It is a read×read distance method like ISM but does NOT do a between-GROUP (HP1 vs HP1-1) PERMANOVA structure test. PERMANOVA itself (Anderson; scikit-bio: pseudo-F = between/within variance on a distance matrix, permutation p) is a standard ecology test; applying it to haplotype-partitioned read methylation distance matrices is NOT an established published standard — ISM's CORE-3 is a genuine (defensible) methodological extension, not a reinvention.
cross.our_findings: ISM computes Δβ as the per-CpG MEAN methylation difference between haplotype groups (HP1 vs HP1-1 somatic-controlled; ALT vs REF allele-axis), paired by CpG, tested with Wilcoxon signed-rank + Cohen d, on raw mod probabilities binarized at >0.8 / <0.2. Per-CpG significance uses Fisher exact + BH-FDR. Probabilities are max-collapsed across any-mod (5mC+5hmC). NO beta-binomial dispersion shrinkage, NO BSmooth-style spatial smoothing, NO M-value variance stabilization. Coverage floor = min 5 common CpG for read-distance; sparse cells gated by Cramér-V Cochran rule (min expected cell >=5). The DISTINCTIVE engine is CORE-1/2/3: read-to-read distance matrix (NHD default) -> hierarchical clustering -> PERMANOVA pseudo-F (999 perms) testing whether HP/somatic read groups are STRUCTURALLY separated, plus NormalBaseline residual + copy-partition (d_HP = d_copy + d_within + drift) for cis-vs-drift attribution. Headline numbers: BRCA2 HP-axis Δβ=−0.122 (n=197, ~80% copy-component, true-cis d_within=−0.023 perm p=0.022); chr17/TBC1D16 clean cis d_within=0.142 perm p=0.001; strong-ASM 0.34% genome-wide; cross-sample 6/6 excess-over-null mean 0.168; methyl->TP/FP filter NEGATIVE four ways. 5mC-driven, 5hmC marginal (delta 0.03-0.07). Single main sample HCC1395, tier 3.
cross.alignment:
PARTIAL. ISM aligns with the field on the descriptive layer and diverges on the inferential layer — but the divergences are mostly DEFENSIBLE given ISM's distinct goal (between-molecule STRUCTURE under matched CN/ploidy) rather than population-mean DMR calling.

WHERE ALIGNED / SOUND:
- Reporting Δβ as the human-facing effect size is exactly what Du 2010 and DSS callDML(delta) endorse ("report beta-value to investigators"). ISM's Δβ-as-headline is field-standard.
- Pairing by CpG + Wilcoxon signed-rank + Cohen d is a reasonable nonparametric region-level summary; not the bottleneck.
- ISM's read-to-read distance + concordance lineage is legitimately grounded (MeConcord, epipolymorphism/entropy). ISM's PERMANOVA between-group test is a genuine extension MeConcord lacks; it directly answers "structure not disorder," which the per-CpG family (Fisher/NME/epipoly) cannot. This is ISM's strongest, most novel, and most defensible methodological move.
- ISM holding CN/ploidy/alignment constant via HP-axis + NormalBaseline residual addresses a confound that population DMR tools (DSS/modkit) do NOT control for — this is a real advantage in the cancer/LOH context, not a deficiency.
- On the "no shrinkage / no smoothing" axis, ISM is NO WORSE than modkit dmr (the ONT-native standard also omits both); only DSS/BSmooth shrink/smooth, and those target the REPLICATE-variance regime ISM doesn't claim to be in (single sample, within-locus reads).

WHERE GENUINELY WEAKER (real, not cosmetic):
- B1 (heteroscedasticity, Du 2010): Δβ near 0/1 is exactly where ISM's BRCA2 promoter (likely hyper/hypo extremes) lives; raw mean-difference there has compressed/unstable variance. ISM never variance-stabilizes (no M-value/logit). For a CLAIM about effect-size MAGNITUDE this is a known bias direction.
- B2 (Fisher exact ignores biological/molecular variation — DSS explicit): per-CpG Fisher treats reads as exchangeable Bernoulli, over-stating significance at high read depth and not accounting for between-read dispersion. ISM partly mitigates this by ALSO doing PERMANOVA (which IS dispersion/structure-aware) and the Cramér-V Cochran gate, but the per-CpG Fisher layer in isolation is the weakest component.
- B3 (max-collapse 5mC+5hmC): modkit's multinomial-Dirichlet keeps them as separate states; ISM collapses to any-mod. Since ISM's own result says signal is 5mC-driven and 5hmC marginal (0.03-0.07), the max-collapse risks diluting or (worse) inflating Δβ by mixing two biologically distinct marks — and ISM's own memory notes a prior MSA artifact where 5mC+5hmC dual-column handling halved a value. This is the most actionable fix.
- B4 (low-coverage binarization >0.8/<0.2): discards intermediate-probability reads and the uncertainty; DSS/BSmooth/modkit all keep continuous likelihood. The min-5-CpG floor helps but per-read binarization throws away calibration.
cross.verdict:
SOUND-FOR-PURPOSE WITH BOUNDED, KNOWN BIASES — not a flawed method, but its effect-size MAGNITUDE claims need a variance-stabilized cross-check.

The core architectural choice — read-to-read distance + clustering + PERMANOVA to test haplotype STRUCTURE, decomposed against a normal baseline to separate cis from copy/drift — is sound, novel relative to the published toolset (no standard tool combines these), and correctly targeted at a question (between-molecule organization under matched CN) that DSS/BSmooth/modkit do not address. On model complexity ISM is no worse than the ONT-native standard (modkit dmr also omits shrinkage/smoothing).

HOWEVER, the per-CpG Δβ + Fisher exact + max-collapse + hard binarization stack carries four field-recognized biases that converge on a single weakness: the ABSOLUTE Δβ magnitude (e.g. BRCA2 −0.122, cross-sample mean 0.168) is the least defensible number, because (i) Du 2010 heteroscedasticity makes raw mean differences at the 0/1 extremes unstable, (ii) Fisher exact over-states per-CpG significance by ignoring between-read variation (DSS explicit), (iii) any-mod max-collapse mixes 5mC and 5hmC against ISM's own finding that they behave differently, and (iv) >0.8/<0.2 binarization discards calibration. ISM's own framing already de-emphasizes magnitude (uses relative excess-over-null, perm p, copy-partition, and concludes methyl is NOT a usable filter), which is the RIGHT defensive posture and substantially neutralizes the magnitude risk. Verdict: keep the architecture; treat raw Δβ as a reported (Du-style "report-to-investigator") quantity, not an inference primitive, and add a variance-stabilized / dispersion-aware confirmatory pass on the headline loci.
cross.improve_learn:
Concrete, prioritized fixes (each maps to a verified field method):

1) [HIGH, low-effort] Add an M-value / logit cross-check on headline loci (Du 2010). Recompute BRCA2 (−0.122) and TBC1D16 (+0.142) effect sizes as Δ(M-value) and confirm sign + significance survive variance stabilization. If a Δβ at the 0/1 extreme shrinks or flips under M-value, flag it. Cheap, directly addresses B1. Keep reporting Δβ as the human-facing number (Du's explicit recommendation) but let the M-value version carry the inference.

2) [HIGH] Stop max-collapsing 5mC+5hmC for the effect-size primitive (modkit multinomial-Dirichlet precedent + ISM's own MSA dual-column artifact). Compute Δβ separately for 5mC and 5hmC (ISM already knows 5hmC is marginal at 0.03-0.07). At minimum run BRCA2 both ways and report the gap; this de-risks the exact artifact your own memory (project_zar1l_brca2_asm_verification) flagged where dual-mod handling halved a value.

3) [MED] Confirmatory dispersion-aware pass with modkit dmr on haplotype-partitioned bedMethyl for the strong-ASM loci. modkit is ONT-native, accepts phased modbam, and gives a likelihood-ratio + MAP p-value that accounts for the beta-distributed methylation prob — a second, independent estimator on the SAME data type. Agreement = strong corroboration; disagreement localizes the bias. This is the single best "does the field's standard tool reproduce our call" check.

4) [MED] Demote per-CpG Fisher exact from any standalone significance role (DSS: "Fisher's exact ignores biological variations"). Either (a) lean on PERMANOVA (already dispersion/structure-aware) as the primary inferential layer and use Fisher only descriptively, or (b) add DSS callDML(delta) as the per-CpG confirmatory test on replicate-bearing loci. Note: ISM's PERMANOVA already largely covers the gap Fisher leaves, so this is a labeling/positioning fix as much as a new computation.

5) [LOW] Keep continuous mod-probability (or at least a 3-bin including uncertain) for at least a sensitivity analysis instead of hard >0.8/<0.2 binarization, to show the magnitude is robust to the threshold (BSmooth/DSS/modkit all retain continuous likelihood).

POSITIONING for the paper: ISM's defensible contribution is the read-level STRUCTURE test (PERMANOVA on read distance) + normal-anchored cis/copy/drift decomposition under matched CN — neither DSS, BSmooth, modkit, nor MeConcord does this combination. Frame Δβ as a descriptive companion (Du-style) and let PERMANOVA + perm-p + excess-over-null + the NEGATIVE filter result carry the claims; this is already the direction ISM is heading and it is the statistically conservative one. Do NOT claim ISM's Δβ is more accurate than DSS/modkit — it is differently purposed (within-locus between-molecule structure vs population-mean DMR), and on the shrinkage/smoothing axis it is comparable to modkit, weaker than DSS.

cross.external_findings:
VERIFIED from primary sources:

[Do 2020, Genome Biology, PMC7322865] WGBS+SureSelect, 81+24 samples incl. 16 cancers. SNP-anchored, multi-sample DMR calling (ASM required in >=2 samples; >=3 CpGs, >20% methyl diff, FDR<0.05). 15,112 recurrent ASM DMRs = 0.7% of informative SNP-containing regions. Cancer ASM 5-9x higher than matched normal (5x overall p=1.7e-7; 5x myeloma / 8.5x lymphoma / 9x GBM; 7x excl. placenta). DIRECTION: hypomethylation (loss-of-methylation on one allele) DOMINATES: 72% myeloma / 76% lymphoma / 49% GBM are LOM; only 16-25% are allele-specific gain-of-methylation (poised chromatin).

[Martin-Trujillo 2017, Nat Commun, PMC5589900] Illumina 450K + SNP6 arrays, 306 cancer cell lines + 178 TCGA tumors, 661 probes at 37 imprinted DMRs. In copy-number-NORMAL samples aberrant imprinted methylation is rare (8.1% colon / 9% liver / 12.8% lung / 17.6% breast) -> i.e. ~82-92% of apparent imprinted-DMR methylation change tracks underlying CNA, NOT genuine epigenetic change. Conclusion: imprinted-DMR methylation "simply the parental origin of underlying CNAs." Array-based, IMPRINTED loci only.

[O'Neill / POG 2024, Cell Genomics, PMC11605692] ONT PromethION long-read, 189 tumors / 41 normals, haplotype-anchored (NanoMethPhase, 84% CpGs phased). 4.46M total aDMRs (mean 23.61K/sample), ~5x more in tumor than normal (23.61K vs 4.7K), ~462K tumor-specific. 79% of aDMRs map to heterozygous CNV + LOH regions; #aDMR per sample correlates with genome fraction in LOH (Pearson r=0.469, p=2.6e-11). Recurrent aDMRs at RET (26 samples), CDKN2A (9 samples); 2,854 genes with recurrent promoter aDMRs.

[Schalkwyk 2010, AJHG, PMC2820163] Affymetrix SNP6 + MSRE, 10 germline blood/buccal individuals, 7.6% of genome surveyed. 2,704/183,605 informative SNPs (1.5%) show RAS change >=0.10 -> extrapolated >35,000 cis-ASM sites genome-wide. 90.3% cis-acting; ~9.7% show direction-of-skew inconsistency between individuals (non-cis/imprinting/stochastic). GERMLINE, cross-individual, region/SNP-level, NOT cancer.

[Sakamoto 2022, Nat Commun 13:3464] ONT long-read lung cancer phasing paper — PAPER EXISTS and is ONT/cancer/haplotype-phased, but its specific patient-private hap-DMR metric could NOT be fetched from a primary source -> that quantitative claim is UNVERIFIED. cross.our_findings: ISM internal (HCC1395 SEQC2, single main sample, single ClairS-TO pipeline, tier 3): strong-ASM rare 0.34% genome-wide with NO directional bias (hypo 44% / hyper 56%). BRCA2 promoter HP-axis Delta-beta=-0.122 (n=197), ~80% copy-component + only marginal true cis d_within=-0.023 (perm p=0.022); chr17/TBC1D16 the only clean cis exemplar (d_within=0.142, perm p=0.001). ASM x CN partial rho=-0.055 (NOT copy-number-driven at the somatic-controlled HP-axis level; copy-dosage falsified). Cross-sample 6/6 excess-over-null (mean 0.168, 3 cancer types); somatic-private 0/38 (underpowered for recurrence). methyl->TP/FP variant filter NEGATIVE four ways (LOSO 100% sample-circularity, AUC=0.505, strong-ASM anti-discriminative OR=0.194). LOH-constrained phasing: NG=2 inner 93-99% same-haplotype 6/7, n=7 Wilcoxon W=28 p=0.0078. 5mC-driven; 5hmC marginal. O11 epipolymorphism AUC 0.845->0.530 after coverage correction (was artifact).
cross.alignment:
DIFFERENT CALIBER on the headline numbers (not a real conflict), with one genuine partial tension and several strong convergences.

(1) "Rare 0.34%" vs literature "5-9x increased / 4.46M aDMRs" = CALIBER MISMATCH, not conflict. Our 0.34% is a within-sample, somatic-controlled HP-axis read-rate (HP1 vs HP1-1) at strict strong-ASM threshold on ONE tumor; Do 2020's "0.7% of informative regions" + "5x increase" and POG's 4.46M are cross-individual / haplotype-anchored DMR COUNTS that explicitly INCLUDE germline cis-ASM and copy-number/LOH-driven allelic methylation. Notably our 0.34% strong-ASM is the same order of magnitude as Do 2020's 0.7% DMR fraction once you compare like-for-like (stringent threshold, fraction of informative regions) — the apparent gap is the inflation literature gets from germline+CN-driven allelic methylation that our HP-axis design deliberately holds constant.

(2) "No directional bias (hypo 44%/hyper 56%)" vs Do 2020 "hypomethylation dominates (72-76%)" = PARTIAL TENSION but reconcilable. Do 2020's hypo-dominance is measured cross-individual where the dominant driver is global cancer hypomethylation acting allele-specifically; our HP-axis is somatic-controlled (compares the two haplotypes of the SAME tumor) so it factors out the genome-wide hypomethylation tide — under that design a near-symmetric hypo/hyper split is expected, and the symmetry is itself evidence our axis is not just re-detecting bulk hypomethylation. Caveat: single sample, n in the strong-ASM set is small, so "no bias" is low-powered.

(3) BRCA2 hypo (-0.122) vs imprinted-canonical-hyper = NOT a conflict; different locus class. Our BRCA2 is a somatic tumor-suppressor promoter, not an imprinted DMR; comparing its direction to imprinted-DMR canonical hypermethylation is a category mismatch (already flagged in our memory as one of the "3 non-alignments" to defend).

(4) STRONG CONVERGENCE on copy-number confounding — but our finding is MORE refined, not contradictory. Martin-Trujillo (82-92% of imprinted methylation = CN) and POG (79% of aDMRs in CNV/LOH; r=0.469 with LOH fraction) both say the BULK allelic-methylation signal is copy-number/LOH-driven. Our BRCA2 ~80% copy-component agrees with that bulk picture EXACTLY. The apparent paradox with our genome-level "ASM x CN partial rho=-0.055, copy-dosage falsified" is resolved by level-of-analysis: at the bulk/locus level CN dominates (we agree), but our HP-axis somatic-controlled design holds CN/ploidy/alignment CONSTANT, so the residual within-haplotype signal is correctly NOT CN-driven. We are measuring the cis residual that the literature's CN-confounded methods cannot isolate. VERIFIED FROM PRIMARY SOURCES. The external "methylation-locus-association" literature splits into 3 distinct axes, and NONE occupies ISM's exact cell.

AXIS (a) WITHIN-READ CpG-CpG co-methylation / LD (intra-molecule):
- MHB/MHL (Guo/Shen, Nat Genet 2017, PMID 28263317): defines Methylation Haplotype Blocks via LINKAGE DISEQUILIBRIUM between ADJACENT CpGs computed from individual reads (147,888 blocks); MHL = conservation of consecutively-methylated CpG stretches across the population. SHORT-READ (61 WGBS + 101 RRBS + 637 arrays). Application = cancer cfDNA tumor-load + tissue-of-origin (59 lung/CRC patients), NOT germline imprinting. mHapTk (Bioinformatics 2022, btac650) is the modern toolkit re-implementation. (UNVERIFIED: mHapTk metric-by-metric details not fetched.)
- Metheor (Lee et al., PLoS Comp Biol 2023, pcbi.1010946; github.com/dohlee/metheor): Rust tool on Bismark-tagged BAM = SHORT-READ bisulfite. Reconciled metric taxonomy (verified PMC10062925): PDR = within-read per-read concordant/discordant classification; LPMD = within-read, CpG pairs "present on the same sequencing read" at fixed distance, n_disc/(n_conc+n_disc), read-length-bias-free; MHL = within-read. FDRP/qFDRP = BETWEEN-read (compare PAIRS OF READS overlapping a CpG) — disorder/diversity family. ME (entropy) / PM (epipolymorphism) = population epiallele-level. All are DISORDER/heterogeneity metrics, none does read-read distance+clustering+significance.

AXIS (b) BETWEEN-READ read-read distance + clustering (where ISM lives):
- cvlr (Raineri et al., Bioinformatics Advances 2023, vbac101): the ONLY verified close neighbor. ONT long-read. EM on a MIXTURE OF MULTIVARIATE BERNOULLI distributions over a reads x positions binary matrix (0/1/-1 unknown); user-set k (examples k=2); reports MEDIAN ABSOLUTE methylation difference between clusters + covariance; NO prior phasing required → captures allele-specific AND other heterogeneity. KEY GAPS vs ISM: no read-read pairwise DISTANCE matrix (it's model-based EM, not distance+UPGMA), NO PERMANOVA/dispersion significance test, NO normal-anchored somatic cis-test, no 5mC/5hmC split, not cancer-somatic-specific.

AXIS (c) COHORT CpG-CpG correlation networks (cross-sample):
- CoMeBack (Bioinformatics 2020, 36/9/2675): array CMRs by chaining adjacent probes (<2kb, CpG density >=1/400bp) with R2>0.3 across INDIVIDUALS. ARRAY/cross-sample, not read-level.
- Comethyl (Mordaunt et al., Brief Bioinform 2022, bbab554): WGCNA on region methylation across samples → eigennode modules vs traits. SHORT-READ WGBS / cross-sample, not read-level.

ADJACENT ONT-CANCER HAPLOTYPE TOOLS (axis-b-ish but frequency-aggregated, not read-read):
- NanoMethPhase (Genome Biol 2021, s13059-021-02283-5, PMC7898412): ONT; Clair SNV → WhatsHap phase → per-haplotype methylation FREQUENCY → DSS DMR calling. Explicitly does NOT compute distance matrices, cluster reads, or run PERMANOVA. Imprinting + general ASM.
- pycoMeth (Genome Biol 2023, s13059-023-02917-w): ONT; Bayesian changepoint SEGMENTATION + haplotype-aware diff-methylation testing on binarized calls (contingency / beta-score difference + IHW). Region/segment-level, not read-read distance/clustering.
cross.our_findings:
ISM (verified from C++ source per task brief) occupies AXIS (b) — between-molecule read-read DISTANCE + clustering — but with a configuration no verified external tool matches:
- CORE 1: explicit read-to-read pairwise DISTANCE matrix (NHD default, +L1/Bernoulli/Pearson/Jaccard; min common CpG=5; NaN→MAX_DIST; strand-aware) — distance-based, vs cvlr's model-based Bernoulli-mixture EM.
- CORE 2: hierarchical clustering (UPGMA/Ward/Single/Complete) with silhouette k=2..10 — vs cvlr's user-fixed k EM.
- CORE 3: PERMANOVA (pseudo-F, 999 perms, SS_within/SS_between) + dispersion test ON the distance matrix → a STRUCTURAL SIGNIFICANCE test of whether HP/somatic read groups are separated. This is ISM's distinguishing engine; NO verified external read-level tool runs PERMANOVA-on-distance.
- CORE 4: also computes the disorder family (per-CpG Fisher+BH-FDR, NME, epipolymorphism) for explicit contrast — i.e. ISM internalizes Metheor-style metrics as a CONTRAST baseline against its structure engine.
- CORE 5: Cramer V with Cochran reliability gate (min expected cell >=5) — reliability-gated global HP-vs-meth association absent from the comparators.
- CORE 6: NormalBaseline residual (raw - per-CpG normal mean) + normal-anchored cis-test (d_somatic=C-B, d_cis=C-A, d_drift=B-A across tumor HP1-1 / tumor HP1 / NORMAL HP1) separating true cis-driven somatic ASM from drift while holding CN/ploidy/alignment constant. No verified external tool does this normal-anchored 3-way decomposition.
- Delta-beta: HP-axis (HP1 vs HP1-1, somatic-controlled) vs ALLELE-axis (ALT vs REF), with copy-partition d_HP = d_copy + d_within(true cis) + drift.
- 5mC AND 5hmC from BAM MM/ML; ONT cancer somatic (tumor-normal paired / tumor-only).
- Positioning honesty: concludes methyl is NOT a usable TP/FP variant filter; LOH-constrained phasing is the live positive — consistent with the field (NanoMethPhase/cvlr also frame methylation as characterization/phasing, not somatic-caller filtering).
cross.alignment: COMPLEMENTARY-WITH-A-GENUINE-UNFILLED-NICHE. The three external axes are largely orthogonal to ISM's core: (a) within-read LD/disorder (MHB/MHL, Metheor) and (c) cohort networks (CoMeBack/Comethyl) answer different questions (intra-molecule co-methylation; cross-sample correlation) and are mostly short-read/array. ISM sits in axis (b) read-read distance+clustering, where the only verified true neighbor is cvlr (ONT, Bernoulli-mixture EM). ISM differs from cvlr on three verified-as-unfilled fronts simultaneously: (1) explicit read-read DISTANCE matrix + UPGMA + silhouette k-selection vs fixed-k model-based EM; (2) PERMANOVA/dispersion STRUCTURAL SIGNIFICANCE test on the distance matrix (no verified read-level tool does this); (3) normal-anchored somatic cis-test decomposition (d_somatic/d_cis/d_drift) holding CN/ploidy/alignment constant, plus 5mC/5hmC split, in the cancer-somatic/LOH context. Adjacent ONT-cancer tools (NanoMethPhase, pycoMeth) are frequency/segment-aggregated DMR callers (DSS / changepoint), not read-read distance engines. Convergent framing: the field independently concludes haplotype/allele methylation is characterization+phasing, aligning with ISM's "methyl is not a TP/FP filter" honesty.
cross.verdict: DEFENSIBLE NICHE, NARROW BUT REAL. ISM's individual ingredients are NOT novel in isolation: read-read clustering for ASM exists (cvlr); within-read co-methylation/LD exists (MHB/MHL, Metheor); haplotype DMR calling exists (NanoMethPhase, pycoMeth); the disorder family (NME/epipolymorphism/PDR) is standard (Metheor). The genuinely unfilled combination, verified against primary sources, is the COUPLING of: read-read distance matrix (multi-metric, distance-based not model-based) + PERMANOVA/dispersion structural-significance test + normal-anchored somatic cis-decomposition (d_somatic/d_cis/d_drift, CN/ploidy/alignment held constant) + 5mC/5hmC split, all in the ONT CANCER SOMATIC / LOH context. No single verified tool combines even three of these. CAVEAT to claim strength: cvlr already does read-level ONT ASM clustering without phasing, so the "read-read clustering" piece alone is NOT a contribution — the contribution is the significance engine (PERMANOVA-on-distance) + normal-anchoring + somatic framing. Recommend positioning ISM as "structure-not-disorder, normal-anchored somatic read-read engine," explicitly citing cvlr (closest method), Metheor/MHB (disorder & within-read contrast it subsumes as CORE 4), and NanoMethPhase/pycoMeth (frequency/segment-level ASM it differs from). cross.dimension: Literature cross-validation of two ISM internal conclusions: (1) methylation->TP/FP somatic variant filter is NEGATIVE and ML-circularity is a recognized pitfall; (2) methyl-assisted phasing belongs in the LOH/cancer whitespace, since published methyl-phasing tools are germline-only while LOH-phasing tools use CNA/SV/Hi-C, not methylation. Context = ONT long-read CANCER somatic methylation (region/read/haplotype-level).
cross.external_findings:
CONCLUSION 1 — methyl->FP filter NEGATIVE; ML-circularity is recognized.
(a) NO published somatic small-variant caller uses methylation as a standalone FP filter. Verified from primary sources for every major long-read/short-read caller:
  - ClairS-TO (Nat Commun 2025, s41467-025-64547-z; GitHub HKU-BAL/ClairS-TO; our own pipeline): FP filtering = 9 hard-filters + 4 PoNs (gnomAD/dbSNP/1000G/CoLoRSdb) + "verdict" module that statistically separates somatic vs germline using estimated tumor purity + copy-number profile + phasing/strand-bias/realignment features. NO methylation anywhere. [long-read + short-read, tumor-only/somatic]
  - ClairS + LongPhase-S (biorxiv 2023.08.17.553778): FP post-filter = reconstruct somatic haplotypes + infer tumor purity, flag variants inconsistent with somatic haplotype as LowQual. NO methylation. [long-read, somatic, haplotype-level]
  - DeepSomatic (Nat Biotech 2025, s41587-025-02839-x): DeepVariant-derived pileup-tensor CNN, short+long-read somatic SNV/indel. NO methylation feature mentioned. [both platforms, somatic]
  So methylation as an FP filter is genuinely unattempted in the literature — consistent with our NEGATIVE.
(b) ML-circularity / sample-level data leakage IS a formally recognized pitfall, confirming our LOSO design:
  - Soneson, Gerster & Delorenzi 2014, PLOS ONE 9(6):e100335 (PMID 24967636): "Batch Effect Confounding Leads to Strong Bias in Performance Estimates Obtained by Cross-Validation" — batch/sample-composition confounds inflate CV metrics; canonical statement of the exact circularity our LOSO exposed.
  - Bernett, Blumenthal, Grimm, Haselbeck, Joeres, Kalinina, List 2024, Nature Methods (s41592-024-02362-y, published 2024-08-09): "Guiding questions to avoid data leakage in biological ML" — naive random CV shares information between train/test giving "performance estimates far better than the intended application scenario"; recommends group-aware splitting (DataSail/GraphPart). Group/leave-one-group-out splitting is the prescribed remedy = our LOSO.
  - Kapoor & Narayanan leakage survey (cited via Nature Methods s41592-024-02362-y and meta-analysis Mol Psychiatry s41380-025-03336-y): leakage affects hundreds of papers across 17 fields; genomics feature-selection leakage inflates AUROC by avg ~0.18. UNVERIFIED exact Kapoor numbers (could not fetch the Patterns 2023 paper directly), but the existence/recognition of the pitfall is confirmed via two independent primary sources.

CONCLUSION 2 — methyl-phasing tools are germline-only; LOH-phasing done via CNA/SV/Hi-C, not methylation. The whitespace (methyl-assisted phasing IN cancer LOH) is real.
Methylation-based phasing tools (ALL germline, ALL leave cancer/LOH as out-of-scope or future work):
  - MethPhaser (Nat Commun 2024, s41467-024-49588-0; PMC11193733; PMID 38909018): operates ON pre-phased SNV blocks (WhatsHap/HapCUT2) + ONT methylation tags to bridge phaseblocks; germline diploid only; N50 +78-151%, accuracy 83.4-98.7%, switch-error +0.0012%; excludes X/Y. VERBATIM future-work quote: "we plan to leverage and improve the detection of heterogeneous signals in the methylation data to improve phasing also for cancer genomes where larger amplifications of regions will carry different methylation signals." [long-read ONT, germline, haplotype-level, EXPLICITLY defers cancer]
  - NanoMethPhase (Genome Biol 2021, 10.1186/s13059-021-02283-5; PMC7898412; PMID 33618748): phase 5mC from nanopore; germline allele-specific methylation / imprinting (ICRs), block N50 1.8 Mb (Clair+WhatsHap). Germline, no cancer/LOH. [long-read ONT, germline]
  - HapBridge (biorxiv 2025.11.07.687303): methylation-guided switch-error correction + phaseblock bridging using haplotype-specific methylation inter-site consistency; benchmarked vs MethPhaser on ONT R9/R10 + PacBio HiFi (germline, HG002-class); reduces switch errors 3.07-18.72%, N50 +5.84-68.61%. Germline phasing AID, not a variant filter; depends on heterozygous ASM (absent in LOH). [long-read+HiFi, germline] (full-text 403; abstract/search verified)
LOH/cancer-genome phasing tools (use CNA/allelic-imbalance/SV/Hi-C — NOT methylation):
  - Wakhan (medRxiv 2025.12.11.25342098; GitHub KolmogorovLab/Wakhan): haplotype-specific somatic CNA; extends phased blocks + corrects switch errors using copy-number differences between haplotypes + somatic SV; handles copy-neutral LOH and BFB. Inputs = tumor BAM + phased VCF (Clair3+Longphase recommended) + optional somatic SV. Explicitly "does NOT use methylation." [long-read ONT/PacBio, cancer, LOH-capable]
  - HiCancer (Sci Rep 2021, s41598-021-86104-6; PMC7987978; PMID 33758310): Hi-C cancer phasing; removes somatic SNPs + phases LOH regions correctly via allelic copy-number imbalance + LD; 4-step pipeline. NO methylation. [Hi-C, cancer, LOH-explicit]
  - Sakamoto/POG advanced-cancer cohort (PMC11605692, Cell Genomics 2024): phases somatic mutations (cis/trans double-hits) via SNVs+WhatsHap; methylation phased DOWNSTREAM onto SNV blocks for aDMR DISCOVERY (4.46M aDMRs; recurrent RET/CDKN2A), NOT as phasing mechanism nor FP filter; notes LOH as a phasing challenge. [long-read ONT PromethION, cancer]
cross.our_findings:
ISM internal (HCC1395 SEQC2 truth, tier 3, single ClairS-TO pipeline, ONT long-read 5mC/5hmC, cancer somatic):
C1) methyl->TP/FP variant filter NEGATIVE four ways: LOSO 100% sample-level circularity; AUC=0.505 (chance); strong-ASM anti-discriminative (enriched in FP, OR=0.194); methylation 5th-rank vestigial.
Supporting ASM characterization: strong-ASM rare (0.34% genome-wide; hypo 44%/hyper 56%, no directional bias); ASM x CN partial rho=-0.055 (NOT copy-number-driven, copy-dosage falsified); 5mC-driven, 5hmC marginal (0.03-0.07); O11 epipolymorphism AUC 0.845->0.530 after coverage correction (was artifact). BRCA2 promoter HP-axis Delta-beta=-0.122 (n=197) ~80% copy-component + marginal true cis d_within=-0.023 (perm p=0.022); chr17/TBC1D16 only clean cis exemplar (d_within=0.142, perm p=0.001). cross-sample 6/6 excess-over-null (mean 0.168, 3 cancer types); somatic-private 0/38 (underpowered for recurrence).
C2) LOH-constrained phasing POSITIVE: NG=2 inner 93-99% same-haplotype 6/7 samples, n=7 Wilcoxon W=28 p=0.0078 (Grade B+) — i.e. methylation carries haplotype-level signal usable for phasing assist, distinct from the failed read-level TP/FP filter.
cross.alignment:
STRONGLY ALIGNED on both, with one nuance.
Conclusion 1: Fully corroborated. (a) Our methyl-FP-filter NEGATIVE matches the literature gap — no caller (ClairS-TO/ClairS+LongPhase-S/DeepSomatic) uses methylation as an FP filter; they rely on PoN, tumor-purity+CN germline-somatic separation, somatic-haplotype consistency, and pileup CNNs. We are not contradicting a known-positive method; we tested an unattempted idea and it failed cleanly. (b) Our LOSO design is the textbook remedy — Soneson 2014 (batch-confound CV inflation) and Bernett et al. 2024 Nature Methods (group-aware splitting) make sample-level circularity a formally recognized pitfall; our 100%-circularity finding (in-dist +0.022 collapsing to held-out ~0) is exactly the documented failure mode. Direction and statistics agree.
Conclusion 2: Corroborated with a sharpened framing. The literature cleanly bifurcates: methylation-phasing tools (MethPhaser, NanoMethPhase, HapBridge) are all germline and depend on heterozygous haplotype-specific methylation — MethPhaser verbatim defers cancer/amplified-region methylation to future work; HapBridge needs het ASM that LOH erases. Meanwhile cancer/LOH-phasing tools (Wakhan, HiCancer, Sakamoto/POG) phase LOH via CNA/allelic-imbalance/SV/Hi-C and treat methylation only as downstream aDMR discovery — none use methylation to phase. So the specific niche "methylation-assisted phasing inside cancer LOH whitespace" is genuinely unoccupied, exactly as claimed. NUANCE: our positive signal is haplotype-level (LOH NG=2 same-hap), the same level where MethPhaser/HapBridge operate — so the whitespace is not "methylation phasing is novel" (it isn't, in germline) but "applying it where SNV-phasing dies (LOH) in cancer, which germline tools explicitly skip and CNA/SV/Hi-C tools fill non-methylation-wise."
cross.verdict:
BOTH CONCLUSIONS SUPPORTED by primary-source literature.

(1) methyl->TP/FP filter NEGATIVE: VERIFIED-CONSISTENT. No published somatic caller uses methylation as a standalone FP filter (ClairS-TO/ClairS+LongPhase-S/DeepSomatic all verified to use PoN/tumor-purity-CN/haplotype-consistency/pileup-CNN instead). ML/sample-level circularity (our LOSO finding) is a formally recognized pitfall (Soneson 2014 PLOS ONE; Bernett 2024 Nat Methods; Kapoor-Narayanan survey). Our NEGATIVE is a clean negative result on an unattempted idea, not a contradiction of a known method — defensible as a methods/characterization contribution.

(2) methyl-assisted phasing in LOH whitespace: VERIFIED-REAL whitespace. MethPhaser/NanoMethPhase/HapBridge are germline-only and explicitly defer cancer/LOH (MethPhaser future-work quote; HapBridge needs het ASM absent in LOH). Wakhan/HiCancer/Sakamoto do cancer LOH-phasing via CNA/allelic-imbalance/SV/Hi-C, with methylation only as downstream aDMR discovery — never as the phasing signal. The niche is unoccupied.

CAVEATS for our claims: (i) single main sample HCC1395 + single ClairS-TO pipeline = tier-3 ceiling; the LOH-phasing positive (n=7 Wilcoxon p=0.0078) is the more transferable result but still needs an independent caller + a non-cancer/germline null to rule out generic ASM. (ii) Kapoor exact numbers UNVERIFIED (Patterns 2023 not fetched); pitfall existence verified via two other primary sources. (iii) HapBridge full text 403 (verified via abstract+search, not PDF). (iv) MethPhaser switch-error/N50/accuracy numbers VERIFIED via PMC full text; Wakhan/HiCancer algorithm verified via GitHub/abstract (not full methods PDF for Wakhan).
cross.improve_learn:
PHASING-WHITESPACE IMPROVEMENT PLAN (how to convert the LOH-phasing positive into a defensible, novel cancer contribution):

1. POSITION as the explicit gap-filler, not a new method-class. Frame = "germline methyl-phasing (MethPhaser/HapBridge) explicitly stops at LOH/cancer; cancer LOH-phasers (Wakhan/HiCancer) use CNA/SV/Hi-C and ignore methylation. We test whether haplotype-specific methylation rescues read-to-haplotype assignment in cnLOH blocks where SNV heterozygosity is gone." This is the precise unoccupied cell and is directly citable against MethPhaser's own future-work sentence.

2. KILL THE CONFOUND THAT SANK THE FILTER. In LOH, cnLOH retains haplotype-level ASM (germline-imprinting-like), which is exactly what MethPhaser exploits in germline — so the NG=2 same-hap signal could be inherited germline ASM, not somatic. Add a germline/normal-matched anchor (HCC1395BL normal, or COLO829BL): show the methylation haplotype-split in tumor LOH is concordant with the matched-normal haplotype phasing. If it just recovers germline ASM, that is still a valid phasing AID (like MethPhaser) but must NOT be sold as somatic-specific.

3. BENCHMARK AGAINST THE RIGHT BASELINE. Compare methyl-assisted LOH read-assignment vs (a) Longphase/WhatsHap SNV-only (which fails in LOH by construction) and (b) Wakhan's CNA-based haplotype extension. The interesting claim is "methylation recovers phase where SNV-density-zero AND where CNA is copy-neutral (cnLOH) so Wakhan's CN-difference signal is also weak" — that double-blind-spot region is the true whitespace. Quantify switch-error / phasing accuracy in cnLOH blocks specifically.

4. ESCAPE TIER-3 CEILING. Add >=1 independent caller (DeepSomatic or ClairS+matched-normal) and >=1 additional sample with orthogonal truth (COLO829 with its consensus truth set) — the n=7 Wilcoxon is already the strongest cross-sample result; report it as the headline and treat HCC1395 single-sample ASM characterization as supporting.

5. STATISTICS DISCIPLINE (carry forward LOSO lesson). Any "methylation improves phasing" claim must use leave-one-sample-out or leave-one-block-out, with a HP-label-shuffle null (you already use excess-over-null) — per Bernett 2024 group-aware splitting, the split unit must be the sample/haplotype-block, never the read. This pre-empts the same circularity that killed the FP filter.

6. ADOPT HapBridge's inter-site consistency idea. HapBridge bridges blocks using methylation inter-CpG consistency; the LOH whitespace version is "bridge across an LOH gap (where SNVs vanish) using methylation block-to-block consistency." This is a concrete, novel, citable mechanism that neither germline tools (skip cancer) nor CNA tools (ignore methylation) implement. That is the publishable kernel.

top_improvements.title: Adopt per-CpG beta-binomial + lognormal dispersion shrinkage to replace Fisher exact, giving Δβ a model-based SE/CI
top_improvements.rationale: VERIFIED gap: ISM's per-CpG test is Fisher exact on a 2x2 (PerCpgAsm.cpp) with NO overdispersion model and NO cross-site stabilization; the only 'dispersion' in the codebase is the PERMANOVA centroid-homogeneity ANOVA-F (StructureTest), unrelated to count overdispersion. Long reads from the same haplotype/subclone are non-independent, so Fisher treats correlated Bernoulli draws as independent -> variance underestimated -> inflated significant-CpG counts. A beta-binomial absorbs read-level overdispersion and DSS's lognormal prior shrinks each CpG's dispersion toward a per-region prior, converting a bare Δβ point difference into an effect size WITH a CI (a Δβ from 5 reads currently looks identical to one from 200). Directly relevant: the project's own O11 epipolymorphism NEGATIVE was 'all n_reads confound' — a coverage-explicit beta-binomial separates true overdispersion from coverage artifact.
top_improvements.effort: High — re-implement beta-binomial+lognormal-shrinkage at the HP-group read level in the ISM/Python stack (DSS is R/short-read, do NOT pipe ONT through it); validate against the existing HP-shuffle null. ~1-2 week pilot.
top_improvements.source_basis: DSS (Feng/Conneely/Wu 2014 NAR; Wu 2015 pseudo-replicate). ISM-side verified: PerCpgAsm Fisher+BH only; no beta-binom/shrinkage/empirical-Bayes in src/core.

top_improvements.title: Build the read-read distance matrix on SOFT methylation probabilities instead of hard >0.8/<0.2 binarization
top_improvements.rationale: VERIFIED: DistanceMatrix.hpp:27-28 binarizes every CpG to methylated/unmethylated/ambiguous before NHD/Jaccard, discarding ML/mod_qual confidence. cvlr's Bernoulli-mixture and pycoMeth's BernoulliPosterior both keep p(methylated). Propagating soft probabilities into the matrix reduces low-coverage noise (the regime where ISM penalizes pairs to MAX_DIST=1.0) and lets PERMANOVA/clustering weight high-confidence calls. PARTIALLY PILOTED ALREADY: script 55 (modkit GMM re-test) already runs continuous mod_qual on candidate loci, so the soft-prob path extends work in flight, not greenfield.
top_improvements.effort: Medium — add a soft-distance option alongside binary; matrix plumbing exists. Pilot on a known subclonal cancer region, compare soft vs hard ARI vs HP tags.
top_improvements.source_basis: cvlr (Raineri 2023 Bioinformatics Advances, multivariate-Bernoulli EM); pycoMeth BernoulliPosterior (Snajder 2023 Genome Biol). ISM-side verified: DistanceMatrix.hpp binary thresholds; modkit continuous beta already extracted in scripts 54-55.

top_improvements.title: Add a directed HP-stratified CpG-PAIR (tuple) co-methylation log-odds score complementing per-CpG Fisher — exploiting the long-read advantage DAMEfinder lacks
top_improvements.rationale: VERIFIED gap: no tuple/cpg-pair/co-methylation/concordance code in src/core+include; ISM captures on-read structure ONLY via unsupervised NME/epipolymorphism, with no DIRECTED HP1-vs-HP1-1 concordance statistic. DAMEfinder's core insight is on-read MM/UU vs MU/UM concordance carries allele-specificity single-CpG tests miss. ISM has the ideal substrate (full read×CpG matrix; long reads span >>150bp so the short-read tuple-distance cap dissolves) and phased HP tags DAMEfinder reconstructs via SNP tricks. This is the column-axis (MHB/MHL transpose) view complementing ISM's row-axis distance — reporting both gives reviewers coordination AND partition. CAVEAT: this is a CHARACTERIZATION sharpener, NOT a filter — project memory (filter-DEAD, strong-ASM enriched in FP) says a better ASM score localizes WHERE ASM is, not discriminate TP/FP.
